_**User (2026-05-22 01:10:58Z)**_

Now that we have the start of a computer vision detector and actuator pipeline for marvin, I'd like to plan how we can improve performance. I think this will require frame by frame logging of the video stream (or at least part of screen) and detector and actuator state. Let's start by crunching some numbers of maximum required bandwidth for full 720x480 RGB888 + state data at 60Hz. Then I expect we'll need to scale it down some to acheive reasonable bandwidth. Also calculate memory requirement for various lengths of capture from a few seconds to full song (minutes). Also make some estimates of available bandwidth of various log storage mechanisms, for example UART, USB, write to sd card, ethernet, etc.

86	- **FreeRTOS analytics not yet enabled.** No runtime stats, task list dumps, or stack high-water-mark queries available. UI button? log on idle hook?) so we can size stacks empirically, attribute CPU, and catch latency regressions. Already bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. Pull `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` into the same scope: MCC's default is a silent spin, so an actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze — patching the hook to emit task name + spin (carefully, since the stack is already corrupt) belongs with the rest of the analytics work.

With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.

We bind callbacks once after the first `screenShow_Screen0`. If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.

92	- **Spec ↔ implementation drift on capture format.** Spec still uses "BGRX32" in ~10 places (§2 status table, §2.1 diagram, §3.1 hardware list, §4.1 video task, §4.2 detector input, §4.6.5 keyframe filename + size math, §4.7 sample config). The actual capture has been BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel) since the 2026-05-02 switch (`isc_capture.c:65-74`). Fixed §4.2.2 inline 2026-05-20 because M1 reads against it; the rest needs a sweep — including recalc of keyframe size (720×480 × 3 = 1.04 MB, not 1.38 MB) and on-disk recording layout. Defer to a doc-only pass before M5.
93	
94	- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
95	
96	  1. **`plib_csi.c` — `CSI_Analog_Init` refactor.** MCC emits per-lane HS-RX init inline with three bugs: Lane 1 in the 2-lane branch is missing the bit-rate write, Lane 2's lane-select code is `0x24` instead of `0x64`, and the 4-lane else-if branch skips Lane 1 entirely. Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
97	
98	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
99	
100	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
101	
102	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
103	
104	  5. **`initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` — per-pin VBUS calls.** MCC emits a single `VBUS_AH_*_Set/Clear()` call expecting one pin named `VBUS_AH`, but our config has VBUS on two pins (PC27 + PC31, one per USB port). The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Replace lines 162-163 (Set branch) and 169-170 (Clear branch) with explicit calls to both per-pin macros — `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set(); VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();` and the matching Clear pair. The MCC comment in the function ("name it to 'VBUS_AH'") acknowledges the single-pin assumption.
105	
106	  6. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
107	
108	  7. **`usb_host_cdc.c` — accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0` in CDC ACM Communications-interface match.** Two checks (single-interface path ~line 677, IAD path ~line 798) currently require `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.

112	  - ~~`plib_lvdsc.c` `LVDSC_CFGR.DEN_POL`~~ — Latest Harmony gfx library intentionally omits the DEN_POL field. File reverted to MCC default; not load-bearing.

Easy/Medium/Hard place notes higher up the highway with longer travel time, so the same 220 ms may strike too early. Open: per-difficulty preset, runtime-tunable from the manual-control surface, or auto-tuned from observed note-velocity. Defer until the game-state controller (spec §4.8) lands and difficulty is known to marvin — until then, expert-tuned 220 ms is the working default.

130	### 2026-05-21 — cv_marvin_v1 threshold tuning + timing-pipeline tweaks
131	
132	First end-to-end gameplay test on hardware. Detector was firing roughly random presses at first; resolved by reading actual signal values rather than guessing.
133	
134	**Visibility added:**
135	- State-reactive overlay in `cv_marvin_v1.c` — position rings always; filled center dot when `s_pressed[i]` (white in the hold ring) or `s_edge_active[i]` (fret-color in the edge ring). Lets the user watch chatter live: stable note → steady dot for hold duration; strum window → flash on the edge dot.
136	- Periodic ~2 Hz log dump (`frame_count % 30 == 0`) showing per-fret `hold_dist / edge_dist / P E` flags.
137	
138	**Diagnosis (Easy mode, no real B/O presses):**
139	- Idle hold floor sits at 22–48 across all five frets, **not** the limited-range 16 floor `display_path.md` would suggest. Playfield-glow at the sample sites is well above the limited-range black point.
140	- Real-press hold spikes to 67–186, leaving a clean gap above the noise ceiling.
141	- Hold threshold 50 with release-frac 0.6 (release=30) was *below* the idle floor for Y and B → those frets latched permanently pressed and never released.
142	- Edge threshold 50 was at the peak of real-edge signal (40–53), almost never tripping. timing_pipeline only uses `pressed` today, so dead edges aren't the chatter source — but lowering edge threshold lets `s_edge_active` overlay flicker meaningfully again.
143	
144	**Settings landed (in `cv_marvin_v1.c`):**
145	- `CV_HOLD_THRESH`: 50 → **100** (after iterating 65 → 80 → 100; 100 cleanly above noise across all frets, real presses still spike to 150–186).
146	- `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`: 0.60 → **0.78** (release ≈ 78 — above the noise ceiling, comfortably below real-press floor).
147	- `CV_EDGE_THRESH`: 50 → **25** (gives the overlay an honest edge indicator without affecting pipeline behavior).
148	- Sample coords nudged 1 px on G/R/Y/B/O edges + B hold for slightly cleaner alignment.
149	
150	**Performance:** Expert-mode play is now quite good — clean note recognition, fret hold-through across consecutive same-fret notes confirmed by trace through `process_releases` (release suppressed when the next chord-commit's `note_q` entry already needs the bit, within `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS − TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS = 190 ms` of detector-release-to-detector-press).

152	**Timing-pipeline tweaks** (Greg's hand-edits): `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` 50→25, `TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS` 20→30, `TP_FIFO_CAP` 16→32.

156	### 2026-05-21 — Manual fretboard-control producer + timing-pipeline gate
157	
158	Stood up the actuator-side half of a basic on-device manual-control surface — primarily for game-menu navigation (start a song, advance menus, hit pause) where single-finger input is the natural shape. UI half waits on a Microchip Graphics Composer regen.
159	
160	What landed:
161	
162	- `actuator/manual_control.{h,c}` — second producer of `FretboardLink_Send`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Internal state: `s_fret_mask` (bits 0..4) and `s_strum_mask` (bits 5..6). Public API: `Initialize / SetEnabled / IsEnabled / SetFret / SetStrum`. Both fret and strum are momentary — held while the UI button is down, cleared on release. `recompute_and_send` only calls `FretboardLink_Send` while enabled.
163	- `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool)` — output gate on `publish_mask`. Pipeline still advances internal state when gated, so the next `advance()` (≤ `TP_TICK_MS` = 5 ms) after re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame.
164	- `ManualControl_SetEnabled` ordering: enter manual mode = gate timing pipeline first, zero local state, send `0`, set enabled flag (so a stale pipeline frame can't race a manual zero on the wire); exit = clear enabled flag, zero state, send `0`, ungate pipeline.
165	- App init wires `ManualControl_Initialize()` after `TimingPipeline_Initialize()`. No Legato dependency at this stage.
166	- `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` adds `manual_control.c` and `ui/manual_input.c`.
167	
168	UI half landed same session after Greg ran the Composer regen. Composer added 8 buttons to `Screen0` — `Screen0_Button_Manual_{Green,Red,Yellow,Blue,Orange,StrumDown,StrumUp,Enable}` — plus 15 extern `event_Screen0_Button_Manual_*` handler declarations the application must define. The binding shape came out simpler than the plan called for: `screenShow_Screen0` itself calls `setPressedEventCallback` / `setReleasedEventCallback` with those extern symbols, so the linker resolves them and **no `ManualInput_Bind()` walk is needed**. `ui/manual_input.c` is just the 15 function bodies forwarding to `ManualControl_SetFret / Strum / SetEnabled`. The originally planned `APP_Tasks` poll-loop for null widget pointers is moot — `APP_Tasks` keeps the existing `vTaskDelete(NULL)`.
169	
170	Strum buttons are momentary, not one-shot: holding the strum button keeps the fretboard's strum line asserted, which Guitar Hero / Rock Band menus interpret as auto-repeat scrolling — the primary use case for this surface. Gameplay-path strums still pulse correctly because they go through `timing_pipeline`, which has its own `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` one-shot. The Enable button is `setToggleable(LE_TRUE)` with only `OnReleased`; both the widget and `ManualControl` default to off, so a simple `SetEnabled(!IsEnabled())` flip stays in sync without querying the widget's toggle state.
171	
172	Plan agent flagged two real blockers worth recording: (1) Legato's input pipeline routes each touch to one focus widget — multi-finger momentary chords aren't possible without a custom dispatcher, so the model is single-finger only; (2) the lazy widget-pointer init means any code that walks the `Screen0_*` pointers has to run post-`screenShow_Screen0` — moot here because Composer does the wiring itself, but still true for any future shim that needs to read or modify widget state.
173	
174	Decision-log entries above cover the producer-as-peer pattern, the Composer-driven UI choice, and the single-finger input model.
175	
176	**Bring-up over the wire.** Marvin enumerates the EDBG CDC and `FretboardLink_Send` round-trips cleanly through the queue, but the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 wasn't receiving anything. Two real fixes:
177	
178	1. **EDBG bridge needs DTR raised.** The bridge holds its UART TX idle until the host asserts DTR. Added `USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet` with `dtr=1, carrier=1` to `open_cdc()` after the existing `LineCodingSet(115200)`. Baud matters here — fretboard runs a real UART at 115200, not USB-CDC-ignored.
179	2. **Control-pipe completion handlers run from ISR context.** First instrumented attempt logged `LOG_INFO` directly from the new `SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE` / `SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE` event cases; system froze mid-print. Microchip's CDC stack dispatches *all* class events from ISR (the existing `WRITE_COMPLETE` case already uses `*FromISR` primitives — that was the precedent). `log_vprintf` takes a mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`, illegal from ISR. Stripped both the diagnostic logging and the latch infrastructure once the link was confirmed functional. Captured for the journal because it's a recurring shape: any new event-handler case in this stack must stay strictly ISR-safe.

181	### 2026-05-20 — USB CDC host attach: EDBG composite enumerates, CDC class driver now binds
182	
183	Picked up where the prior session left off — VBUS not asserting, no device detected. Closed both halves.
184	
185	**VBUS.** MCC's `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` callback is wired in the host driver but the host stack never invokes it on this build. Asserted the two VBUS GPIOs (`VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set` / `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set`) directly from `APP_Initialize` ahead of consumer init and `USB_HOST_BusEnable`. EDBG immediately enumerates.
186	
187	**Class-driver binding.** Enumeration succeeded but the CDC attach handler never fired. Added per-interface descriptor logging inside `F_USB_HOST_UpdateDeviceTask` to see what was actually being matched. Output revealed VID `0x03EB` PID `0x2175` — an EDBG composite with five interfaces: HID/CMSIS-DAP, CDC ACM IAD pair (comm + data), vendor, MSC. The IAD passed TPL match and got assigned to the CDC driver, but the CDC instance still flipped to `STATE_ERROR` without our app-level handler ever seeing the attach.
188	
189	Root cause was inside Microchip's CDC class driver: `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` (both single-interface and IAD paths) requires the comm interface to declare `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG declares `0x00` (none) — functionally identical CDC ACM in practice; Linux/macOS accept either. The TPL/IAD pre-check passes (TPL wildcards subclass/protocol), the CDC driver gets the interface group, then immediately rejects it on the AT-V.250 check. The interrupt pipe never opens, the instance errors out, and the app-level listener stays silent.
190	
191	Fix: relaxed both checks to `(AT_V250 || NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. After the patch the FBL log shows `CDC device attached, handle opened` and `c=Y` heartbeat as expected. Logged as patch #7 in the MCC re-apply list.
192	
193	Also tested a hypothesis from the prior session that `USB_HOST_Initialize` had to run *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits. With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. Backed out the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Decision-log entry above.
194	
195	Diagnostic instrumentation stripped at the end of the session: the per-interface descriptor dump and enumeration state-change logger in `usb_host.c`, and the periodic OHCI/EHCI register heartbeat in `fretboard_link.c`. What remains on disk: the two `usb_host_cdc.c` protocol-relaxation lines (patch #7), the app-level VBUS asserts, and a minimal `USB_HOST_EVENT` printf so future host-stack drama still surfaces in the log.

200	
201	First on-target test after the M2 actuator path landed. Symptoms: video stream not starting, USB ports unpowered, FBL heartbeat firing with `connected=N`. Boot stopped after `TC358743: probe starting`.

203	Root cause: the USB MCC regen reordered SYS_Initialize so `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize` ran *after* `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize`. 1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGRX32, zero-copy). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over UART, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next

41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed (commits `5a63704`, `6b85d5e`, `e28c497`). |
43	| Lightweight log shim | ✅ landed (commit `a79042f`). |

45	| Fretboard UART link | 🚧 not started. §4.3. |

48	| Reference-data recording & export | 🚧 not started. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 partial (logging done). §4.7. |

123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGRX32. |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 500 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGRX32 frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.

199	
200	## 4. Subsystems
201	
202	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
203	
204	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
205	
206	**What this subsystem owns:**
207	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
208	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
209	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
210	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
211	
212	**What it doesn't own:**
213	- CV processing (§4.2).
214	- Recording / export (§4.6).
215	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
216	
217	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
218	
219	#### 4.2.1 Role
220	
221	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
222	
223	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
224	
225	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
226	
227	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
228	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 500 Hz rate.
229	
230	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
231	
232	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
233	
234	```
235	typedef struct {
236	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
237	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
238	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
239	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
240	    struct {
241	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
242	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
243	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
244	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
245	} detector_state_t;
246	```
247	
248	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
249	
250	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
251	
252	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
253	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
254	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
255	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
256	
257	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
258	
259	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
260	
261	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
262	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
263	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
264	
265	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
266	
267	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
268	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
269	
270	### 4.3 Fretboard link 🚧
271	
272	UART between marvin and the fretboard MCU, bidirectional, framed.
273	
274	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). Same intent as fret-tuner's existing 1-byte bitmask; precise framing TBD in §5.
275	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 500 Hz, plus enable/SW0 state. Reuses the fret-tuner 12-byte ADC frame format if practical.
276	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
277	
278	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
279	
280	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
281	
282	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
283	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
284	- Per-fret release scheduling.
285	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
286	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
287	
288	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
289	
290	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
291	
292	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
293	
294	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
295	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
296	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
297	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
298	
299	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
300	
301	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
302	
303	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
304	
305	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
306	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
307	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
308	
309	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
310	
311	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
312	
313	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
314	
315	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
316	
317	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
318	
319	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
320	
321	```
322	recordings/
323	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
324	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
325	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
326	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
327	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
328	    └── keyframes/
329	        ├── 000000.bgrx        // raw BGRX32 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
330	        ├── 000060.bgrx
331	        └── ...
332	```
333	
334	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
335	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
336	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 500 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~6 KB/s. Modest.
337	- **Keyframes** — raw BGRX32 dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 BGRX = 1.38 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.38 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~415 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
338	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
339	
340	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
341	
342	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
343	
344	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
345	
346	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
347	
348	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
349	
350	Minimum fields:
351	
352	```json
353	{
354	  "schema_version": 1,
355	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
356	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
357	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGRX32" },
358	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
359	  "detectors": [
360	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
361	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
362	  ],
363	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
364	  "ended_utc": null
365	}
366	```
367	
368	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
369	
370	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
371	
372	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.38 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
373	
374	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
375	
376	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
377	
378	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
379	
380	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
381	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
382	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
383	
384	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
385	
386	### 4.7 System services 🚧
387	
388	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
389	
390	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
391	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
392	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
393	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
394	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
395	
396	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
397	
398	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
399	
400	#### 4.8.1 Role
401	
402	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
403	
404	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
405	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
406	
407	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
408	
409	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
410	
411	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
412	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
413	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
414	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
415	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
416	
417	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
418	
419	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
420	
421	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
422	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
423	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
424	
425	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
426	
427	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
428	
429	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
430	
431	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
432	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
433	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
434	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
435	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
436	
437	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
438	
439	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
440	
441	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
442	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
443	
444	---
445	
446	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
447	
448	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
449	
450	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
451	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
452	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
453	
454	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
455	
456	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
457	
458	| Toggle | Effect |
459	|---|---|
460	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
461	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
462	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
463	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
464	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
465	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
466	
467	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
468	
469	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
470	
471	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
472	
473	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
474	
475	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
476	
477	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
478	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
479	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
480	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
481	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
482	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
483	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
484	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
485	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
486	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
487	
488	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.

Read both spec and journal. The capture is actually BGR888-packed (3 B/pixel) on disk — same byte count as RGB888 — so all the bandwidth math holds. Numbers below.

## 1. Full-fat baseline: 720×480 RGB888 @ 60 Hz

Per frame: `720 × 480 × 3 = 1,036,800 B ≈ 1.04 MB` (1012.5 KiB)

| Component | Per-frame | Per-second |
|---|---|---|
| Video pixels | 1.04 MB | **62.2 MB/s ≈ 498 Mb/s** |
| Detector state (spec §4.2.3, 28 B × 2 detectors) | 56 B | 3.4 KB/s |
| Actuator state + timing-pipeline FIFO snapshot (~64 B) | 64 B | 3.8 KB/s |
| Per-frame metadata header (frame_epoch, ts_us, flags ~32 B) | 32 B | 1.9 KB/s |
| **Total** | **~1.04 MB** | **~62.2 MB/s** |

State payload is a rounding error against pixels — this is a video-bandwidth problem.

## 2. Scaled-down variants

| Variant | Per frame | Rate | Bandwidth |
|---|---|---|---|
| 720×480 RGB888 @ 60 Hz (full) | 1.04 MB | 60 | **62.2 MB/s** |
| 720×480 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 1.04 MB | 30 | 31.1 MB/s |
| 720×480 RGB565 @ 60 Hz | 691 KB | 60 | 41.5 MB/s |
| 720×480 grayscale @ 60 Hz | 346 KB | 60 | 20.7 MB/s |
| 360×240 RGB888 @ 60 Hz (½) | 259 KB | 60 | 15.6 MB/s |
| 360×240 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 259 KB | 30 | 7.78 MB/s |
| 180×120 RGB888 @ 30 Hz (¼) | 64.8 KB | 30 | 1.94 MB/s |
| Strike-line strip 720×80 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 173 KB | 60 | 10.4 MB/s |
| 5 ROI patches 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 15.4 KB | 60 | 922 KB/s |
| State only (no pixels) @ 60 Hz | ~152 B | 60 | **9.1 KB/s** |

The strike-line strip and ROI patches are interesting — they preserve everything cv_marvin_v1 actually looks at while dropping 90%+ of pixels.

## 3. Memory / capacity over time

| Variant | 1 s | 10 s | 1 min | 5 min (song) | 10 min |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Full (62.2 MB/s) | 62 MB | 622 MB | 3.73 GB | **18.7 GB** | 37.3 GB |
| Half-res 60 Hz (15.6 MB/s) | 16 MB | 156 MB | 933 MB | 4.67 GB | 9.3 GB |
| Half-res 30 Hz (7.8 MB/s) | 7.8 MB | 78 MB | 467 MB | 2.33 GB | 4.67 GB |
| Strip 60 Hz (10.4 MB/s) | 10 MB | 104 MB | 622 MB | 3.11 GB | 6.22 GB |
| ROI patches 60 Hz (922 KB/s) | 922 KB | 9.2 MB | 55 MB | 277 MB | 553 MB |
| State only (9.1 KB/s) | 9 KB | 91 KB | 547 KB | **2.7 MB** | 5.5 MB |
| Sparse keyframes per spec §4.6 (1.04 MB/s) | 1.04 MB | 10.4 MB | 62 MB | 311 MB | 622 MB |

DDR is 256 MB total, ~16 MB nocache region (already mostly the framebuffer pool). On-chip buffering caps at maybe 1-2 seconds of full video before we have to be writing somewhere.

## 4. Storage / transport bandwidth (SAM9X75 specifics)

| Channel | Theoretical | Realistic sustained | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| UART 115.2 kBd (FLEXCOM4 console) | 14.4 KB/s | **~11 KB/s** | 8N1 → 10 bits/byte. State-only fits; pixels don't. |
| UART 921.6 kBd | 115 KB/s | ~92 KB/s | Most USB-serial bridges cap here. |
| UART 3 Mbd (FLEXCOM max) | 375 KB/s | ~300 KB/s | EDBG bridge probably won't pass this. |
| USB CDC ACM (HS device) | 60 MB/s | **~5–15 MB/s** | CDC-class + host stack overhead. Marvin's USB device peripheral is currently unused (spec §3.2). |
| USB Bulk (HS device, raw) | 60 MB/s | ~30–40 MB/s | Vendor class; needs a custom host-side reader. |
| SDMMC Class-10 / FAT32 | 100+ MB/s bus | **~5–10 MB/s** | Spec already commits to this for keyframes. |
| SDMMC UHS-I | 100 MB/s | ~25–50 MB/s | SAM9X75 SDMMC can clock there but FAT/file-system overhead bites. |
| GMAC Ethernet (UDP) | 125 MB/s | **~30–60 MB/s** | Cortex-A5 + LwIP realistic. GMAC currently unused. |
| GMAC Ethernet (TCP) | 125 MB/s | ~10–20 MB/s | Stack and ack overhead heavier. |

## 5. What fits where

| Target stream | Bandwidth | UART 115k | UART 3M | USB CDC | SD | Ethernet UDP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| State only (9 KB/s) | 9 KB/s | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| ROI patches 60 Hz (0.9 MB/s) | 922 KB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 1 keyframe/s + state (1 MB/s) | 1.04 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 180×120 30 Hz (1.9 MB/s) | 1.94 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| 360×240 30 Hz (7.8 MB/s) | 7.78 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ⚠ tight | ⚠ tight | ✅ |
| Strike-strip 60 Hz (10 MB/s) | 10.4 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ⚠ | ⚠ | ✅ |
| 360×240 60 Hz (16 MB/s) | 15.6 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✅ |
| Full 60 Hz (62 MB/s) | 62.2 MB/s | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ (TCP); ⚠ UDP |

## Headlines

- **Full-rate raw is ~62 MB/s.** Only Ethernet UDP can take it, and only barely. Not realistic.
- **The "obvious good spot" is ~1 MB/s** — half a song fits on any SD card, fits over USB CDC easily, and matches the spec's committed sparse-keyframe budget (1 keyframe/s + dense state). Already designed for.
- **State-only fits anywhere**, including the 115 kBd console UART. If perf-debugging just needs detector/timing/actuator state, no new transport is required.
- **For per-frame ROI dumps** (5 patches × 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz ≈ 0.9 MB/s) you keep everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples and can stream it over USB CDC indefinitely or write minutes-long sessions to SD with room to spare.
- **The "minutes of full video" wish doesn't fit** even on a 64 GB SD: 5 minutes of full RGB888 @ 60 = 18.7 GB *and* the SAM9X75 can't sustain 62 MB/s to it anyway.

Captured. Now to keep planning — the bandwidth math says the architecture forks on **what perf question we're trying to answer**, because the answer dictates the stream and the stream dictates everything downstream (transport, on-device buffering, host-side viewer).

Before I start sketching designs, I want to make sure I'm aiming at the right target. Some candidates I can see:

1. **Latency attribution** — "where do the milliseconds go between frame-arrival and strum-emit?" Wants per-stage timestamps (ISC IRQ, CV done, timing-pipeline tick, FretboardLink_Send). State-only, ~9 KB/s, fits anywhere.

2. **Frame-rate / scheduling stability** — "are we actually hitting 60 Hz, are we dropping frames, what's task jitter?" Wants per-frame epoch + arrival-time + FreeRTOS runtime stats. State-only + a periodic task-stats dump. The carried-forward "FreeRTOS analytics not yet enabled" item directly feeds this.

3. **Detector behavior over time** — "did the threshold actually hold through that song? where did chatter spike?" Wants per-fret hold/edge distances and pressed/edge flags every frame. Already partially built (the 2 Hz log dump). State-rich, still tiny (~30 KB/s with all internal distances).

4. **"Did the detector see what I think it saw"** — replay grade. Wants pixels at the fret ROIs synchronized with detector output. ROI patches at ~1 MB/s, USB CDC or SD.

5. **Actuator-side ground truth** — fretboard-emitted commands echoed back, compared against marvin's intent. Wants the fretboard→marvin telemetry path that doesn't fully exist yet.

These mostly stack rather than compete (1+2+3 are basically the same stream), so the real fork is whether pixels need to be in the log at all.

Good — that gives the design a clear shape. Quick math on the maximalist scope, then the open architectural decisions:

## Stream sizing (all four answered, with patches)

Per-frame perf record:
- 7–9 stage timestamps as u32 μs offsets (~32 B)
- Per-fret detector internals (hold_dist, edge_dist, color distances, press_count, flags) — 5×~10B = 50 B
- Timing-pipeline state (chord-window fill, FIFO depth, strum dir, last mask) — ~16 B
- Actuator state (intent mask, send count delta, optional fretboard echo) — ~8 B
- 5 frets × 2 patches (hold + edge) × 5×5 × 3 B = 750 B
- Header (frame_epoch, host clock, flags) — 16 B

**Total: ~870 B/frame × 60 Hz ≈ 52 KB/s with patches; ~7 KB/s state-only.**

Both sit comfortably under every transport, including USB CDC and SD by ~100×, and even raw 921.6 kBd UART for the state-only tier. The bandwidth scoping was the wrong worry — the real constraints are now structural.

## Architectural shape (proposed)

A single producer pattern, fan-out to whichever sinks are enabled, with the existing `§6` toggle model:

```
modules ──► perf_log ring (per-frame, indexed by frame_epoch % N)
                │
                ▼
        perf_log_writer task
            │       │
            ▼       ▼
         SD file  USB CDC device
        (when     (when
         _sd)      _cdc)
```

Two tiers sharing one record schema (patches are an optional trailer per record):
- **Tier 1 — state-only (~7 KB/s)** — always-on during any recording session. Strict superset of today's 2 Hz log dump; replaces it.
- **Tier 2 — replay-grade (~52 KB/s)** — adds ROI patches; toggled when actually hunting a bug. Off by default.

## Key decisions I want your steer on before I sketch the plan deeper

1. **Coupling timing-pipeline and actuator stamps to the detector frame.** `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS=220` means the wire-out happens ~13 frames after detection. Two options:
   - (a) **Per-frame record stays open for ~14 frames**; ring size ≥ 32 slots; producer writes into "its" frame's slot whenever its work for that frame finishes.
   - (b) **Decoupled records per stage** (frame-ingest record + actuator-emit record, both keyed by `frame_epoch`); host-side joins them. Matches the 500 Hz `adc_fretboard` reality where detector emits don't 1:1 with frames.

   I'd lean (b) — simpler producer, no multi-writer-into-one-slot races, scales naturally to the multi-detector world the spec already commits to.

2. **Where the latency stamps come from.** Most stages already have a natural call site (ISC IRQ, `Video_FrameInfo` publish, cv task wake/done, `xDetectorStateQueue` send, timing_pipeline tick, `FretboardLink_Send`). The fretboard *wire-out* completion is the messy one — control-pipe completions run from ISR and the existing CDC stack is touchy about logging from there (see 2026-05-21 freeze). Two real options: a write-completion stamp captured in the existing ISR handler (no logging from ISR — just `xTaskGetTickCountFromISR` into a static), or skip wire-out entirely and stamp at submit-time.

3. **FreeRTOS analytics piggy-back.** The carried-forward "FreeRTOS analytics not yet enabled" item is exactly the scheduling-stability data we need — runtime stats + stack HWM. Cheapest path: enable `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS`, sample `vTaskGetRunTimeStats` at 1 Hz into the perf stream as a periodic record. Want me to bundle that into this design or keep it as a parallel item?

4. **Format.** Packed binary, fixed-size header + variable trailer for patches, little-endian — matches the spec's `state.bin` layout and means one host-side decoder serves both. Alternative is CBOR for self-describing records (handy for evolving the schema), but CBOR encoding cost on the Cortex-A5 isn't free at 60 Hz. I'd default to packed binary and version it explicitly in the manifest.

5. **Live-tail wire format.** Same packed binary, framed (length-prefix + CRC) so a host-side reader can resync on a mid-session connect. USB CDC device peripheral is currently unused (spec §3.2) so this is new MCC config + a host-side reader tool — non-trivial, but the only way to get true live tail.

If (b), packed binary, write-completion stamp from the existing ISR, and bundling FreeRTOS analytics in all sound right, I'll write the M-something plan into the journal next. Otherwise tell me where to push.

20	 * capture (HEO shows whatever is in the framebuffer — possibly stale).
21	 *
22	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, display hidden, window
23	 * unset. Layout is app policy — DisplayShow is a no-op until the
24	 * caller has set a window with Video_SetWindow. */
25	
26	void Video_Initialize(void);
27	
28	/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
29	 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
30	 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
31	void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
32	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);
33	
34	/* Display layer control. SHOW: HEO visible, BASE DISCEN cleared under
35	 * the HEO rect (saves DDR read bandwidth). HIDE: HEO disabled, BASE
36	 * owns full panel. Independent of capture state. */
37	void Video_DisplayShow(void);
38	void Video_DisplayHide(void);
39	
40	/* Destination rect on the 1280×800 panel. dst_w/dst_h matching the
41	 * source frame size → 1:1, scaler bypassed. Otherwise HEO bilinear
42	 * scaler engages and stretches to fill the rect. The rect must fit
43	 * within the panel. Takes effect on the next display bind (next
44	 * DisplayShow call, or when capture/lock state changes). */
45	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h);
46	
47	/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
48	typedef struct
49	{
50	    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
51	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
52	    uint16_t width;
53	    uint16_t height;
54	    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
55	} Video_FrameInfo;
56	
57	/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
58	 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
59	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
60	 * queue. Create the queue with:
61	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
62	 *
63	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
64	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
65	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
66	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
67	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
68	 * independently.
69	 *
70	 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
71	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
72	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
73	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
74	 * second-next frame.
75	 *
76	 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
77	 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
78	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
79	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
80	
81	/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
82	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
83	
84	/* Synchronous read of the current frame state. Doesn't block. May
85	 * report frame_count = 0 / buffer = NULL if capture has never armed. */
86	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info);
87	
88	#endif
89

62	/* HEO scaler factor is 12.20 fixed-point, factor = (src / dst) << 20.
63	 * 1.0 (= 0x100000) means 1:1, no scaling. Mirrors plib_xlcdc.c's
64	 * static CALC_SCALING_FACT. */
65	static uint32_t scaler_factor(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst)
66	{
67	    if (dst == 0u) { return 0x100000u; }
68	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)src << 20) / dst);
69	}

73	/* Point HEO at the capture buffer at (x, y) sized dst_w × dst_h. If the
74	 * destination size matches the source size, the HEO scaler stays at its
75	 * 1.0 factor (effectively bypassed). Otherwise the bilinear scaler is
76	 * engaged. BASE DISCEN is set to the destination rect so BASE skips DMA
77	 * for the area HEO covers (§44.6.4.7). */
78	static void lcd_bind(uint32_t src_w, uint32_t src_h,
79	                     uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
80	{
81	    if (x + dst_w > LCD_PANEL_W || y + dst_h > LCD_PANEL_H)
82	    {
83	        LOG_WARN("VIDEO: window %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) exceeds panel %ux%u; skipping bind\r\n",

86	                 LCD_PANEL_W, LCD_PANEL_H);
87	        return;
88	    }
89	
90	    /* Initial HEO address: the latest completed buffer if we have one,
91	     * else fall back to the framebuffer base. The on_frame_done IRQ
92	     * re-points HEO at every subsequent completed buffer, so this is
93	     * the seed that holds for at most one frame-time before the first
94	     * IRQ overwrites it. */
95	    uint32_t initial_addr = s_latest_buffer;
96	    if (initial_addr == 0u) { initial_addr = ISC_Capture_GetBufferAddress(); }
97	
98	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
99	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO,
100	                               XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
101	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, initial_addr, false);
102	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, 0u, false);
103	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
104	
105	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3) and source-memory rect (HEOCFG4) are the same
106	     * for 1:1 and differ for scaling. Write them directly — XLCDC_Set-
107	     * LayerWindowXYSize writes both registers to the same value, which is
108	     * only correct for 1:1. */
109	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u)
110	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
111	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(src_w - 1u)
112	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(src_h - 1u);
113	
114	    bool scaling = (dst_w != src_w) || (dst_h != src_h);
115	    if (scaling)

117	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(src_w, dst_w);
118	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(src_h, dst_h);
119	
120	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1)
121	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)
122	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(1)
123	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(1);
124	        /* Bicubic luminance + bicubic chrominance, both planes. Mirrors
125	         * MCC's surface-set path — best image quality for video. */
126	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG30 = LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYCFG(1)
127	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYBICU(1)
128	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCCFG(1)
129	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCBICU(1);
130	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG31 = LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYCFG(1)
131	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYBICU(1)
132	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCCFG(1)
133	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCBICU(1);
134	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG24 = LCDC_HEOCFG24_VXSYFACT(vf);
135	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG25 = LCDC_HEOCFG25_VXSCFACT(vf);
136	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG26 = LCDC_HEOCFG26_HXSYFACT(hf);
137	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG27 = LCDC_HEOCFG27_HXSCFACT(hf);
138	    }
139	    else
140	    {
141	        /* Disable scaler — matches MCC's HEO-setup defaults. */
142	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(0)
143	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(0)
144	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0)
145	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);

148	    /* §44.6.4.7 — discard BASE DMA in the destination rect. HEO with MCC's

162	
163	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: HEO bound src %lux%lu → dst %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) %s\r\n",
164	             (unsigned long)src_w, (unsigned long)src_h,
165	             (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
166	             (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y,
167	             scaling ? "scaled" : "1:1");
168	}

178	/* ─── Frame-done ISR (runs in IRQ context) ─────────────────────────────── */

180	static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
181	                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
182	                          uintptr_t ctx)
183	{
184	    (void)ctx;
185	
186	    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;
187	
188	    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
189	     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
190	     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
191	     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
192	     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
193	    if (s_display_bound)
194	    {
195	        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
196	    }
197	
198	    Video_FrameInfo info =
199	    {
200	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
201	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
202	        .width           = s_src_w,
203	        .height          = s_src_h,
204	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
205	    };
206	
207	    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
208	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
209	    {
210	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
211	        if (q != NULL)
212	        {
213	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
214	        }
215	    }
216	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
217	}

220	
221	static bool capture_arm(void)
222	{
223	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
224	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
225	
226	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
227	    s_src_w = w;
228	    s_src_h = h;
229	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
230	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
231	    {
232	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
233	        return false;
234	    }
235	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
236	    return true;
237	}
238	
239	static void capture_disarm(void)
240	{
241	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
242	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
243	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
244	}

246	/* Bind/unbind display from current intent + most-recent source size +

250	static void display_apply(void)
251	{
252	    window_t w = s_window;
253	    bool window_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
254	    bool source_valid = (s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u);
255	    bool want = s_display_shown && source_valid && window_valid;
256	
257	    if (want && !s_display_bound)
258	    {
259	        lcd_bind(s_src_w, s_src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
260	        s_display_bound = true;
261	    }
262	    else if (!want && s_display_bound)
263	    {
264	        lcd_unbind();
265	        s_display_bound = false;
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* Each tick: align current chain state (capture armed / display bound) to
270	 * the user's intent flags, given the current source-lock state. */
271	static void reconcile(void)
272	{
273	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
274	
275	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
276	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
277	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
278	    {
279	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
280	    }
281	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
282	    {
283	        capture_disarm();
284	        s_capture_armed = false;
285	    }
286	
287	    /* Display: shown iff intent + we have a source size to work with. The
288	     * source size is captured at arm time and persists across capture

290	    display_apply();
291	}

293	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
294	
295	static void video_task(void *param)
296	{
297	    (void)param;
298	
299	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
300	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge,
301	     * backlight, and parks the panel in UI-only mode. */
302	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
303	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
304	    TC358743_Initialize();
305	    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
306	    lcd_unbind();
307	
308	    for (;;)
309	    {
310	        TC358743_Tasks();
311	        reconcile();
312	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
313	    }
314	}
315	
316	/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
317	
318	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
319	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
320	
321	void Video_Initialize(void)
322	{
323	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
324	                            "VideoTask",
325	                            VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
326	                            NULL,
327	                            VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
328	                            s_task_stack,
329	                            &s_task_tcb);
330	}
331	
332	void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
333	void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
334	
335	void Video_DisplayShow(void)    { s_display_shown = true;    }
336	void Video_DisplayHide(void)    { s_display_shown = false;   }
337	
338	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
339	{
340	    window_t w = { x, y, dst_w, dst_h };
341	    s_window = w;
342	    /* Force a re-bind on next reconcile if we're currently shown. */
343	    s_display_bound = false;
344	}

346	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
347	{
348	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
349	
350	    bool ok = false;
351	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
352	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
353	    {
354	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q) { ok = true; break; }     /* already in */
355	        if (s_subscribers[i] == NULL)
356	        {
357	            s_subscribers[i] = q;
358	            ok = true;
359	            break;
360	        }
361	    }
362	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
363	
364	    if (!ok) { LOG_ERROR("VIDEO: subscriber table full (max %u)\r\n",
365	                         (unsigned)VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS); }
366	    return ok;
367	}
368	
369	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
370	{
371	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
372	
373	    bool ok = false;
374	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
375	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
376	    {
377	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q)
378	        {
379	            s_subscribers[i] = NULL;
380	            ok = true;
381	            break;
382	        }
383	    }
384	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
385	    return ok;
386	}

389	{

391	    info->buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
392	    info->frame_count     = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
393	    info->width           = s_src_w;

12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app

30	static void drain_task(void *param)
31	{
32	    (void)param;
33	
34	    TickType_t window_start = xTaskGetTickCount();
35	    uint32_t   window_count = 0;
36	
37	    for (;;)
38	    {
39	        detector_state_t state;
40	        if (xQueueReceive(s_bus_queue, &state, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE)
41	        {
42	            continue;
43	        }
44	        window_count++;
45	
46	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
47	        if ((uint32_t)(now - window_start) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(DRAIN_LOG_INTERVAL_MS))
48	        {
49	            LOG_INFO("DETECTOR: bus drain %lu records/s (last epoch=%lu id=%u)\r\n",
50	                     (unsigned long)window_count,
51	                     (unsigned long)state.frame_epoch,
52	                     (unsigned)state.detector_id);
53	            window_start = now;
54	            window_count = 0;
55	        }
56	    }
57	}
58

60	{

65	    configASSERT(s_bus_queue != NULL);
66

68	
69	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(drain_task,

72	                            NULL,
73	                            DRAIN_TASK_PRIORITY,
74	                            s_drain_stack,
75	                            &s_drain_tcb);

19	/* Capture frames are BGR888 packed, 3 bytes per pixel. Frames whose
20	 * bytes_per_pixel disagrees are skipped — defensive guard against

22	#define CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL     3u

25	/* Hold sensor (brightness): rising edge above CV_HOLD_THRESH; releases

28	 * fret needs its own. Mirrors fret-tuner detect_video.py defaults. */
29	#define CV_HOLD_THRESH         100.0f
30	#define CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC   0.78f
31	#define CV_EDGE_THRESH         25.0f

35	/* Sensor coordinates in native capture-frame space, anchored to 720×480
36	 * (Wii 480p60 — primary production source). (hx,hy) = brightness sensor,
37	 * (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor; both above the strike line.
38	 * Derived from fret-tuner detect_video.py 1920×1080 defaults via the
39	 * same Elgato HDMI capture, scaled by (3/8, 4/9). Runtime calibration
40	 * UI lands with M6. */
41	typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } sensor_xy_t;
42	
43	static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] =
44	{
45	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
46	    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },
47	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { 355, 311, 368, 311 },
48	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
49	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },
50	};

52	/* Per-fret BGR target / reject weights. Edge signal is
53	 * (target·c − max(0, reject·c)) × sat_ratio. Reject totals exceed 1.0
54	 * so camera-captured whites with color-temperature bias get suppressed,
55	 * not just mathematically perfect whites. */
56	typedef struct { float target[3]; float reject[3]; } color_filter_t;
57	
58	static const color_filter_t s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT] =
59	{
60	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.0f, 0.7f } },
61	    [FRET_RED]    = { { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.7f, 0.0f } },
62	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { { 0.0f, 0.5f, 0.5f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
63	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { { 1.0f, 0.4f, 0.0f }, { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.4f } },
64	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
65	};

70	static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
