81	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
82	
83	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
84	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
85	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
86	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
87	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
88	{
89	    int cx = (int)px;
90	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
91	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
92	    int cy = (int)py;
93	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
94	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
95	
96	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
97	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
98	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
99	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
100	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
101	
102	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
103	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
104	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
105	    {
106	        const uint8_t *row = frame
107	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
108	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
109	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
110	        {
111	            sum_b += row[0];
112	            sum_g += row[1];
113	            sum_r += row[2];
114	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
115	        }
116	    }
117	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
118	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
119	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
120	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
121	}
122	
123	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
124	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
125	{
126	    float m = bgr[0];
127	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
128	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
129	    return m;
130	}
131	
132	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
133	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
134	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
135	{
136	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
137	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
138	    float cmin = bgr[0];
139	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
140	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
141	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
142	
143	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
144	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
145	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
146	    return (target - reject) * sat;
147	}
148	
149	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
150	
151	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
152	{
153	    detector_state_t state;
154	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
155	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
156	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
157	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
158	
159	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
160	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
161	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
162	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
163	
164	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
165	    {
166	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
167	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
168	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
170	
171	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
172	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
173	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
174	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
175	
176	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
177	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
178	
179	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
180	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
181	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
182	
183	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
184	
185	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
186	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
187	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
188	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
189	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
190	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
191	
192	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
193	        float h = hd;
194	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
195	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
196	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
197	    }
198	
199	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
200	}

7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via
11	 * FretboardLink_Send. One of several possible producers — game menu
12	 * control (spec §4.8) and manual test inputs share the same submit API.
13	 *
14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33	
34	/* Output gate. Default: true. When false, the pipeline still advances
35	 * internal state but suppresses the FretboardLink_Send call so a peer
36	 * producer (manual_control today, future game-state controller §4.8) can
37	 * own the wire. Internal state stays current so the next advance() after
38	 * re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame. */
39	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled);
40	
41	#endif
42

7	/* Fretboard link — USB CDC host writer that ferries a 7-bit GPIO bitmask
8	 * to the fretboard MCU as a stream of single-byte messages. Spec §4.4
9	 * actuator transport. Initialize first among the actuator modules so the
10	 * submit queue exists by the time any producer task starts running. Also
11	 * enables the USB host bus, so call after SYS_Initialize.
12	 *
13	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, game menu controller (spec §4.8) and
14	 * manual test inputs in the future — all submit through FretboardLink_Send.
15	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one, so
16	 * a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level arbitration
17	 * (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one layer up; the link
18	 * stays dumb. */

10	 * scheduler is running, so log_printf is safe to call from
11	 * APP_Initialize / SYS_Initialize.

14	 * diagnostics (queue to a task, or atomic counter polled by a task).
15	 */

19	    LOG_LEVEL_ERROR = 0,
20	    LOG_LEVEL_WARN  = 1,
21	    LOG_LEVEL_INFO  = 2,
22	    LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG = 3,
23	} log_level_t;

26	 * Pass the initial filter level. */

30	log_level_t log_get_level(void);

33	void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
34	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));

38	#define LOG_WARN(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_WARN,  __VA_ARGS__)
39	#define LOG_INFO(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_INFO,  __VA_ARGS__)

1	#include "log.h"
2	
3	#include <stdarg.h>
4	#include <stdbool.h>
5	#include <stdio.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "semphr.h"
9	#include "task.h"
10	
11	static volatile log_level_t s_level = LOG_LEVEL_INFO;
12	static SemaphoreHandle_t    s_mutex;
13	static StaticSemaphore_t    s_mutex_buf;
14	
15	void log_init(log_level_t initial_level)
16	{
17	    s_level = initial_level;
18	    /* Safe before vTaskStartScheduler; only Take/Give require the
19	     * scheduler to be running. */
20	    s_mutex = xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic(&s_mutex_buf);
21	}
22	
23	void log_set_level(log_level_t lvl)
24	{
25	    s_level = lvl;
26	}
27	
28	log_level_t log_get_level(void)
29	{
30	    return s_level;
31	}
32	
33	void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap)
34	{
35	    if ((int)lvl > (int)s_level) { return; }
36	
37	    /* Take the mutex only when the scheduler is running and the mutex
38	     * was created. Pre-scheduler we're single-threaded so interleaving
39	     * isn't possible; xSemaphoreTake with portMAX_DELAY would hang
40	     * before vTaskStartScheduler. */
41	    bool locked = false;
42	    if (s_mutex != NULL
43	        && xTaskGetSchedulerState() == taskSCHEDULER_RUNNING)
44	    {
45	        if (xSemaphoreTake(s_mutex, portMAX_DELAY) == pdTRUE)
46	        {
47	            locked = true;
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    (void)vprintf(fmt, ap);
52	
53	    if (locked)
54	    {
55	        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_mutex);
56	    }
57	}
58	
59	void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
60	{
61	    va_list ap;
62	    va_start(ap, fmt);
63	    log_vprintf(lvl, fmt, ap);
64	    va_end(ap);
65	}

184	        close_cdc();

203	    for (;;)

206	        {

209	        }

211	        uint8_t mask;
212	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
213	        {
214	            last_mask = mask;
215	        }
216	        else

218	            mask = last_mask;
219	        }

### 6. Log Module
**[log.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/log.c) | [log.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/log.h)**

**Severity levels** (lines 17–23 in header): `LOG_LEVEL_ERROR=0`, `WARN=1`, `INFO=2`, `DEBUG=3`

**Output sink**: Goes through libc `printf` → `xc32_monitor` → DBGU (see comment line 9 in log.h)

**Mutex protection**: Lines 44–49 in `log_vprintf`: Takes `s_mutex` with `portMAX_DELAY` **only when scheduler is running** (line 43: `xTaskGetSchedulerState() == taskSCHEDULER_RUNNING`). Pre-scheduler it's single-threaded so no lock. **ISR-illegal**: `portMAX_DELAY` blocks indefinitely, violates ISR restrictions.

**Reuse for perf-log?** No — log module uses blocking mutex (`portMAX_DELAY`) which is ISR-illegal. Perf-log needs its own non-blocking writer (lock-free ring buffer or ISR-safe queue). For binary streaming, consider a dedicated circular buffer + background drain task.

SemaphoreHandle_t sem = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_sem_buf);

```

# Marvin perf-log subsystem — implementation plan

## 1. Recommended producer architecture

**Pick option (b) with one twist: two FreeRTOS queues feeding a single drain task, where the small queue is MPSC and always present, and the large (patch) queue is conditionally allocated for Phase B.** Rationale:

- **(a) rejected**: a union-sized record forces ~1 KB/slot for all producers. State-only at 60 Hz becomes 60 × ~14 records × 1 KB = 800 KB/s of *queue* traffic, and the patch tier punishes every other record. Wrong fit.
- **(c) rejected**: per-producer SPSC rings duplicate static plumbing we already have working everywhere else (`xQueueCreateStatic`), and N-way host-side stitching costs maintenance for a marginal latency win on a Cortex-A5 that handles seven `xQueueSendFromISR` calls per frame trivially.
- **(b) wins** because the ~30× size ratio between state and patch records makes them deserve different slots, and a single drain task with `xQueueSelectFromSet` (static queue set) multiplexes deterministically.

Concrete shape:

- `s_state_q` — MPSC, **40 B** slots (see §2 for why 40 not 32), depth **128** (≈ 2 frames headroom: ISC IRQ + video publish + cv start/end + TP tick + FBL send + CDC complete = 7 producers × ~2 frames = 14 records/frame minimum). Static BSS storage: 5 KB.
- `s_patch_q` — MPSC, **800 B** slots, depth **8**. Allocated only when `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` is set at compile time (Phase B); otherwise the 6.4 KB BSS isn't paid.
- `s_drain_task` at `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` — below detector and timing tasks, above idle. 2 KB stack.
- All seven producers go through one façade: `PerfLog_Emit_*` internally branches on `xPortIsInsideInterrupt()` to pick `xQueueSendFromISR` vs `xQueueSend(..., 0)`. Both with **zero** block time. **Drop on full, never block.**

**Failure modes:**
- *Full small queue*: increment `s_dropped_state` (LDREX/STREX or `__atomic_add_fetch`); next successfully-emitted record from drain task carries the count via a periodic `PERF_REC_DROP` (once per second). Never log from ISR.
- *Full patch queue*: separate counter; state stream unaffected. Graceful degradation is the point of separating them.
- *Drain task starved*: visible as growing drop counter on the host. We do **not** raise drain above detector/timing — losing perf data is preferable to dropping a real frame.
- *Out-of-order across the two queues*: records carry `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`; host sorts. Wire order is best-effort.

**μs timestamp source (Q5):** use `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` — TC0 CH0 already drives SYS_TIME at **266.66 MHz** (~3.75 ns/tick), backed by a single register read of `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV`. ISR-safe, lock-free, atomic 32-bit per the journal's existing video-fan-out invariant. The on-target record carries the raw 32-bit counter value plus a one-shot `PERF_REC_SESSION` carrying `SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet()`; host divides to μs. 32-bit @ 266 MHz wraps every ~16 s — drain task observes wraps and emits a wrap marker, or we widen to 64-bit on-device by sampling `xTaskGetTickCount()` alongside (cheap, single tick read). The current `xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK` pattern at `cv_marvin_v1.c:156` is millisecond resolution masquerading as μs and **must not be reused** for perf records.

## 2. Record schema

Fixed-width little-endian, naturally aligned, consistent with §4.6.5.

**Common 16 B header (every record):**
- `uint16_t magic` = `0x4D56` ("MV", little-endian on the wire)
- `uint8_t  type` (PERF_REC_*)
- `uint8_t  flags` (bit 0 = `from_isr`, bits 1..7 reserved)
- `uint32_t frame_epoch` (from `Video_FrameInfo.frame_count`)
- `uint64_t ts_counter` (raw `SYS_TIME_CounterGet`, host divides by FreqGet)

**Bodies (small queue):**
- `PERF_REC_STAMP` (type=1) — body 16 B: `uint8_t stage_id; uint8_t reserved[3]; uint32_t aux; uint64_t reserved`. `stage_id` enum: `ISC_IRQ`, `VIDEO_PUBLISH`, `CV_START`, `CV_END`, `TP_TICK`, `FBL_SEND`, `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE`. `aux` carries scalars (e.g. `publish_mask` for FBL_SEND, FIFO depth for TP_TICK). Total record = **32 B**.
- `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` (type=2) — body 24 B: 5 × `(uint16_t hold_dist, uint16_t edge_dist)` = 20 B + `uint8_t pressed_mask` + `uint8_t edge_active_mask` + 2 B pad = 24 B. `hold_dist`/`edge_dist` are 16-bit fixed-point conversions of cv_marvin_v1's floats (reuse the existing `detector_state_t.confidence`/`raw_value` scaling so the host decoder shares one conversion). Total record = **40 B** — sets the small-queue slot size.
- `PERF_REC_TIMING` (type=3) — body 16 B: `uint8_t window_fill; uint8_t fifo_depth; uint8_t publish_mask; int8_t strum_dir; uint32_t reserved; uint64_t reserved`. Total **32 B**.
- `PERF_REC_DROP` (type=4) — body 16 B: `uint32_t dropped_state; uint32_t dropped_patch; uint64_t reserved`. Drain task emits 1 Hz.
- `PERF_REC_SESSION` (type=5) — body 16 B: `uint32_t timer_freq_hz; uint32_t schema_version; uint64_t fw_git_short`. Emitted once on perf-log start.

**Body (large queue):**
- `PERF_REC_PATCH` (type=6) — body 768 B: 16 B sub-header (per-fret offsets, sample coords) + 5 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 3 = 750 B + 2 B pad. Total record = **784 B**, fits 800 B slot.

**Slot sizes (final): small queue 40 B, large queue 800 B.**

**Wire framing (Phase A & B):** `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56` start-of-frame + `uint16_t length` + payload + `uint16_t CRC-16/CCITT` over length+payload. Mid-session connect resyncs by scanning for the magic and validating CRC. CRC-16 chosen for table-driven simplicity; ~5 cycles/byte is negligible at 11 KB/s.

**Schema versioning:** `PERF_REC_SESSION.schema_version = 1`; bump on any wire-format change. Decoder rejects unknown magic or unsupported `schema_version`.

## 3. Decoupled records-per-stage model — endorsed

Validated. Each producer emits its own typed record keyed by `frame_epoch`, host stitches. Reasons:

- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` means the same `frame_epoch` is touched across ~13 real-time frames.** Forcing a wide per-frame record requires either buffering 13 frames of partial state in firmware (unbounded) or emitting partial records with TBD markers (unparseable mid-stream). Decoupled records-per-stage with `frame_epoch` keys lets each producer fire at its natural moment with no rendezvous.
- **Matches existing bus mechanics** (§4.2.4): `detector_state_t` is already per-emit on `xDetectorStateQueue`. Same shape for the perf bus → consistent mental model.
- **Host-side join is trivial**: group by `frame_epoch`, sort by `ts_counter` within group, render Gantt-style.

Minor push-back: where two records are naturally co-produced (`PERF_REC_DETECTOR` and `PERF_REC_TIMING` both during `detect_frame` / `tp_handle_state`), emit them back-to-back from the same call site to amortise queue overhead. No structural change.

## 4. Drain-task duties

- **Sink fan-out.** Static array of `perf_log_sink_t` function-pointer + ctx pairs (max 4). Phase A registers DBGU UART; Phase B adds USB CDC device. Multiple sinks can be active simultaneously per §6 toggle model. Drain writes to each in sequence; each sink owns its backpressure.
- **Framing.** Drain wraps each dequeued record in start-of-frame + length + CRC before handing to sinks. Sinks see framed bytes only — keeps them dumb.
- **Backpressure.** Sink `write` is non-blocking and returns bytes-written. If a sink stalls, drain drops *for that sink* (per-sink drop counter) and moves on. Never blocks across sinks. UART sink uses a small TX ring (~2 KB) with non-blocking USART writes; CDC sink (Phase B) mirrors `fretboard_link.c`'s host-side write/semaphore pattern in the device direction.
- **Drop-on-full vs blocking write: drop, always.** The whole subsystem must be able to vanish without affecting the real-time pipeline.
- **Priority: `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2`.** Below detector/timing, above idle. Stack 2 KB static.

## 5. ISR producer details

Beyond the §1 façade:

- `on_frame_done` (`video.c:180`): emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=ISC_IRQ}` *before* the subscriber fan-out loop, and `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=VIDEO_PUBLISH}` *after*. Two `*FromISR` calls.
- `cdc_event_handler` (`fretboard_link.c:60`) `WRITE_COMPLETE` case: emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE}`. Existing `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` precedent confirms `*FromISR` is correct. **Critical: do not LOG_INFO from this handler** — that's the 2026-05-21 freeze pattern. Perf-log emit path uses no mutexes, by construction.
- Task-context producers (cv_marvin_v1, timing_pipeline, FretboardLink_Send) take the non-ISR branch (`xQueueSend(..., 0)`). Zero block.

## 6. FreeRTOS analytics integration

**Keep parallel** — do not bundle into Phase A. Reasons:
1. `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` needs a *second* TC channel for the stats counter; TC0 CH0 is owned by SYS_TIME and we shouldn't reuse it without a re-architecture pass.
2. Analytics output (`vTaskGetRunTimeStats` text dump) is fundamentally a different consumer from binary perf records.
3. The journal already lists analytics as a separate carry-forward item.

**Cheap freebie**: emit a periodic `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` (10 s cadence) calling `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` for each known task — no FreeRTOS config flag needed, addresses the freeze-misdiagnosis lesson from 2026-05-21. Add as Phase A stretch, not blocker.

## 7. Phase B USB device CDC — the port question

**This is a real hardware-level snag.** Per `initialization.c:176-199`, both PC27 and PC31 belong to UHPHS (USB Host High-Speed; one EHCI, one OHCI, shared interrupt). SAM9X75 has a separate UDPHS (USB Device High-Speed) peripheral on different pads. To get a device-mode port, we need either:

- **(a)** Route UDPHS to a free pad set on this board. Requires schematic verification — UDPHS pins must physically reach a connector.
- **(b)** Reconfigure one UHPHS port as Dual-Role / OTG (only viable if the SAM9X75 supports DRD on UHPHS — datasheet check required).

**Action: confirm UDPHS pad availability on the SAM9X75 board before any Phase B implementation work.** If unavailable, fallbacks are (i) Ethernet (5 MB/s per the journal's bandwidth table), (ii) ship state-only over UART forever and defer patches to the SD recording path. **Phase B is gated on this hardware question.**

## 8. Module file layout

New files (matches the existing tree):

- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.h` — public API: `PerfLog_Init`, `PerfLog_Start`, `PerfLog_EmitStamp(stage, aux)`, `PerfLog_EmitDetector(...)`, `PerfLog_EmitTiming(...)`, `PerfLog_EmitPatch(...)`, `PerfLog_RegisterSink(sink)`. All safe in task or ISR context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c` — implementation, queues, drain task, façade, framing, CRC.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h` — wire-format structs and enums (the §2 schema). Header-only; copy-pasted into the host decoder at schema bumps.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_uart.c` — Phase A sink, framed binary over FLEXCOM4 DBGU. Coexists with `log_printf` text; the host decoder demuxes by start-of-frame magic and treats unframed bytes as passthrough text.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — Phase B sink (stubbed in Phase A).

Host-side decoder (Phase A deliverable, shared with Phase B):

- `tools/perf-log-decoder/` — Python (consistent with `tools/fret-tuner/`). Reads framed binary from a serial port or stdin, validates CRC, demuxes by record type, joins by `frame_epoch`, emits CSV/JSON or a Gantt-style HTML report. `perf_log_records.py` mirrors `perf_log_records.h` (single source of truth in C; Python derived by hand at schema bumps).

`cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` additions: append `src/perf_log/perf_log.c` and `src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_uart.c` to `target_sources`. Add `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` in Phase B with a `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` `target_compile_definitions` toggle.

## 9. Phase A deliverables

1. Land `perf_log/` module: queues, drain-task skeleton, façade, framing, CRC, no producers wired. `PerfLog_Init` from `APP_Initialize`; `PerfLog_Start` from `app.c` after scheduler-dependent services. Verify a `PERF_REC_SESSION` record is visible on the host.
2. Wire ISR producers (video.c × 2, fretboard_link.c CDC complete). Smoke-test by hammering the CDC write path with manual-control input while perf-log is live — must not freeze (regression check on 2026-05-21).
3. Wire task-context producers (cv_marvin_v1 start/end, timing_pipeline tick, FretboardLink_Send).
4. Implement `perf_log_sink_uart.c` — framed binary writes through the existing console UART. Don't clobber `LOG_INFO` text; host decoder filters by magic.
5. Build `tools/perf-log-decoder/`: CSV for spreadsheet inspection, Gantt HTML for visual latency attribution.
6. Validate end-to-end: 60 Hz session, decode, confirm `ISC_IRQ → CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` is single-digit ms and `frame_epoch → strum` is ~220 ms (TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS).
7. Stretch: periodic `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` (10 s).

## 10. Phase B deliverables

0. **GATE: confirm UDPHS pad availability** on the SAM9X75 board. Schematic + datasheet. If unavailable, halt and revisit.
1. MCC regen with USB device peripheral (UDPHS) + USB device CDC class. New entry in the MCC re-apply list (similar shape to existing patch #5).
2. Implement `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — device-side CDC write. Mirrors `fretboard_link.c`'s host-side write/`xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` pattern in the device direction.
3. Enable `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` build flag; allocate the 800 B × 8 patch queue. Wire `PERF_REC_PATCH` emit in `cv_marvin_v1.detect_frame` after the 5×5 sample loop (copy patches into the record).
4. Update host decoder for `PERF_REC_PATCH` — render per-frame strip image (5 frets × 2 patches = 10 thumbnails) overlaid on the Gantt timeline.
5. Validate sustained 54 KB/s over USB CDC device, confirm patch queue drop rate ≈ 0 at steady state.

## 11. Risks / open questions to surface before implementation

1. **UDPHS pad availability** (§7) — Phase B gate. Highest-priority unknown; ask the user before scheduling Phase B.
2. **`SYS_TIME_CounterGet` ISR safety on this build.** Strongly believed safe (single register read of `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV`), but worth a one-line confirmation test (read counter from a high-priority ISR vs task-side, cross-check) before all seven producers depend on it.
3. **Console UART contention.** Phase A shares FLEXCOM4 with `log_printf`. 115.2 kBd ⇒ ~11 KB/s budget; state-only is ~9 KB/s; a verbose `LOG_INFO` burst will starve perf records. Options: drop low-frequency perf records when text logs spike; accept gaps as expected; or raise log-level filter while perf-log is active. **Surface this trade-off to the user** before committing.
4. **`frame_epoch` rollover at ~830 days.** Out of scope for perf-log (M5 owns the persistent counter); host decoder must handle the 32-bit wrap if a session straddles. Document.
5. **Detector fixed-point conversion.** cv_marvin_v1's `hold_dist`/`edge_dist` are floats; `detector_state_t` already has `confidence`/`raw_value` (uint16) scaling. Reuse exactly that scaling in `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` to keep one conversion path. 5-minute decision; flag for confirmation.
6. **Drain-task starvation under heavy detection load.** Acceptance test: 60 Hz steady-state for 5 min, measure `dropped_state`. Non-zero → raise drain priority by 1 and retest.
7. **CRC choice.** Picked CRC-16/CCITT (table-driven, simple). CRC-32 is overkill for 32 B payloads but matches what the future SD recording format may want. One-line decision before implementation.

# What's being built

A perf-log subsystem that captures, per-frame:

1. **Latency stamps** — μs-resolution timestamps at: ISC IRQ entry, video publish, cv detector start/end, timing-pipeline tick, fretboard_link send, USB CDC write-completion ISR. Lets us attribute frame-to-wire latency.
2. **Detector internals** — per-fret hold_dist and edge_dist (currently float in cv_marvin_v1.c; 16-bit fixed in the log), pressed/edge_active flags. cv_marvin_v1's `s_press_count[]` stays private — not in the record.
3. **Timing-pipeline state** — chord-window fill, FIFO depth, last publish_mask, current strum direction.
4. **(Tier 2) ROI patches** — 5 frets × 2 patches (hold + edge) × 5×5 BGR = 750 B. Optional per-record.

Stream sizing:
- State-only @ 60 Hz: ~9 KB/s
- With patches @ 60 Hz: ~54 KB/s

# Phasing

- **Phase A**: Producer + ring + binary stream over existing DBGU console UART (FLEXCOM4, 115.2 kBd, ~11 KB/s). State-only fits; no patches. Includes a host-side decoder tool.
- **Phase B**: USB device CDC sink. Brings full ~54 KB/s with patches. Requires new MCC config (USB device peripheral currently unused), new host-side reader. Host-side decoder is shared with Phase A.

NOT in scope: SD sink (defer to milestone M4 recording bring-up; no SDMMC/SYS_FS exists yet).

# Producers (real call sites in the codebase)

Per the prior exploration:
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c:180` — `on_frame_done` ISR entry. Need ISR-safe push.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c:213` — `xQueueSendFromISR` to subscribers. Same ISR.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:325` — task wakes from `xQueueReceive`. Task context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:199` — `detect_frame` populates state and pushes to bus. Task context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c` — bus-receive site (~line 300+) and `publish_mask` (line 137). Task context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:262` — `FretboardLink_Send`. Task context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c:60` — `cdc_event_handler` ISR, fires on `WRITE_COMPLETE`. ISR context. Existing handler already uses `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR`.

# Constraints / known traps

- **TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms**: detector frame N's wire-out is ~13 frames later. Implies records keyed on `frame_epoch` are emitted across many real-time frames. Producers across the pipeline don't all see the *same* frame at the same wall-clock instant.
- **The existing log shim takes a mutex with portMAX_DELAY** — ISR-illegal. Perf-log cannot reuse it. Past freeze: 2026-05-21 entry where logging from a CDC ISR locked the system.
- **`frame_epoch` source**: today it comes from `Video_FrameInfo.frame_count`, monotonic since arm; M5 will replace with a persistent counter. Don't block on that.
- **Cortex-A5 atomicity**: aligned 32-bit pointer reads/writes are atomic per the journal (the multi-subscriber video fan-out relies on this). LDREX/STREX exist, so `stdatomic` works if needed.

# Specific design questions to answer

1. **Ring/queue strategy.** Three candidates:
   (a) **Single MPMC FreeRTOS queue** with fixed-size records (union over all record types, sized to largest tag). Simple, ISR-safe via `*FromISR`, drops on full. Fixed-size means the patch tier blows up the per-record size for everyone — bad fit.
   (b) **Two queues** — one fixed-size for state records (~32 B), one bigger-record queue for patches (~1 KB). Drain task pulls from both, interleaves by timestamp at the wire.
   (c) **Lock-free SPSC ring per producer** — one ring per producer, drain task arbitrates. Avoids MPSC at the cost of stitching on the host side.
   Pick one, justify, identify failure modes.

2. **Record format.** Tagged union with discriminator? Per-type sub-records keyed by frame_epoch? Endianness, padding, schema versioning. The on-disk recording schema in spec §4.6 is fixed-width little-endian — perf-log should match where reasonable so a future shared decoder is feasible.

3. **The decoupled-records-per-stage model.** I'm leaning on each producer emitting its own typed record keyed by frame_epoch, host-side joining. Validate or push back.

4. **Drain-task duties.** Sink fan-out (multiple sinks active simultaneously per spec §6 toggle model), framing (length-prefix + CRC for resync on mid-session connect), backpressure (drop on full ring vs blocking write). Drain-task priority relative to detector + timing tasks.

5. **ISR producer details.** From video.c's `on_frame_done` ISR and fretboard_link.c's `cdc_event_handler` ISR, the FreeRTOS-safe pattern is `xQueueSendFromISR`. But the record we want includes a timestamp — calling `xTaskGetTickCountFromISR` is fine, but for μs resolution we need a free-running cycle counter or SYS_TIME. Identify the right μs source on this platform (the existing modules use `xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK = 1000` which is ms-resolution masquerading as μs — not good enough for latency attribution within a 16.7 ms frame).

6. **FreeRTOS analytics integration.** `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` and `configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY` are both 0 today. The journal lists "FreeRTOS analytics not yet enabled" as a carried-forward item. Recommend whether to bundle these into Phase A or keep parallel.

7. **Phase B USB device CDC.** Note: SAM9X75's two USB ports (VBUS_AH on PC27, PC31) are both currently host-mode for fretboard_link. Identify whether one of them can switch to device for the perf-log sink, or whether device mode requires a different physical port. This may be a hardware-level snag; flag it.

8. **Module file layout** that fits the existing tree pattern (`default/src/perf_log/perf_log.{c,h}` etc.), and `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` additions.

# What I want back

A written implementation plan, structured as:
1. Recommended producer architecture (1.5 of the design questions resolved with rationale)
2. Record schema (concrete C-struct sketches, fixed sizes called out)
3. Module file layout + new files
4. Phase A deliverables (concrete tasks)
5. Phase B deliverables (concrete tasks; flag the USB-port question)
6. Risks / open questions worth surfacing to the user before implementation

Aim for 800–1500 words. No code blocks longer than 20 lines. Don't write any files. Don't run tests.

Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.

#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)

```
typedef struct {
    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
    uint8_t  reserved[3];
    struct {
        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
} detector_state_t;
```

Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.

#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics

- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.

#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities

`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:

- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.

#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here

- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)

### 4.3 Fretboard link 🚧

UART between marvin and the fretboard MCU, bidirectional, framed.

- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). Same intent as fret-tuner's existing 1-byte bitmask; precise framing TBD in §5.
- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 500 Hz, plus enable/SW0 state. Reuses the fret-tuner 12-byte ADC frame format if practical.
- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.

### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧

Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:

- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
- Per-fret release scheduling.
- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.

**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.

### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧

10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:

- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).

**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).

### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧

#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)

1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.

Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.

#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card

Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.

Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.

#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes

A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:

```
recordings/
└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
    └── keyframes/
        ├── 000000.bgrx        // raw BGRX32 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
        ├── 000060.bgrx
        └── ...
```

- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 500 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~6 KB/s. Modest.
- **Keyframes** — raw BGRX32 dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 BGRX = 1.38 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.38 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~415 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.

Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.

#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`

A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.

For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.

#### 4.6.5 manifest.json

Minimum fields:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGRX32" },
  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
  "detectors": [
    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
```
</details></tool-use>

|---|---|
| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |

A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.

/* Hide HEO and let BASE (Legato UI) fill the whole panel. */
static void lcd_unbind(void)
{
    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 &= ~LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
}

/* ─── Frame-done ISR (runs in IRQ context) ─────────────────────────────── */

static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
                          uintptr_t ctx)
{
    (void)ctx;

    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;

    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
    if (s_display_bound)
    {
        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
    }

    Video_FrameInfo info =
    {
        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
        .frame_count     = frame_count,
        .width           = s_src_w,
        .height          = s_src_h,
        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
    };

    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
    {
        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
        if (q != NULL)
        {
            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
        }
    }
    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
}

/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static bool capture_arm(void)
{
    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }

/* ─── Calibration overlay ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u

static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
};

static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
                                 int x, int y,
                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
{
    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
}

/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
{
    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
    while (x >= y)
    {
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
        y++;
        err += 1 + 2 * y;
        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
    }
}

static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
{
    int rr = radius * radius;
    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
    {
        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
        {
            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
            {
                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
            }
        }
    }
}

/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u

static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
{
    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
    {
        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];

        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);

        if (s_pressed[i])
        {
            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
        }
        if (s_edge_active[i])
        {
            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
        }
    }
}

/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
    configASSERT(subscribed);

    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
    configASSERT(bus != NULL);

    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");

    for (;;)
    {
        Video_FrameInfo frame;
        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }

        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }

bool FretboardLink_IsConnected(void)
{
    return s_connected;

void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask)
{
    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
     * stale chord state. */
    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);
}
---tp publish_mask---
}

static bool strum_q_any_needs(uint8_t bit)
{
    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_strum_count; i++)
    {
        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
        if (s_strum_q[idx].fret_mask & bit) { return true; }
    }
    return false;
}

static void publish_mask(uint8_t mask)
{
    s_output_mask = mask;
    if (s_pipeline_enabled)
    {
        FretboardLink_Send(mask);
    }
}

The pin-macro generator produces `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_*` and `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_*` separately and no unified wrapper, so the MCC-emitted code fails to compile. Replace lines 162-163 (Set branch) and 169-170 (Clear branch) with explicit calls to both per-pin macros — `VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set(); VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();` and the matching Clear pair. The MCC comment in the function ("name it to 'VBUS_AH'") acknowledges the single-pin assumption.
106:  6. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. 108:  7. **`usb_host_cdc.c` — accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0` in CDC ACM Communications-interface match.** Two checks (single-interface path ~line 677, IAD path ~line 798) currently require `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG-style USB-to-UART bridges (the on-board PIC/AVR debugger CDC, common across Microchip dev boards — including the fretboard board this project uses) declare the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol = USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC` (`0x00`). Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. 243:**VBUS.** MCC's `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` callback is wired in the host driver but the host stack never invokes it on this build. 245:**Class-driver binding.** Enumeration succeeded but the CDC attach handler never fired. Output revealed VID `0x03EB` PID `0x2175` — an EDBG composite with five interfaces: HID/CMSIS-DAP, CDC ACM IAD pair (comm + data), vendor, MSC. The IAD passed TPL match and got assigned to the CDC driver, but the CDC instance still flipped to `STATE_ERROR` without our app-level handler ever seeing the attach.
247:Root cause was inside Microchip's CDC class driver: `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` (both single-interface and IAD paths) requires the comm interface to declare `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG declares `0x00` (none) — functionally identical CDC ACM in practice; Linux/macOS accept either. The TPL/IAD pre-check passes (TPL wildcards subclass/protocol), the CDC driver gets the interface group, then immediately rejects it on the AT-V.250 check. The interrupt pipe never opens, the instance errors out, and the app-level listener stays silent.

With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. # Marvin perf-log subsystem — implementation plan

## 1. Recommended producer architecture

**Pick option (b) with a twist: two FreeRTOS queues feeding a single drain task, where the "small" queue is MPMC and the "large" queue is created lazily for Phase B.** Justification below; (a) is rejected because a union-sized record forces ~1 KB per slot for everyone (state-only @ 60 Hz becomes 60 × 1 KB = 60 KB/s of *queue traffic*, dwarfing the 9 KB/s wire), and (c) (per-producer SPSC rings) is rejected because we already have battle-tested static FreeRTOS queue plumbing everywhere else and the host-side stitch cost from N rings is a real maintenance tax for a marginal latency win on a Cortex-A5 that handles a few `xQueueSendFromISR` per frame trivially.

Concrete shape:

- `s_state_q` — MPSC FreeRTOS queue, fixed-size **32 B** records (the largest "small" tag, see §2). Depth = **128** entries (≈ 2 frames of records at peak fan-in: ISC IRQ + video publish + cv start + cv end + TP tick + FBL send + CDC complete = 7 producers × ~2 frames = 14 records/frame minimum, headroom for backpressure spikes). Sized at compile time; `xQueueCreateStaticArray` storage in BSS.
- `s_patch_q` — MPSC FreeRTOS queue, fixed-size **800 B** records (one slot = one full ROI patch record for one frame, all 5 frets × 2 patches × 5×5 BGR = 750 B + 50 B header). Depth = **8**. Only created when Phase B enables patches at runtime; pre-allocated storage in BSS guarded by a Kconfig-style `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` compile flag so the 6.4 KB doesn't sit unused on Phase A builds.
- `s_drain_task` consumes from both with `xQueueSelectFromSet` (FreeRTOS queue set, also static) so a single task multiplexes them deterministically. Drain priority **just below the detector task** — high enough to keep the wire fed but never starve detection or timing.
- All seven producers are ISR-or-task callable through one façade: `PerfLog_Emit_*FromAny()` — internally branches on `xPortIsInsideInterrupt()` to pick `xQueueSendFromISR` vs `xQueueSend(..., 0)`. Both paths take **zero block time**: drop-on-full is the rule.

**Failure modes & answers:**
- *Full small queue.* Increment a free-running `s_dropped_state` counter (`__atomic_add_fetch`); the next successful record carries a `dropped_since_last` field in its header (or a dedicated `PERF_REC_DROP` sentinel record is emitted by the drain task once per second). Never block, never log from ISR.
- *Full patch queue.* Same shape, separate counter. Patches degrade gracefully without affecting state stream — that's the whole point of separating them.
- *Drain task starved.* Manifests as monotonically growing drop counter; visible in the host decoder. We do **not** raise drain priority above detector — losing perf data is preferable to dropping a real frame.
- *Out-of-order across queues.* Records carry `frame_epoch` + `timestamp_us`; host-side decoder sorts. Wire order is best-effort.

**Question 5 — μs timestamp source:** use `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` (TC0 CH0, 266.66 MHz, ~3.75 ns/tick) divided down to μs in the host decoder, *not* on-target. The on-target record carries the raw 32-bit counter value plus a session-start anchor (one `PERF_REC_SESSION` emitted once at task start with `SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet()` and the counter origin). 32-bit @ 266 MHz wraps every ~16 s — drain task observes wraps and the host stitches; alternatively widen on-device to 64-bit by sampling tick-count alongside (cheap). `SYS_TIME_CounterGet` is a single register read against `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV` — ISR-safe, lock-free, atomic 32-bit on Cortex-A5 per the journal's existing video-fan-out invariant. The current `xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK` pattern in `cv_marvin_v1.c:156` is millisecond resolution masquerading as μs and must not be reused for perf records (we keep it for `detector_state_t.timestamp_us` on the detector bus to avoid churning a separate change, but perf records take their own high-res stamp).

## 2. Record schema

Fixed-width little-endian, naturally aligned, matches §4.6.5 conventions so a future shared decoder can absorb perf-log records into the recording format.

**Common 16-byte header (every record):**
- `uint16_t magic` (0xMARV ⇒ 0x4D56 little-endian)
- `uint8_t  type` (discriminator; see PERF_REC_* below)
- `uint8_t  flags` (bit 0 = `from_isr`; bits 1..7 reserved)
- `uint32_t frame_epoch` (from `Video_FrameInfo.frame_count`)
- `uint64_t ts_counter` (raw `SYS_TIME_CounterGet`, host divides by FreqGet)

**Tagged record bodies (each 16 B body to keep small queue at 32 B total):**
- `PERF_REC_STAMP` (type=1) — body: `uint8_t stage_id; uint8_t reserved[3]; uint32_t aux; uint64_t reserved`. `stage_id` enum: ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE. `aux` carries per-stage scalars (e.g. `publish_mask` for FBL_SEND, FIFO depth for TP_TICK).
- `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` (type=2) — body: per-fret packed `uint16_t hold_dist; uint16_t edge_dist; uint8_t pressed:1; uint8_t edge_active:1` for 5 frets = 5 × (2+2+1) padded = 25 B → won't fit 16 B; **upgrade this record's body to 24 B** by packing `pressed`/`edge_active` as two `uint8_t` bitmasks (1 byte each) and 5 × `(uint16_t hold_dist, uint16_t edge_dist)` = 20 B, totalling 22 B + 2 B pad → 24 B. Total record = 16 + 24 = **40 B**. Bumps small-queue slot size to 40 B; depth stays 128 (5 KB BSS).
- `PERF_REC_TIMING` (type=3) — body: `uint8_t window_fill; uint8_t fifo_depth; uint8_t publish_mask; int8_t strum_dir; uint32_t reserved; uint64_t reserved` = 16 B. Total 32 B.
- `PERF_REC_DROP` (type=4) — body: `uint32_t dropped_state; uint32_t dropped_patch; uint64_t reserved` = 16 B. Emitted by drain task once per second.
- `PERF_REC_SESSION` (type=5) — body: `uint32_t timer_freq_hz; uint32_t schema_version; uint64_t fw_git_short` = 16 B. Emitted once on perf-log start.
- `PERF_REC_PATCH` (type=6, large queue only) — body: 5 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 3 = 750 B + 16 B sub-header (per-fret offsets, sample coords) = 766 B + 2 B pad → 768 B. Total 16 + 768 = **784 B**, fits the 800 B slot.

**On-disk slot sizes (final):** small queue **40 B**, large queue **800 B**.

**Schema versioning:** `PERF_REC_SESSION.schema_version` = 1 today; bump on any wire-format change. Decoder rejects records with unknown `magic` or unsupported `schema_version`.

**Framing on wire (Phase A & B):** `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56` start-of-frame + `uint16_t length` (little-endian, payload bytes) + payload + `uint16_t CRC-16/CCITT` over length+payload. Length-prefix + CRC lets a host that connects mid-stream resync by scanning for the start-of-frame and validating CRC. CRC table fits in flash; `crc16_update()` is ~5 cycles/byte — negligible at 11 KB/s.

## 3. Decoupled records-per-stage model — validated

Endorsed. Each producer emits its own typed record keyed by `frame_epoch`, host stitches. Reasons:

- **TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms means stages fire across 13+ real-time frames for the same `frame_epoch`.** Forcing a single "wide" per-frame record would require either buffering 13 frames of partial state in firmware (unbounded) or emitting partials with a "to-be-filled" marker (unparseable mid-stream). Decoupled records-per-stage with frame_epoch keys lets each producer fire at its natural moment with no cross-producer rendezvous.
- **Matches existing bus mechanics** (§4.2.4) where `detector_state_t` is a per-emit record on `xDetectorStateQueue`. We're applying the same shape to a parallel performance bus, which is consistent with the codebase mental model.
- **Host-side join is trivial** — group by `frame_epoch`, sort by `ts_counter` within group, render as a Gantt-style row per frame. No fancy stitching algorithm.

The only push-back: emit `PERF_REC_TIMING` and `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` together where they're naturally co-produced (cv detector's `detect_frame` already populates both detector state and could emit detector + a timing snapshot in two adjacent calls). Doesn't change the shape, just amortises the queue overhead.

## 4. Drain task duties

- **Sink fan-out.** Holds a static array of `perf_log_sink_t` function-pointer + ctx pairs (max 4 sinks). Phase A registers DBGU UART sink; Phase B adds USB CDC device sink. Multiple sinks can be active simultaneously per §6 toggle model — drain task writes to each in sequence, each sink owns its own backpressure semantics.
- **Framing.** Wraps each dequeued record in the start-of-frame + length + CRC envelope before handing to sinks (sink sees framed bytes, not records — keeps sinks dumb).
- **Backpressure on sinks.** Sink-side `write` returns bytes-written; if a sink stalls, drain task **drops the record for that sink** (per-sink drop counter) and moves on. Never blocks across sinks. UART sink uses a small TX ring (~2 KB) with `USART` non-blocking write; CDC sink uses the existing `USB_HOST_CDC_Write` pattern but in device direction (Phase B).
- **Drop-on-full vs blocking write.** Drop. Always. The whole subsystem must be able to vanish without affecting the real-time pipeline.
- **Drain priority.** `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2`. Detector and timing tasks at +3/+4. Below them; above idle; above any future low-priority background work.
- **Stack.** 2 KB static (CRC + buffered framing temp). Nothing recursive, no printf.

## 5. ISR producer details

Beyond §1's `xPortIsInsideInterrupt` façade:

- `on_frame_done` (video.c:180) — emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=ISC_IRQ}` *before* the subscriber fan-out loop, and `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=VIDEO_PUBLISH}` *after*. Two calls, both `*FromISR`. The journal's atomic-32-bit-pointer guarantee covers our SYS_TIME counter read (single LDR).
- `cdc_event_handler:WRITE_COMPLETE` (fretboard_link.c:60) — emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE}`. Existing `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` precedent confirms `*FromISR` is the right pattern. **Critical: do not LOG_INFO from this handler** — that's exactly the 2026-05-21 freeze pattern. The perf-log emit path uses no mutexes; verified by §1's design.
- Task-context producers (cv_marvin_v1, timing_pipeline, FretboardLink_Send) use the non-ISR branch which is `xQueueSend(..., 0)` — zero block.

## 6. FreeRTOS analytics integration

**Keep parallel.** Bundling `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` + `configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY` into Phase A would (a) require enabling a second TC channel for the runtime-stats counter (TC0 CH0 is owned by SYS_TIME — can't be reused for stats without re-architecting), (b) inflate the FreeRTOSConfig.h surface area when we're already touching it for `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS_INTERFACE`, and (c) the analytics output (vTaskGetRunTimeStats text dump) is fundamentally a different consumer pattern from binary perf records. They live in separate journal carry-forward items for a reason.

That said, perf-log Phase A **should** emit a `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` record (one-shot or periodic) that calls `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` — that's free and addresses the second freeze-misdiagnosis lesson from the journal without dragging in the full trace facility. Add as a stretch goal, not blocker.

## 7. Phase B USB device CDC — flag the port question

**This is a genuine hardware-level snag.** SAM9X75 has both UHPHS (USB Host High-Speed) and UDPHS (USB Device High-Speed) peripherals on separate pad sets. Per `initialization.c:176-199`, both PC27 and PC31 are wired to UHPHS (one EHCI + one OHCI on shared interrupt). To get a USB device-mode port, we need either:

- **(a)** Route UDPHS to a free pad set. Verify in the SAM9X75 datasheet that UDPHS pins are physically broken out on this board; if not, no software fix exists.
- **(b)** Re-MCC one of the two UHPHS ports as a Dual-Role / OTG and hope the SAM9X75 supports DRD on UHPHS (common SoCs do, but it's per-port and per-revision).

Action: **before any Phase B implementation work, confirm the UDPHS pad availability.** If UDPHS is not available, Phase B falls back to "share the existing fretboard_link CDC host port via a custom split protocol" — ugly, expensive, probably not worth doing. Realistic alternative for Phase B if UDPHS is unavailable: switch to Ethernet (the journal's bandwidth table lists Ethernet as a candidate at ~5 MB/s) or just ship state-only over UART forever and defer patches to the SD recording path.

Phase B work is gated on this hardware question. Do not start Phase B MCC config until it's answered.

## 8. Module file layout

New files (matches existing tree pattern):

- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.h` — public API: `PerfLog_Init`, `PerfLog_Start`, `PerfLog_EmitStamp(stage_id, aux)`, `PerfLog_EmitDetector(...)`, `PerfLog_EmitTiming(...)`, `PerfLog_EmitPatch(...)`, `PerfLog_RegisterSink(sink)`. All functions safe in task or ISR context.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c` — implementation: static queue storage, drain task, façade, framing, CRC.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h` — wire-format structs and enums (the §2 schema). Header-only; usable by the host-side decoder via copy-paste or symlink (preferred: copy-paste with schema_version gate).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_uart.c` — Phase A sink, framed binary over the existing FLEXCOM4 DBGU console. Coexists with `log_printf` text by stealing only the bytes we frame; the host-side decoder filters by start-of-frame magic and lets text passthrough.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — Phase B sink, USB device CDC. Stub in Phase A.

Host-side decoder (Phase A deliverable, shared with Phase B):

- `tools/perf-log-decoder/` — Python (consistent with `tools/fret-tuner/`). Reads framed binary from a serial port or stdin, validates CRC, demuxes by record type, joins by `frame_epoch`, emits CSV/JSON or a Gantt-style HTML report. Includes a minimal `perf_log_records.py` that mirrors `perf_log_records.h` (single source of truth lives in the C header; Python is generated/derived by hand at schema bumps).

`cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` additions: append `src/perf_log/perf_log.c` and `src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_uart.c` to `target_sources`. `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` added in Phase B with a `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` `target_compile_definitions` toggle.

7. Add `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` periodic emit (every 10 s) — addresses the journal's stack-overflow visibility gap as a freebie.

## 10. Phase B deliverables (concrete tasks)

## 11. Risks / open questions to surface before implementation

1. **UDPHS availability** (Phase B gate, §7). Highest-priority unknown.
2. **`SYS_TIME_CounterGet` ISR safety on this build.** I'm relying on it being a single register read of `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV`. Worth confirming with a one-line test (read counter from a high-priority ISR, compare with task-side reads) before all seven producers depend on it.

Mitigation: bump perf-log filter to drop low-frequency records when text logs spike, or accept the gaps as expected. Surface this trade-off to the user.
4. **`frame_epoch` rollover at ~830 days.** Out of scope for perf-log specifically (M5 owns the persistent counter), but the host decoder must handle the 32-bit wrap gracefully if a session straddles one. Document and move on.

# Marvin perf-log subsystem — implementation plan

## 1. Recommended producer architecture

**Pick option (b) with one twist: two FreeRTOS queues feeding a single drain task, where the small queue is MPSC and always present, and the large (patch) queue is conditionally allocated for Phase B.** Rationale:

- **(a) rejected**: a union-sized record forces ~1 KB/slot for all producers. State-only at 60 Hz becomes 60 × ~14 records × 1 KB = 800 KB/s of *queue* traffic, and the patch tier punishes every other record. Wrong fit.
- **(c) rejected**: per-producer SPSC rings duplicate static plumbing we already have working everywhere else (`xQueueCreateStatic`), and N-way host-side stitching costs maintenance for a marginal latency win on a Cortex-A5 that handles seven `xQueueSendFromISR` calls per frame trivially.
- **(b) wins** because the ~30× size ratio between state and patch records makes them deserve different slots, and a single drain task with `xQueueSelectFromSet` (static queue set) multiplexes deterministically.

Concrete shape:

- `s_state_q` — MPSC, **40 B** slots (see §2 for why 40 not 32), depth **128** (≈ 2 frames headroom: ISC IRQ + video publish + cv start/end + TP tick + FBL send + CDC complete = 7 producers × ~2 frames = 14 records/frame minimum). Static BSS storage: 5 KB.
- `s_patch_q` — MPSC, **800 B** slots, depth **8**. Allocated only when `PERF_LOG_PATCHES_ENABLED` is set at compile time (Phase B); otherwise the 6.4 KB BSS isn't paid.
- `s_drain_task` at `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` — below detector and timing tasks, above idle. 2 KB stack.
- All seven producers go through one façade: `PerfLog_Emit_*` internally branches on `xPortIsInsideInterrupt()` to pick `xQueueSendFromISR` vs `xQueueSend(..., 0)`. Both with **zero** block time. **Drop on full, never block.**

**Failure modes:**
- *Full small queue*: increment `s_dropped_state` (LDREX/STREX or `__atomic_add_fetch`); next successfully-emitted record from drain task carries the count via a periodic `PERF_REC_DROP` (once per second). Never log from ISR.
- *Full patch queue*: separate counter; state stream unaffected. Graceful degradation is the point of separating them.
- *Drain task starved*: visible as growing drop counter on the host. We do **not** raise drain above detector/timing — losing perf data is preferable to dropping a real frame.
- *Out-of-order across the two queues*: records carry `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`; host sorts. Wire order is best-effort.

**μs timestamp source (Q5):** use `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` — TC0 CH0 already drives SYS_TIME at **266.66 MHz** (~3.75 ns/tick), backed by a single register read of `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV`. ISR-safe, lock-free, atomic 32-bit per the journal's existing video-fan-out invariant. The on-target record carries the raw 32-bit counter value plus a one-shot `PERF_REC_SESSION` carrying `SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet()`; host divides to μs. 32-bit @ 266 MHz wraps every ~16 s — drain task observes wraps and emits a wrap marker, or we widen to 64-bit on-device by sampling `xTaskGetTickCount()` alongside (cheap, single tick read). The current `xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK` pattern at `cv_marvin_v1.c:156` is millisecond resolution masquerading as μs and **must not be reused** for perf records.

## 2. Record schema

Fixed-width little-endian, naturally aligned, consistent with §4.6.5.

**Common 16 B header (every record):**
- `uint16_t magic` = `0x4D56` ("MV", little-endian on the wire)
- `uint8_t  type` (PERF_REC_*)
- `uint8_t  flags` (bit 0 = `from_isr`, bits 1..7 reserved)
- `uint32_t frame_epoch` (from `Video_FrameInfo.frame_count`)
- `uint64_t ts_counter` (raw `SYS_TIME_CounterGet`, host divides by FreqGet)

**Bodies (small queue):**
- `PERF_REC_STAMP` (type=1) — body 16 B: `uint8_t stage_id; uint8_t reserved[3]; uint32_t aux; uint64_t reserved`. `stage_id` enum: `ISC_IRQ`, `VIDEO_PUBLISH`, `CV_START`, `CV_END`, `TP_TICK`, `FBL_SEND`, `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE`. `aux` carries scalars (e.g. `publish_mask` for FBL_SEND, FIFO depth for TP_TICK). Total record = **32 B**.
- `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` (type=2) — body 24 B: 5 × `(uint16_t hold_dist, uint16_t edge_dist)` = 20 B + `uint8_t pressed_mask` + `uint8_t edge_active_mask` + 2 B pad = 24 B. `hold_dist`/`edge_dist` are 16-bit fixed-point conversions of cv_marvin_v1's floats (reuse the existing `detector_state_t.confidence`/`raw_value` scaling so the host decoder shares one conversion). Total record = **40 B** — sets the small-queue slot size.
- `PERF_REC_TIMING` (type=3) — body 16 B: `uint8_t window_fill; uint8_t fifo_depth; uint8_t publish_mask; int8_t strum_dir; uint32_t reserved; uint64_t reserved`. Total **32 B**.
- `PERF_REC_DROP` (type=4) — body 16 B: `uint32_t dropped_state; uint32_t dropped_patch; uint64_t reserved`. Drain task emits 1 Hz.
- `PERF_REC_SESSION` (type=5) — body 16 B: `uint32_t timer_freq_hz; uint32_t schema_version; uint64_t fw_git_short`. Emitted once on perf-log start.

**Body (large queue):**
- `PERF_REC_PATCH` (type=6) — body 768 B: 16 B sub-header (per-fret offsets, sample coords) + 5 × 2 × 5 × 5 × 3 = 750 B + 2 B pad. Total record = **784 B**, fits 800 B slot.

**Slot sizes (final): small queue 40 B, large queue 800 B.**

**Wire framing (Phase A & B):** `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56` start-of-frame + `uint16_t length` + payload + `uint16_t CRC-16/CCITT` over length+payload. Mid-session connect resyncs by scanning for the magic and validating CRC. CRC-16 chosen for table-driven simplicity; ~5 cycles/byte is negligible at 11 KB/s.

**Schema versioning:** `PERF_REC_SESSION.schema_version = 1`; bump on any wire-format change. Decoder rejects unknown magic or unsupported `schema_version`.

## 3. Decoupled records-per-stage model — endorsed

Validated. Each producer emits its own typed record keyed by `frame_epoch`, host stitches. Reasons:

- **`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` means the same `frame_epoch` is touched across ~13 real-time frames.** Forcing a wide per-frame record requires either buffering 13 frames of partial state in firmware (unbounded) or emitting partial records with TBD markers (unparseable mid-stream). Decoupled records-per-stage with `frame_epoch` keys lets each producer fire at its natural moment with no rendezvous.
- **Matches existing bus mechanics** (§4.2.4): `detector_state_t` is already per-emit on `xDetectorStateQueue`. Same shape for the perf bus → consistent mental model.
- **Host-side join is trivial**: group by `frame_epoch`, sort by `ts_counter` within group, render Gantt-style.

Minor push-back: where two records are naturally co-produced (`PERF_REC_DETECTOR` and `PERF_REC_TIMING` both during `detect_frame` / `tp_handle_state`), emit them back-to-back from the same call site to amortise queue overhead. No structural change.

## 4. Drain-task duties

- **Sink fan-out.** Static array of `perf_log_sink_t` function-pointer + ctx pairs (max 4). Phase A registers DBGU UART; Phase B adds USB CDC device. Multiple sinks can be active simultaneously per §6 toggle model. Drain writes to each in sequence; each sink owns its backpressure.
- **Framing.** Drain wraps each dequeued record in start-of-frame + length + CRC before handing to sinks. Sinks see framed bytes only — keeps them dumb.
- **Backpressure.** Sink `write` is non-blocking and returns bytes-written. If a sink stalls, drain drops *for that sink* (per-sink drop counter) and moves on. Never blocks across sinks. UART sink uses a small TX ring (~2 KB) with non-blocking USART writes; CDC sink (Phase B) mirrors `fretboard_link.c`'s host-side write/semaphore pattern in the device direction.
- **Drop-on-full vs blocking write: drop, always.** The whole subsystem must be able to vanish without affecting the real-time pipeline.
- **Priority: `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2`.** Below detector/timing, above idle. Stack 2 KB static.

## 5. ISR producer details

Beyond the §1 façade:

- `on_frame_done` (`video.c:180`): emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=ISC_IRQ}` *before* the subscriber fan-out loop, and `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=VIDEO_PUBLISH}` *after*. Two `*FromISR` calls.
- `cdc_event_handler` (`fretboard_link.c:60`) `WRITE_COMPLETE` case: emit `PERF_REC_STAMP{stage=CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE}`. Existing `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` precedent confirms `*FromISR` is correct. **Critical: do not LOG_INFO from this handler** — that's the 2026-05-21 freeze pattern. Perf-log emit path uses no mutexes, by construction.
- Task-context producers (cv_marvin_v1, timing_pipeline, FretboardLink_Send) take the non-ISR branch (`xQueueSend(..., 0)`). Zero block.

**Keep parallel** — do not bundle into Phase A. Reasons:
1. `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` needs a *second* TC channel for the stats counter; TC0 CH0 is owned by SYS_TIME and we shouldn't reuse it without a re-architecture pass.
2. Analytics output (`vTaskGetRunTimeStats` text dump) is fundamentally a different consumer from binary perf records.

**Cheap freebie**: emit a periodic `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` (10 s cadence) calling `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` for each known task — no FreeRTOS config flag needed, addresses the freeze-misdiagnosis lesson from 2026-05-21. Add as Phase A stretch, not blocker.

- **(b)** Reconfigure one UHPHS port as Dual-Role / OTG (only viable if the SAM9X75 supports DRD on UHPHS — datasheet check required).

**Action: confirm UDPHS pad availability on the SAM9X75 board before any Phase B implementation work.** If unavailable, fallbacks are (i) Ethernet (5 MB/s per the journal's bandwidth table), (ii) ship state-only over UART forever and defer patches to the SD recording path. **Phase B is gated on this hardware question.**
