# Marvin perf-log subsystem

## Context

The marvin firmware now has the first end-to-end CV-detector → timing-pipeline → fretboard-actuator path running (M1 + M2 + M3 mostly done; see `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` and `spec.md`). With the pipeline live, performance tuning needs data: where the milliseconds go between an HDMI frame arriving and a strum reaching the wire, whether the system actually holds 60 Hz, and what the detector internals (`hold_dist`, `edge_dist`, pressed flags) look like over the course of a song. Today the only visibility is a commented-out 2 Hz `printf` block in [cv_marvin_v1.c:336-351](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L336-L351); the 2026-05-21 threshold-tuning session was driven by reading those values by eye.

This subsystem builds a structured per-frame log of latency stamps + detector internals + timing-pipeline state + (Tier 2) ROI pixel patches, streamed off-device over a new USB-device CDC ACM channel for both live tail and post-session capture. The ~52 KB/s peak (with patches) is well within USB HS CDC headroom (~5–15 MB/s sustained per the bandwidth scoping in the 2026-05-21 journal entry).

Scope per the conversation: **single phase, USB-device-CDC only**. The existing console UART (FLEXCOM4 at 115.2 kBd) stays untouched as the log/debug/future-command channel — perf-log doesn't share it. SD-sink is explicitly out of scope (deferred to milestone M4 recording bring-up; SDMMC + SYS_FS are greenfield).

## Architecture

### Producer model — decoupled records keyed by `frame_epoch`

Each producer emits its own typed record at its natural call site, keyed by `frame_epoch` (sourced from `Video_FrameInfo.frame_count` per the existing M1 convention). Host-side joins by `frame_epoch` and sorts by `ts_counter` within group.

This shape matches the multi-frame coupling the pipeline already has: `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` means detection frame N's wire-out happens ~13 real-time frames later. A single per-frame record would have to either buffer 13 frames of partial state (unbounded) or emit partial records (unparseable mid-stream). Decoupled-by-stage avoids both.

### Two-queue ring strategy

- **`s_state_q`** — MPSC, **40 B slots**, depth **128** (~2 frames headroom: 7 producers × ~14 records/frame). Static BSS: ~5 KB.
- **`s_patch_q`** — MPSC, **800 B slots**, depth **8**. Static BSS: ~6.4 KB. Always allocated (Tier 2 patches are in scope from day one).

Why two: small/large record-size ratio is ~30×; a union-sized single queue forces 800 B slots on every record. Drain task multiplexes both queues with `xQueueSelectFromSet` (static queue set).

All seven producers go through one façade — `PerfLog_Emit*` internally branches on `xPortIsInsideInterrupt()` to pick `xQueueSendFromISR` vs `xQueueSend(..., 0)`. Both with **zero block time. Drop on full, never block.** Per-queue drop counters incremented atomically (`__atomic_add_fetch`); drain task emits a `PERF_REC_DROP` once per second.

### μs-resolution timestamp source

**`SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` reading the underlying TC0 CH0 counter.** The driver is already initialized; one register read of `TC0_REGS->TC_CHANNEL[0].TC_CV` is ISR-safe and atomic. ~3.75 ns/tick at 266 MHz (host divides raw counter by `SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet()` reported in `PERF_REC_SESSION`). 32-bit counter wraps every ~16 s — drain task observes wraps and emits a wrap marker.

**Do not reuse** the `xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK = 1000` pattern at [cv_marvin_v1.c:156](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L156) — it's millisecond resolution masquerading as μs and is useless for sub-frame attribution.

### Drain task

- Priority: `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` (below detector + timing, above idle). Stack 2 KB static.
- Wraps each dequeued record in framing (start-of-frame magic `55 4D 52 56` + `uint16_t length` + payload + CRC-16/CCITT). Mid-session reader resyncs by scanning for magic + validating CRC.
- Single sink: USB device CDC. Non-blocking write; if CDC stalls, increment a sink-drop counter and drop. Real-time pipeline must remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.

## Record schema

Fixed-width little-endian, naturally aligned. Common 16 B header on every record:

\```
uint16_t magic;        // 0x4D56 ("MV")
uint8_t  type;         // PERF_REC_*
uint8_t  flags;        // bit 0 = from_isr
uint32_t frame_epoch;  // from Video_FrameInfo.frame_count
uint64_t ts_counter;   // raw SYS_TIME counter
\```

Bodies (small queue, total record size ≤ 40 B):

- **`PERF_REC_STAMP`** (16 B body) — `stage_id` ∈ {ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE}, `aux` u32 (e.g. publish_mask, FIFO depth). Total **32 B**.
- **`PERF_REC_DETECTOR`** (24 B body) — 5 × (`uint16_t hold_dist`, `uint16_t edge_dist`) + `pressed_mask` + `edge_active_mask` + 2 B pad. Reuses the `detector_state_t.confidence` / `raw_value` 16-bit scaling so host decoder shares one float-conversion path. Total **40 B** (sets the slot size).
- **`PERF_REC_TIMING`** (16 B body) — chord-window fill, FIFO depth, last publish_mask, strum direction. Total **32 B**.
- **`PERF_REC_DROP`** (16 B body) — `dropped_state`, `dropped_patch`, `dropped_sink`. Drain emits 1 Hz.
- **`PERF_REC_SESSION`** (16 B body) — `timer_freq_hz`, `schema_version=1`, `fw_git_short`. Once on start.
- **`PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER`** (variable, but ≤ 24 B) — periodic stack high-water dump, 10 s cadence. Phase 1 stretch; addresses the 2026-05-21 freeze-misdiagnosis lesson without enabling FreeRTOS runtime stats.

Body (large queue):

- **`PERF_REC_PATCH`** (768 B body) — 16 B sub-header (per-fret sample coords) + 5 frets × 2 patches (hold + edge) × 5×5 BGR = 750 B + 2 B pad. Total **784 B** in 800 B slot.

## Module file layout

New (matches existing tree pattern under `firmware/marvin/default/src/`):

- `perf_log/perf_log.h` — public API: `PerfLog_Init`, `PerfLog_Start`, `PerfLog_EmitStamp`, `PerfLog_EmitDetector`, `PerfLog_EmitTiming`, `PerfLog_EmitPatch`. Safe in task or ISR context.
- `perf_log/perf_log.c` — queues, drain task, façade, framing, CRC-16/CCITT, drop counters.
- `perf_log/perf_log_records.h` — wire-format structs and enums. Mirrored verbatim into the host decoder at schema bumps.
- `perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — USB device CDC ACM sink. Non-blocking write. Mirrors [fretboard_link.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c)'s host-side write/`xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` pattern in the device direction.

Producer call sites get one or two lines added each:

- [video.c:180](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c#L180) — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(ISC_IRQ, ...)` at ISR entry.
- [video.c:213](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c#L213) — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(VIDEO_PUBLISH, ...)` after subscriber fan-out.
- [cv_marvin_v1.c:325](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L325) — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(CV_START)` after `xQueueReceive` returns.
- [cv_marvin_v1.c:199](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L199) — `PerfLog_EmitDetector(...)` + `PerfLog_EmitStamp(CV_END)` next to bus publish. Replaces the commented-out 2 Hz dump at [336-351](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L336-L351).
- `cv_marvin_v1.c` patch-sample loop — `PerfLog_EmitPatch(...)` after the 5×5 BGR samples are taken (Tier 2; reuses already-sampled patches, no new I/O).
- [timing_pipeline.c:142](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L142) — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(TP_TICK, mask)` + `PerfLog_EmitTiming(...)` next to `FretboardLink_Send`.
- [fretboard_link.c:262](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L262) — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(FBL_SEND)` in `FretboardLink_Send`.
- [fretboard_link.c:60](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L60) WRITE_COMPLETE case — `PerfLog_EmitStamp(CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE)`. **Critical:** no `LOG_INFO` from this ISR (2026-05-21 freeze pattern); perf-log emit path uses no mutexes by construction.

`cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` additions: `src/perf_log/perf_log.c` and `src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c`.

`app.c` additions: `PerfLog_Initialize()` from `APP_Initialize` after `Video_Initialize`; `PerfLog_Start()` after the scheduler is up.

Host-side decoder (parallel deliverable):

- `tools/perf-log-decoder/` — Python (matches `tools/fret-tuner/`). Reads framed binary from a serial-emulated USB CDC, validates CRC, demuxes by record type, joins by `frame_epoch`. Emits CSV for spreadsheet inspection and a Gantt-style HTML report for visual latency attribution. `perf_log_records.py` mirrors `perf_log_records.h` (single source of truth in C; Python derived by hand at schema bumps).

## Implementation order

1. **MCC regen**: enable USB device peripheral (UDPHS) + USB device CDC ACM class. Pick UDPHS pad/connector (user has confirmed availability — pin assignment to be locked in at start of work). Add the resulting MCC modifications (if any) to the re-apply list in `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` "Open questions" §MCC-file modifications.
2. **Land the empty perf_log/ module**: queues, drain-task skeleton, façade, framing, CRC, no producers wired, CDC sink stub. `PerfLog_Init` from `APP_Initialize`; `PerfLog_Start` after scheduler. Goal: a `PERF_REC_SESSION` record reaches the host decoder.
3. **Wire the CDC device sink** for real. Validate sustained 54 KB/s with synthetic record stream. Mirrors fretboard_link's write/semaphore pattern in the device direction.
4. **Wire ISR producers** (video.c × 2, fretboard_link.c CDC complete). Smoke-test by hammering the actuator path with manual-control input while perf-log is live — must not freeze (regression check on 2026-05-21).
5. **Wire task-context producers** (cv_marvin_v1 start/end + detector record, timing_pipeline tick + timing record, FretboardLink_Send).
6. **Build the host-side decoder** (`tools/perf-log-decoder/`): CSV output, Gantt HTML.
7. **Wire patch emission** in `cv_marvin_v1.detect_frame` after the existing 5×5 sample loop.
8. **Stretch:** periodic `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` (10 s cadence) calling `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` for each known task.
9. **Update journal**: session-log entry summarising perf-log landing + any new findings (e.g. measured latencies); add a decision-log entry pinning the schema version + UDPHS pad choice; remove the FreeRTOS-analytics carry-forward note if `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` covers the stack-HWM half.

## Verification

End-to-end test:

1. Flash. Start a Wii session, gameplay through one Easy-mode song.
2. Connect host decoder to the new USB CDC device port, capture full-session binary stream.
3. Decode to CSV + Gantt HTML.
4. Check structural invariants:
   - `dropped_state` ≈ 0 over a 5-minute capture (non-zero ⇒ raise drain task priority by 1 and retest).
   - `dropped_patch` ≈ 0 at steady state.
   - Every `PERF_REC_STAMP{ISC_IRQ}` for `frame_epoch=N` is followed within ~1 frame (≤ 16.7 ms) by a matching `VIDEO_PUBLISH`, `CV_START`, `CV_END`, and `TP_TICK`.
   - Every `frame_epoch=N` that produced a chord eventually gets a matching `FBL_SEND` and `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` at ≈ 220 ms (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS`) later.
5. Check semantic invariants:
   - Detector hold/edge values in `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` line up with the values logged by the existing 2 Hz dump when re-enabled in parallel (cross-validation).
   - Patches in `PERF_REC_PATCH` visually match the on-screen overlay rings drawn by `cv_marvin_v1`.
6. Regression: with manual-control surface live and perf-log running, hammer fret/strum touches; verify no system freeze and no `cdc_event_handler` reentrancy issues.

## Critical files

- `firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c` — ISR producers at [180, 213](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c#L180-L213).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c` — task producers at [199, 325](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c); detector internals (`s_hold_dist`, `s_edge_dist`, `s_pressed`, `s_edge_active`); patch sample loop.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c` — task producer near [142](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L142) (`publish_mask`) and the bus-receive site (~line 300+).

- `firmware/marvin/default/src/log.c` — **reference only, do not reuse**: takes a mutex with `portMAX_DELAY` ⇒ ISR-illegal.
- `firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` — add new module sources.
- `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — session/decision log updates.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` and `configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY` both `0` today; **leave them alone** (parallel work).

## Risks / open questions

1. **UDPHS pin/connector assignment.** User confirmed pads are available; the specific pad set and physical connector need to be pinned down at start of work before MCC regen. New entry on the MCC re-apply list is likely.
2. **`SYS_TIME_CounterGet` ISR safety on this build.** Strongly believed safe (single register read), but worth a 5-line confirmation test (read counter from a high-priority ISR vs task-side, cross-check) before all seven producers depend on it.

```
Bodies (small queue, total record size ≤ 40 B):

- **`PERF_REC_STAMP`** (16 B body) — `stage_id` ∈ {ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE}, `aux` u32 (e.g. publish_mask, FIFO depth). Total **32 B**.
- **`PERF_REC_DETECTOR`** (24 B body) — 5 × (`uint16_t hold_dist`, `uint16_t edge_dist`) + `pressed_mask` + `edge_active_mask` + 2 B pad. Reuses the `detector_state_t.confidence` / `raw_value` 16-bit scaling so host decoder shares one float-conversion path. Total **40 B** (sets the slot size).
- **`PERF_REC_TIMING`** (16 B body) — chord-window fill, FIFO depth, last publish_mask, strum direction. Total **32 B**.
- **`PERF_REC_DROP`** (16 B body) — `dropped_state`, `dropped_patch`, `dropped_sink`. Drain emits 1 Hz.
- **`PERF_REC_SESSION`** (16 B body) — `timer_freq_hz`, `schema_version=1`, `fw_git_short`. Once on start.
- **`PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER`** (variable, but ≤ 24 B) — periodic stack high-water dump, 10 s cadence. Phase 1 stretch; addresses the 2026-05-21 freeze-misdiagnosis lesson without enabling FreeRTOS runtime stats.

Body (large queue):

- **`PERF_REC_PATCH`** (768 B body) — 16 B sub-header (per-fret sample coords) + 5 frets × 2 patches (hold + edge) × 5×5 BGR = 750 B + 2 B pad. Total **784 B** in 800 B slot.

## Module file layout

New (matches existing tree pattern under `firmware/marvin/default/src/`):

- `perf_log/perf_log.h` — public API: `PerfLog_Init`, `PerfLog_Start`, `PerfLog_EmitStamp`, `PerfLog_EmitDetector`, `PerfLog_EmitTiming`, `PerfLog_EmitPatch`. Safe in task or ISR context.
- `perf_log/perf_log.c` — queues, drain task, façade, framing, CRC-16/CCITT, drop counters.
- `perf_log/perf_log_records.h` — wire-format structs and enums. Mirrored verbatim into the host decoder at schema bumps.
- `perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — USB device CDC ACM sink. Non-blocking write. Mirrors [fretboard_link.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c)'s host-side write/`xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` pattern in the device direction.

Producer call sites get one or two lines added each:

Emits CSV for spreadsheet inspection and a Gantt-style HTML report for visual latency attribution. `perf_log_records.py` mirrors `perf_log_records.h` (single source of truth in C; Python derived by hand at schema bumps).

## Implementation order

1. **MCC regen**: enable USB device peripheral (UDPHS) + USB device CDC ACM class. Pick UDPHS pad/connector (user has confirmed availability — pin assignment to be locked in at start of work). Add the resulting MCC modifications (if any) to the re-apply list in `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` "Open questions" §MCC-file modifications.
2. **Land the empty perf_log/ module**: queues, drain-task skeleton, façade, framing, CRC, no producers wired, CDC sink stub. `PerfLog_Init` from `APP_Initialize`; `PerfLog_Start` after scheduler. Goal: a `PERF_REC_SESSION` record reaches the host decoder.
3. **Wire the CDC device sink** for real. Validate sustained 54 KB/s with synthetic record stream. Mirrors fretboard_link's write/semaphore pattern in the device direction.
4. **Wire ISR producers** (video.c × 2, fretboard_link.c CDC complete). Smoke-test by hammering the actuator path with manual-control input while perf-log is live — must not freeze (regression check on 2026-05-21).
5. **Wire task-context producers** (cv_marvin_v1 start/end + detector record, timing_pipeline tick + timing record, FretboardLink_Send).
6. **Build the host-side decoder** (`tools/perf-log-decoder/`): CSV output, Gantt HTML.
7. **Wire patch emission** in `cv_marvin_v1.detect_frame` after the existing 5×5 sample loop.
8. **Stretch:** periodic `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` (10 s cadence) calling `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` for each known task.
9. **Update journal**: session-log entry summarising perf-log landing + any new findings (e.g. measured latencies); add a decision-log entry pinning the schema version + UDPHS pad choice; remove the FreeRTOS-analytics carry-forward note if `PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER` covers the stack-HWM half.

## Verification

End-to-end test:

1. Flash. Start a Wii session, gameplay through one Easy-mode song.
2. Connect host decoder to the new USB CDC device port, capture full-session binary stream.
3. Decode to CSV + Gantt HTML.
4. Check structural invariants:
   - `dropped_state` ≈ 0 over a 5-minute capture (non-zero ⇒ raise drain task priority by 1 and retest).
   - `dropped_patch` ≈ 0 at steady state.
   - Every `PERF_REC_STAMP{ISC_IRQ}` for `frame_epoch=N` is followed within ~1 frame (≤ 16.7 ms) by a matching `VIDEO_PUBLISH`, `CV_START`, `CV_END`, and `TP_TICK`.
   - Every `frame_epoch=N` that produced a chord eventually gets a matching `FBL_SEND` and `CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE` at ≈ 220 ms (`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS`) later.
5. Check semantic invariants:
   - Detector hold/edge values in `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` line up with the values logged by the existing 2 Hz dump when re-enabled in parallel (cross-validation).
   - Patches in `PERF_REC_PATCH` visually match the on-screen overlay rings drawn by `cv_marvin_v1`.
6. Regression: with manual-control surface live and perf-log running, hammer fret/strum touches; verify no system freeze and no `cdc_event_handler` reentrancy issues.

## Risks / open questions

1. **UDPHS pin/connector assignment.** User confirmed pads are available; the specific pad set and physical connector need to be pinned down at start of work before MCC regen. New entry on the MCC re-apply list is likely.
2. **`SYS_TIME_CounterGet` ISR safety on this build.** Strongly believed safe (single register read), but worth a 5-line confirmation test (read counter from a high-priority ISR vs task-side, cross-check) before all seven producers depend on it.
3. **Fixed-point conversion of detector floats.** Plan reuses the existing `detector_state_t.confidence` / `raw_value` 16-bit scaling. Confirm this scaling captures the dynamic range observed during 2026-05-21 tuning (hold ranges 22–186; edge ranges ~0–53).
4. **Drain-task starvation.** Acceptance test in §verification step 4 catches it; mitigation is +1 priority bump.
5. **`frame_epoch` 32-bit rollover at ~830 days.** M5's persistent counter will fix at the source; host decoder must handle the wrap if a session straddles. Document.
6. **CDC bring-up surprises.** Host-side CDC bring-up was non-trivial (VBUS quirks, EDBG protocol relaxation, ISR-context logging freeze — all in 2026-05-20/21 journal). Device side will have its own; budget for it.
```

```text
11	 * publishing at 60 Hz and the stub consumer draining every tick, depth 8
12	 * absorbs a few ms of consumer stall without dropping records. Bump when
13	 * adding more producers or a slower consumer. */
14	#define DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH       8u
15	
16	#define DRAIN_TASK_STACK_WORDS   512u
17	#define DRAIN_TASK_PRIORITY      1u
18	#define DRAIN_LOG_INTERVAL_MS    1000u
19	
20	static QueueHandle_t   s_bus_queue;
21	static StaticQueue_t   s_bus_queue_buf;
22	static uint8_t         s_bus_queue_storage[DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH * sizeof(detector_state_t)];
23	
24	static StackType_t     s_drain_stack[DRAIN_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
25	static StaticTask_t    s_drain_tcb;
26	
27	static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask;
28	static volatile uint8_t  s_active_id = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
29	
30	static void drain_task(void *param)
31	{
32	    (void)param;
33	
34	    TickType_t window_start = xTaskGetTickCount();
35	    uint32_t   window_count = 0;
36	
37	    for (;;)
38	    {
39	        detector_state_t state;
40	        if (xQueueReceive(s_bus_queue, &state, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE)
41	        {
42	            continue;
43	        }
44	        window_count++;
45	
46	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
47	        if ((uint32_t)(now - window_start) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(DRAIN_LOG_INTERVAL_MS))
48	        {
49	            LOG_INFO("DETECTOR: bus drain %lu records/s (last epoch=%lu id=%u)\r\n",
50	                     (unsigned long)window_count,
51	                     (unsigned long)state.frame_epoch,
52	                     (unsigned)state.detector_id);
53	            window_start = now;
54	            window_count = 0;
55	        }
56	    }
57	}
58	
59	void Detector_Initialize(void)
60	{
61	    s_bus_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH,
62	                                     sizeof(detector_state_t),
63	                                     s_bus_queue_storage,
64	                                     &s_bus_queue_buf);
65	    configASSERT(s_bus_queue != NULL);
66	
67	    CvMarvinV1_Initialize();
68	
69	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(drain_task,
70	                            "DetectorDrain",
71	                            DRAIN_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
72	                            NULL,
73	                            DRAIN_TASK_PRIORITY,
74	                            s_drain_stack,
75	                            &s_drain_tcb);
76	}

81	}

83	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id)
84	{
85	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
86	    s_enabled_mask |= (1u << (uint32_t)id);

88	}
```

```text
12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)
70	 * acts on. Only one active at a time, irrespective of how many are
71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
74	detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
75	
76	#endif
```

```text
94	     * IRQ overwrites it. */
95	    uint32_t initial_addr = s_latest_buffer;
96	    if (initial_addr == 0u) { initial_addr = ISC_Capture_GetBufferAddress(); }
97	
98	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
99	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO,
100	                               XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
101	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, initial_addr, false);
102	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, 0u, false);
103	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
104	
105	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3) and source-memory rect (HEOCFG4) are the same
106	     * for 1:1 and differ for scaling. Write them directly — XLCDC_Set-
107	     * LayerWindowXYSize writes both registers to the same value, which is
108	     * only correct for 1:1. */
109	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u)
110	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
111	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(src_w - 1u)
112	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(src_h - 1u);
113	
114	    bool scaling = (dst_w != src_w) || (dst_h != src_h);
115	    if (scaling)
116	    {
117	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(src_w, dst_w);
118	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(src_h, dst_h);
119	
120	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1)
121	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)
122	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(1)
123	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(1);
124	        /* Bicubic luminance + bicubic chrominance, both planes. Mirrors
125	         * MCC's surface-set path — best image quality for video. */
126	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG30 = LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYCFG(1)
127	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYBICU(1)
128	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCCFG(1)
129	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCBICU(1);
130	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG31 = LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYCFG(1)
131	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYBICU(1)
132	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCCFG(1)
133	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCBICU(1);
134	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG24 = LCDC_HEOCFG24_VXSYFACT(vf);
135	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG25 = LCDC_HEOCFG25_VXSCFACT(vf);
136	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG26 = LCDC_HEOCFG26_HXSYFACT(hf);
137	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG27 = LCDC_HEOCFG27_HXSCFACT(hf);
138	    }
139	    else
140	    {
141	        /* Disable scaler — matches MCC's HEO-setup defaults. */
142	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(0)
143	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(0)
144	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0)
145	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);
146	    }
147	
148	    /* §44.6.4.7 — discard BASE DMA in the destination rect. HEO with MCC's
149	     * default SFACTC=4 (A0×As) / DFACTC=6 (1−A0×As) reaches 100% opacity
150	     * for RGB_888_PACKED (no per-pixel alpha → As sourced from A0=255),
151	     * so BASE pixels in this rect are blended out. DISCEN tells the BASE
152	     * channel to skip fetching them. */
153	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG5 = LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCXPOS(x)
154	                              | LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCYPOS(y);
155	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG6 = LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCXSIZE(dst_w - 1u)
156	                              | LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCYSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
157	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 |= LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
158	
159	    /* HEO and BASE attribute updates triggered together. */
160	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, true, true);
161	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
162	
163	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: HEO bound src %lux%lu → dst %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) %s\r\n",
164	             (unsigned long)src_w, (unsigned long)src_h,
165	             (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
166	             (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y,
167	             scaling ? "scaled" : "1:1");
168	}
169	
170	/* Hide HEO and let BASE (Legato UI) fill the whole panel. */
171	static void lcd_unbind(void)
172	{
173	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
174	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 &= ~LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
175	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
176	}
177	
178	/* ─── Frame-done ISR (runs in IRQ context) ─────────────────────────────── */
179	
180	static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
181	                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
182	                          uintptr_t ctx)
183	{
184	    (void)ctx;
185	
186	    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;
187	
188	    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
189	     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
190	     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
191	     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
192	     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
193	    if (s_display_bound)
194	    {
195	        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
196	    }
197	
198	    Video_FrameInfo info =
199	    {
200	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
201	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
202	        .width           = s_src_w,
203	        .height          = s_src_h,
204	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
205	    };
206	
207	    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
208	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
209	    {
210	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
211	        if (q != NULL)
212	        {
213	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
214	        }
215	    }
216	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
217	}
218	
219	/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
220	
221	static bool capture_arm(void)
222	{
223	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
224	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
225	
226	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
227	    s_src_w = w;
228	    s_src_h = h;
229	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
230	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
231	    {
232	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
233	        return false;
234	    }
235	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
236	    return true;
237	}
238	
239	static void capture_disarm(void)
240	{
241	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
242	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
243	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
244	}
245	
246	/* Bind/unbind display from current intent + most-recent source size +
247	 * caller-set window. A zero-sized window means the app hasn't set one
248	 * yet — silently skip the bind in that case rather than emit a malformed
249	 * HEO geometry; DisplayShow without a prior SetWindow is a no-op. */
250	static void display_apply(void)
251	{
252	    window_t w = s_window;
253	    bool window_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
254	    bool source_valid = (s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u);
255	    bool want = s_display_shown && source_valid && window_valid;
256	
257	    if (want && !s_display_bound)
258	    {
259	        lcd_bind(s_src_w, s_src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
260	        s_display_bound = true;
261	    }
262	    else if (!want && s_display_bound)
263	    {
264	        lcd_unbind();
265	        s_display_bound = false;
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* Each tick: align current chain state (capture armed / display bound) to
270	 * the user's intent flags, given the current source-lock state. */
271	static void reconcile(void)
272	{
273	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
274	
275	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
276	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
277	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
278	    {
279	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
280	    }
281	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
282	    {
283	        capture_disarm();
284	        s_capture_armed = false;
285	    }
286	
287	    /* Display: shown iff intent + we have a source size to work with. The
288	     * source size is captured at arm time and persists across capture
289	     * teardown so the user can leave HEO bound on a stale frame. */
290	    display_apply();
291	}
292	
293	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
294	
295	static void video_task(void *param)
296	{
297	    (void)param;
298	
299	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
300	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge,
301	     * backlight, and parks the panel in UI-only mode. */
302	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
303	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
304	    TC358743_Initialize();
305	    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
306	    lcd_unbind();
307	
308	    for (;;)
309	    {
310	        TC358743_Tasks();
311	        reconcile();
312	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
313	    }
314	}
315	
316	/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
317	
318	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
319	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
320	
321	void Video_Initialize(void)
322	{
323	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
324	                            "VideoTask",
325	                            VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
326	                            NULL,
327	                            VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
328	                            s_task_stack,
329	                            &s_task_tcb);
330	}
331	
332	void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
333	void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
334	
335	void Video_DisplayShow(void)    { s_display_shown = true;    }
336	void Video_DisplayHide(void)    { s_display_shown = false;   }
337	
338	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
339	{
340	    window_t w = { x, y, dst_w, dst_h };
341	    s_window = w;
342	    /* Force a re-bind on next reconcile if we're currently shown. */
343	    s_display_bound = false;
344	}
345	
346	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
347	{
348	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
349	
350	    bool ok = false;
351	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
352	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
353	    {
354	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q) { ok = true; break; }     /* already in */
355	        if (s_subscribers[i] == NULL)
356	        {
357	            s_subscribers[i] = q;
358	            ok = true;
359	            break;
360	        }
361	    }
362	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
363	
364	    if (!ok) { LOG_ERROR("VIDEO: subscriber table full (max %u)\r\n",
365	                         (unsigned)VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS); }
366	    return ok;
367	}
368	
369	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
370	{
371	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
372	
373	    bool ok = false;
374	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
375	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
376	    {
377	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q)
378	        {
379	            s_subscribers[i] = NULL;
380	            ok = true;
381	            break;
382	        }
383	    }
384	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
385	    return ok;
386	}
387	
388	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)
389	{
390	    if (info == NULL) { return; }
391	    info->buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
392	    info->frame_count     = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
393	    info->width           = s_src_w;
394	    info->height          = s_src_h;
395	    info->bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
396	}
```

```text
10	/* Video pipeline: HDMI source → TC358743 bridge → CSI-2 → CSI2DC → ISC →
11	 * DDR → XLCDC HEO. The module owns its own FreeRTOS task; everything below
12	 * (tc358743, isc_capture, HEO bind/unbind, capture/display state machine)
13	 * runs inside that task except the frame-arrival notification which fires
14	 * from the ISC IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR.
15	 *
16	 * Capture and display are independent. CaptureEnable arms the bridge +
17	 * ISC chain when the source is locked; DisplayShow makes the HEO layer
18	 * visible at the configured window. You can run capture without display
19	 * (frames flow into DDR, BASE/UI fills the panel) or display without
20	 * capture (HEO shows whatever is in the framebuffer — possibly stale).
21	 *
22	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, display hidden, window
23	 * unset. Layout is app policy — DisplayShow is a no-op until the
24	 * caller has set a window with Video_SetWindow. */
25	
26	void Video_Initialize(void);
27	
28	/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
29	 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
30	 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
31	void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
32	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);
33	
34	/* Display layer control. SHOW: HEO visible, BASE DISCEN cleared under
35	 * the HEO rect (saves DDR read bandwidth). HIDE: HEO disabled, BASE
36	 * owns full panel. Independent of capture state. */
37	void Video_DisplayShow(void);
38	void Video_DisplayHide(void);
39	
40	/* Destination rect on the 1280×800 panel. dst_w/dst_h matching the
41	 * source frame size → 1:1, scaler bypassed. Otherwise HEO bilinear
42	 * scaler engages and stretches to fill the rect. The rect must fit
43	 * within the panel. Takes effect on the next display bind (next
44	 * DisplayShow call, or when capture/lock state changes). */
45	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h);
46	
47	/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
48	typedef struct
49	{
50	    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
51	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
52	    uint16_t width;
53	    uint16_t height;
54	    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
55	} Video_FrameInfo;
56	
57	/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
58	 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
59	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
60	 * queue. Create the queue with:
61	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
62	 *
63	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
64	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
65	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
66	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
67	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
68	 * independently.
69	 *
70	 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
71	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
72	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
73	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
74	 * second-next frame.
75	 *
76	 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
77	 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
78	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
79	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
80	
81	/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
82	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
83	
84	/* Synchronous read of the current frame state. Doesn't block. May
85	 * report frame_count = 0 / buffer = NULL if capture has never armed. */
86	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info);
87	
88	#endif
```

```text
5	
6	/* Lightweight logging shim. Goes through libc printf → xc32_monitor →
7	 * DBGU. Adds a runtime severity filter and FreeRTOS-aware locking.
8	 *
9	 * Pre-scheduler calls work too — the mutex is taken only when the
10	 * scheduler is running, so log_printf is safe to call from
11	 * APP_Initialize / SYS_Initialize.
12	 *
13	 * Do NOT call from an ISR — use a different mechanism for ISR-side
14	 * diagnostics (queue to a task, or atomic counter polled by a task).
15	 */
16	
17	typedef enum
18	{
19	    LOG_LEVEL_ERROR = 0,
20	    LOG_LEVEL_WARN  = 1,
21	    LOG_LEVEL_INFO  = 2,
22	    LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG = 3,
23	} log_level_t;
24	
25	/* Set up the FreeRTOS mutex. Safe to call before vTaskStartScheduler.
26	 * Pass the initial filter level. */
27	void log_init(log_level_t initial_level);
28	
29	void        log_set_level(log_level_t lvl);
30	log_level_t log_get_level(void);
31	
32	void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
33	void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
34	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
35	
36	/* Convenience macros — match a typical embedded log API. */
37	#define LOG_ERROR(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, __VA_ARGS__)
38	#define LOG_WARN(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_WARN,  __VA_ARGS__)
39	#define LOG_INFO(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_INFO,  __VA_ARGS__)
40	#define LOG_DEBUG(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG, __VA_ARGS__)
41	
42	#endif
```

```text
1	#include "log.h"
2	
3	#include <stdarg.h>
4	#include <stdbool.h>
5	#include <stdio.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "semphr.h"
9	#include "task.h"
10	
11	static volatile log_level_t s_level = LOG_LEVEL_INFO;
12	static SemaphoreHandle_t    s_mutex;
13	static StaticSemaphore_t    s_mutex_buf;
14	
15	void log_init(log_level_t initial_level)
16	{
17	    s_level = initial_level;
18	    /* Safe before vTaskStartScheduler; only Take/Give require the
19	     * scheduler to be running. */
20	    s_mutex = xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic(&s_mutex_buf);
21	}
22	
23	void log_set_level(log_level_t lvl)
24	{
25	    s_level = lvl;
26	}
27	
28	log_level_t log_get_level(void)
29	{
30	    return s_level;
31	}
32	
33	void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap)
34	{
35	    if ((int)lvl > (int)s_level) { return; }
36	
37	    /* Take the mutex only when the scheduler is running and the mutex
38	     * was created. Pre-scheduler we're single-threaded so interleaving
39	     * isn't possible; xSemaphoreTake with portMAX_DELAY would hang
40	     * before vTaskStartScheduler. */
41	    bool locked = false;
42	    if (s_mutex != NULL
43	        && xTaskGetSchedulerState() == taskSCHEDULER_RUNNING)
44	    {
45	        if (xSemaphoreTake(s_mutex, portMAX_DELAY) == pdTRUE)
46	        {
47	            locked = true;
48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    (void)vprintf(fmt, ap);
52	
53	    if (locked)
54	    {
55	        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_mutex);
56	    }
57	}
58	
59	void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
60	{
61	    va_list ap;
62	    va_start(ap, fmt);
63	    log_vprintf(lvl, fmt, ap);
64	    va_end(ap);
65	}
```

```text
85	                                                         void *eventData,

87	{
88	    (void)eventData;
89	    (void)context;

91	    return USB_HOST_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;

104

108	
109	void APP_Initialize ( void )
110	{
111	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
112	
113	    /* Logging shim: thin wrapper over libc printf with severity filter
114	     * and FreeRTOS-aware locking. Initialized first so subsequent code
115	     * (including video task startup) can use LOG_*. Default level is
116	     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
117	    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);
118	
119	    /* Spawn the video task. xTaskCreate is safe before vTaskStartScheduler;
120	     * the task runs once the scheduler picks it up. The video module owns
121	     * its capture-pipeline init (ISC, TC358743, backlight, HEO unbind),
122	     * the capture/display state machine, and the bridge-status polling. */
123	    Video_Initialize();
124	
125	    /* App-side video layout: 720×480 video at (280, 76) on the 1280×800
126	     * panel — 1:1 with the bridge's typical 480p source, leaves a UI
127	     * strip below. Set before DisplayShow; the video module has no
128	     * default window of its own. */
129	    Video_SetWindow(280u, 76u, 720u, 480u);
130	
131	    /* Default: arm the capture chain when source locks, and show video. */
132	    Video_CaptureEnable();
133	    Video_DisplayShow();
134	
135	    /* Reference detector (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. M1 stub
136	     * publisher; real detection logic lands incrementally. Must follow
137	     * Video_Initialize since cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to the video frame
138	     * queue from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; explicitly
139	     * enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline. */
140	    Detector_Initialize();
141	    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
142	    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
143	
144	    /* USB host bring-up — shared across all USB consumers (fretboard CDC
145	     * link today; future modules may add HID, MSC, etc.). VBUS_AH_PC27/PC31
146	     * gate external power switches on the SAM9X75 Curiosity. The Harmony
147	     * driver's portPowerEnable callback is wired but never invoked, so we
148	     * assert these GPIOs directly. Class-driver attach listeners (CDC etc.)
149	     * must be registered before USB_HOST_BusEnable, so consumer module
150	     * init runs first. */
151	    VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set();
152	    VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set();
153	    (void)USB_HOST_EventHandlerSet(app_usb_host_event_handler, 0u);
154	
155	    /* M2 actuator path: fretboard_link owns the submit queue + USB CDC
156	     * writer and registers the CDC attach listener. */
157	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
158	
159	    USB_HOST_RESULT be = USB_HOST_BusEnable(USB_HOST_BUS_ALL);
160	    LOG_INFO("USB_HOST_BusEnable -> %d\r\n", (int)be);
161	
162	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
163	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
164	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
165	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();
166	
167	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation
168	     * (game-menu navigation, manual test). UI buttons are authored in
169	     * Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated screenShow_Screen0
170	     * registers the event_Screen0_Button_Manual_* callbacks defined in
171	     * ui/manual_input.c, so no explicit bind step is needed here. */
172	    ManualControl_Initialize();
173	}

179	
180	  Remarks:
181	    See prototype in app.h.
182	 */
183	
184	void APP_Tasks ( void )
185	{
186	    /* APP is a one-shot launcher — task creation happened in APP_Initialize.
187	     * Self-delete here so the (1024-word) stack and TCB are released to the
188	     * idle task. The MCC-generated lAPP_Tasks loop will not iterate again
189	     * because vTaskDelete(NULL) never returns to its caller. */
190	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
```

```text
25	/* Hold sensor (brightness): rising edge above CV_HOLD_THRESH; releases
26	 * when it falls below CV_HOLD_THRESH × CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC. Per-color
27	 * edge thresholds are uniform at 50 by default — separable later if any
28	 * fret needs its own. Mirrors fret-tuner detect_video.py defaults. */
29	#define CV_HOLD_THRESH         100.0f
30	#define CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC   0.78f

35	/* Sensor coordinates in native capture-frame space, anchored to 720×480
36	 * (Wii 480p60 — primary production source). (hx,hy) = brightness sensor,
37	 * (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor; both above the strike line.
38	 * Derived from fret-tuner detect_video.py 1920×1080 defaults via the
39	 * same Elgato HDMI capture, scaled by (3/8, 4/9). Runtime calibration
40	 * UI lands with M6. */
41	typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } sensor_xy_t;
42	
43	static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] =
44	{
45	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
46	    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },
47	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { 355, 311, 368, 311 },
48	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
49	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },
50	};

52	/* Per-fret BGR target / reject weights. Edge signal is
53	 * (target·c − max(0, reject·c)) × sat_ratio. Reject totals exceed 1.0
54	 * so camera-captured whites with color-temperature bias get suppressed,
55	 * not just mathematically perfect whites. */
56	typedef struct { float target[3]; float reject[3]; } color_filter_t;
57	
58	static const color_filter_t s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT] =
59	{
60	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.0f, 0.7f } },
61	    [FRET_RED]    = { { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.7f, 0.0f } },
62	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { { 0.0f, 0.5f, 0.5f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
63	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { { 1.0f, 0.4f, 0.0f }, { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.4f } },
64	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
65	};
66	
67	/* Per-fret detector state. Private — not on the bus. press_count is the
68	 * rising-edge counter the strum scheduler will eventually consume. */
69	static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
70	static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
71	static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];
72	static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];
73	static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];
74	
75	static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
76	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
77	
78	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
79	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;

81	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
82	
83	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
84	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
85	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
86	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
87	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
88	{
89	    int cx = (int)px;
90	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
91	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
92	    int cy = (int)py;
93	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
94	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
95	
96	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
97	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
98	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
99	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
100	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
101	
102	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
103	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
104	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
105	    {
106	        const uint8_t *row = frame
107	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
108	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
109	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
110	        {
111	            sum_b += row[0];
112	            sum_g += row[1];
113	            sum_r += row[2];
114	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
115	        }
116	    }
117	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
118	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
119	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
120	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
121	}
122	
123	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
124	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
125	{
126	    float m = bgr[0];
127	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
128	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
129	    return m;
130	}
131	
132	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
133	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
134	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
135	{
136	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
137	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
138	    float cmin = bgr[0];
139	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
140	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
141	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
142	
143	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
144	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
145	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
146	    return (target - reject) * sat;
147	}
148	
149	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
150	
151	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
152	{
153	    detector_state_t state;
154	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
155	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
156	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
157	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
158	
159	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
160	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
161	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
162	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
163	
164	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
165	    {
166	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
167	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
168	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
170	
171	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
172	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
173	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
174	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
175	
176	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
177	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
178	
179	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
180	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
181	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
182	
183	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
184	
185	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
186	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
187	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
188	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
189	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
190	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
191	
192	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
193	        float h = hd;
194	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
195	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
196	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
197	    }
198	
199	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
200	}
201	
202	/* ─── Calibration overlay ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
203	
204	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
205	 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
206	 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
207	 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
208	 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
209	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
210	
211	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
212	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
213	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
214	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
215	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
216	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
217	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
218	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
219	};
220	
221	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
222	                                 int x, int y,
223	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
224	{
225	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
226	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
227	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
228	}
229	
230	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
231	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
232	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
233	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
234	{
235	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
236	    while (x >= y)
237	    {
238	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
239	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
240	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
241	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
242	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
243	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
244	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
245	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
246	        y++;
247	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
248	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
249	    }
250	}
251	
252	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
253	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
254	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
255	{
256	    int rr = radius * radius;
257	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
258	    {
259	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
260	        {
261	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
262	            {
263	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
264	            }
265	        }
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
270	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
271	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
272	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
273	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
274	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
275	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
276	
277	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
278	{
279	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
280	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
281	    {
282	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
283	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
284	
285	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
286	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
287	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
288	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
289	
290	        if (s_pressed[i])
291	        {
292	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
293	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
294	        }
295	        if (s_edge_active[i])
296	        {
297	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
298	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
299	        }
300	    }
301	}

303	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
304	
305	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
306	{
307	    (void)param;
308	
309	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
310	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
311	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
312	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
```

```text
178	        return false;
179	    }
180	
181	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
182	    {

184	        close_cdc();

186	    }
187	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
188	    {

196	{
197	    (void)param;
198	
199	    LOG_INFO("FBL: fretboard link started\r\n");
200	
201	    uint8_t last_mask = 0u;
202	
203	    for (;;)
204	    {
205	        if (s_cdc_obj_valid && s_cdc_handle == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
206	        {
207	            s_cdc_obj_valid = false;
208	            (void)open_cdc(s_cdc_obj_pending);
209	        }
210	
211	        uint8_t mask;
212	        if (xQueueReceive(s_cmd_queue, &mask, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_HEARTBEAT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
213	        {
214	            last_mask = mask;
215	        }
216	        else
217	        {
218	            mask = last_mask;
219	        }
220	
221	        if (s_connected)
222	        {
223	            (void)send_one_byte(mask);
224	        }
225	    }
226	}

263	{
```

```h
#ifndef PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H
#define PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "game/fret.h"

/* Perf-log wire format. Mirror this header byte-for-byte in the host
 * decoder (tools/perf-log-decoder). Bump PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION on
 * every layout change; the host refuses streams that don't match.
 *
 * All fields little-endian, naturally aligned, fixed width. Records
 * are framed on the wire by the drain task (SOF magic + length + CRC);
 * the structs below are the framed payload only. */

#define PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION   1u

#define PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC        0x4D56u   /* 'M','V' little-endian */

/* SOF bytes: 0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 ("UMRV"). Distinct from the 16-bit
 * header magic so a mid-stream reader can resync on a 4-byte pattern. */
#define PERF_LOG_SOF_0            0x55u
#define PERF_LOG_SOF_1            0x4Du
#define PERF_LOG_SOF_2            0x52u
#define PERF_LOG_SOF_3            0x56u

typedef enum
{
    PERF_REC_SESSION        = 0x01,
    PERF_REC_STAMP          = 0x02,
    PERF_REC_DETECTOR       = 0x03,
    PERF_REC_TIMING         = 0x04,
    PERF_REC_PATCH          = 0x05,
    PERF_REC_DROP           = 0x06,
    PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER = 0x07,
} perf_rec_type_t;

/* stage_id values for PERF_REC_STAMP. Producer call sites map 1:1. */
typedef enum
{
    PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ            = 0x10,
    PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH      = 0x11,
    PERF_STAGE_CV_START           = 0x20,
    PERF_STAGE_CV_END             = 0x21,
    PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK            = 0x30,
    PERF_STAGE_FBL_SEND           = 0x40,
    PERF_STAGE_CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE = 0x41,
} perf_stage_t;

#define PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR        0x01u

/* Common header on every record. 16 B. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    uint16_t magic;           /* PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC */
    uint8_t  type;            /* perf_rec_type_t */
    uint8_t  flags;           /* PERF_FLAG_* */
    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* Video_FrameInfo.frame_count at producer site */
    uint64_t ts_counter;      /* SYS_TIME raw counter; host divides by timer_freq_hz */
} perf_hdr_t;

/* PERF_REC_SESSION — emitted once when the drain task starts. The host
 * decoder uses timer_freq_hz to convert ts_counter to seconds and
 * schema_version to refuse mismatched streams. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint32_t   timer_freq_hz;
    uint16_t   schema_version;
    uint16_t   reserved;
    uint32_t   fw_git_short;  /* zero until we wire a build-time symbol */
    uint32_t   reserved2;
} perf_rec_session_t;

/* PERF_REC_STAMP — single-point timestamp marker. aux is stage-specific:
 *   ISC_IRQ           : reserved (0)
 *   VIDEO_PUBLISH     : subscriber bitmask
 *   CV_START / CV_END : reserved (0)
 *   TP_TICK           : publish_mask (low 7 bits)
 *   FBL_SEND          : queued mask
 *   CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE: USB CDC result code */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint8_t    stage_id;      /* perf_stage_t */
    uint8_t    reserved[3];
    uint32_t   aux;
    uint32_t   reserved2;
    uint32_t   reserved3;
} perf_rec_stamp_t;

/* PERF_REC_DETECTOR — per-frame snapshot of cv_marvin_v1 internals.
 * hold/edge values use the same 0..65535 scaling as
 * detector_state_t.{raw_value, confidence} so the host can share one
 * conversion path. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint16_t   hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
    uint16_t   edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
    uint8_t    pressed_mask;
    uint8_t    edge_active_mask;
    uint16_t   reserved;
} perf_rec_detector_t;

/* PERF_REC_TIMING — timing_pipeline state at the per-frame tick. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint8_t    publish_mask;       /* low 7 bits = chord on the wire */
    uint8_t    chord_window_fill;  /* records currently held in chord window */
    uint8_t    fifo_depth;         /* delay FIFO depth */
    uint8_t    strum_dir;          /* 0 = none, 1 = down, 2 = up */
    uint32_t   reserved;
    uint32_t   reserved2;
    uint32_t   reserved3;
} perf_rec_timing_t;

/* PERF_REC_DROP — drain task emits at 1 Hz. Counters are cumulative
 * since session start; host computes deltas. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint32_t   dropped_state;
    uint32_t   dropped_patch;
    uint32_t   dropped_sink;
    uint32_t   reserved;
} perf_rec_drop_t;

/* PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER — periodic stack high-water dump. task_id is
 * a stable enum mirrored in the host decoder; words is the
 * uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark return (StackType_t units). */
typedef enum
{
    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,
    PERF_TASK_TIMING         = 3,
    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,
} perf_task_id_t;

typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint8_t    task_id;
    uint8_t    reserved[3];
    uint32_t   words;
} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;

/* PERF_REC_PATCH — Tier 2 ROI dump. Two 5×5 BGR patches per fret
 * (hold sensor + edge sensor). Coords are the (hx,hy) / (ex,ey) the
 * detector actually sampled — host can replay the detector math
 * pixel-for-pixel. */
#define PERF_PATCH_DIM        5u    /* matches CV_PATCH_RADIUS = 2 */
#define PERF_PATCH_PIXELS     (PERF_PATCH_DIM * PERF_PATCH_DIM)
#define PERF_PATCH_BYTES      (PERF_PATCH_PIXELS * 3u)   /* 75 B per patch */

typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    uint16_t hx, hy;
    uint16_t ex, ey;
    uint8_t  hold_bgr[PERF_PATCH_BYTES];
    uint8_t  edge_bgr[PERF_PATCH_BYTES];
} perf_patch_fret_t;        /* 8 + 75 + 75 = 158 B */

typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t        hdr;
    uint16_t          frame_w;
    uint16_t          frame_h;
    uint32_t          reserved;
    perf_patch_fret_t fret[FRET_COUNT];   /* 5 × 158 = 790 B */
} perf_rec_patch_t;          /* 16 + 8 + 790 = 814 B */

#endif /* PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H */

```

```h
#ifndef PERF_LOG_H
#define PERF_LOG_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "perf_log_records.h"

/* Per-frame performance log. Producers post records onto two static
 * queues (small / patch); a low-priority drain task frames them
 * (SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT) and pushes the bytes out the
 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.
 *
 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */

void PerfLog_Initialize(void);     /* call after Video_Initialize */
void PerfLog_Start(void);          /* call after vTaskStartScheduler */

bool PerfLog_IsRunning(void);

/* ─── Task-context emit ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLog_EmitStamp(perf_stage_t stage, uint32_t frame_epoch, uint32_t aux);
void PerfLog_EmitDetector(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                          const uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT],
                          const uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT],
                          uint8_t  pressed_mask,
                          uint8_t  edge_active_mask);
void PerfLog_EmitTiming(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                        uint8_t  publish_mask,
                        uint8_t  chord_window_fill,
                        uint8_t  fifo_depth,
                        uint8_t  strum_dir);
void PerfLog_EmitPatch(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                       uint16_t frame_w, uint16_t frame_h,
                       const perf_patch_fret_t fret[FRET_COUNT]);

/* ─── ISR-context emit ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
                              uint32_t frame_epoch,
                              uint32_t aux,
                              BaseType_t *higher_priority_task_woken);

#endif /* PERF_LOG_H */

```

```text
52	static uint8_t         s_strum_head, s_strum_tail, s_strum_count;
53	
54	static bool     s_chord_open;
55	static uint32_t s_chord_start_ms;
56	static uint8_t  s_chord_mask;
57	
58	static uint8_t  s_frets_active;
59	static bool     s_strum_active;
60	static uint32_t s_strum_release_at_ms;
61	static bool     s_strum_direction;        /* toggles down/up each strum */
62	
63	static uint8_t  s_prev_pressed_mask;
64	static uint16_t s_prev_press_count[FRET_COUNT];
65	static bool     s_press_count_seen;
66	static uint32_t s_release_at_ms[FRET_COUNT];
67	static uint8_t  s_release_pending_mask;
68	
69	static uint8_t  s_output_mask;
70	static uint32_t s_now_ms;
71	static uint64_t s_last_frame_us;
72	
73	static volatile bool s_pipeline_enabled = true;
74	
75	static const uint8_t s_fret_bit[FRET_COUNT] =
76	{
77	    [FRET_GREEN]  = TIMING_BIT_GREEN,
78	    [FRET_RED]    = TIMING_BIT_RED,
79	    [FRET_YELLOW] = TIMING_BIT_YELLOW,
80	    [FRET_BLUE]   = TIMING_BIT_BLUE,
81	    [FRET_ORANGE] = TIMING_BIT_ORANGE,
82	};
83	
84	static inline bool note_q_empty(void) { return s_note_count == 0u; }
85	static inline bool note_q_full(void)  { return s_note_count >= TP_FIFO_CAP; }
86	static inline bool strum_q_empty(void){ return s_strum_count == 0u; }
87	static inline bool strum_q_full(void) { return s_strum_count >= TP_FIFO_CAP; }
88	
89	static void note_q_push(pending_note_t n)
90	{
91	    s_note_q[s_note_tail] = n;
92	    s_note_tail = (uint8_t)((s_note_tail + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
93	    s_note_count++;
94	}
95	
96	static void note_q_pop(void)
97	{
98	    s_note_head = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
99	    s_note_count--;
100	}
101	
102	static void strum_q_push(pending_strum_t s)
103	{
104	    s_strum_q[s_strum_tail] = s;
105	    s_strum_tail = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
106	    s_strum_count++;
107	}
108	
109	static void strum_q_pop(void)
110	{
111	    s_strum_head = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
112	    s_strum_count--;
113	}
114	
115	/* Iterator helpers for the "is this fret needed by an outstanding entry?"
116	 * release-suppression check below. */
117	static bool note_q_any_needs(uint8_t bit)
118	{
119	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
120	    {
121	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
122	        if (s_note_q[idx].fret_mask & bit) { return true; }
123	    }
124	    return false;
125	}
126	
127	static bool strum_q_any_needs(uint8_t bit)
128	{
129	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_strum_count; i++)
130	    {
131	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
132	        if (s_strum_q[idx].fret_mask & bit) { return true; }
133	    }
134	    return false;
135	}
136	
137	static void publish_mask(uint8_t mask)
138	{
139	    s_output_mask = mask;
140	    if (s_pipeline_enabled)
141	    {
142	        FretboardLink_Send(mask);
143	    }
144	}
145	
146	/* Edge derivation:
147	 *   - presses_mask: rising edge (press_count change preferred; pressed-edge
148	 *     fallback if the detector doesn't expose press_count for that fret)
149	 *   - releases_mask: falling edge of pressed
150	 * confidence is unused by the pipeline but is the natural future home for
151	 * a quality gate; left untouched here. */
152	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
153	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
154	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
155	{
156	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
157	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
158	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
159	
160	    bool first = !s_press_count_seen;
161	
162	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
163	    {
164	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
165	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
166	
167	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
168	        uint16_t pc = state->fret[i].confidence;  /* placeholder slot */
169	        (void)pc;
170	
171	        /* press_count is private to the detector; for now we infer rising
172	         * edge from pressed transitions only. If a detector later exposes
173	         * a press_count via a side channel, plug it in here. */
174	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
175	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
176	
177	        s_prev_press_count[i] = state->fret[i].confidence;
178	    }
179	
180	    if (first) { s_press_count_seen = true; }
181	
182	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
183	    *presses_mask  = pm;
184	    *releases_mask = rm;
185	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
186	}
187	
188	static void chord_commit(void)
189	{
190	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
191	    {
192	        s_chord_open = false;
193	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
194	        return;
195	    }
196	
197	    uint32_t assert_at = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS - TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
198	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
199	
200	    if (!strum_q_empty())
201	    {
202	        uint8_t  last_idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + TP_FIFO_CAP - 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
203	        uint32_t earliest = s_strum_q[last_idx].strum_at_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
204	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0)
205	        {
206	            assert_at = earliest;
207	            strum_at  = assert_at + TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
208	        }
209	    }
210	
211	    pending_note_t  n = { .assert_at_ms = assert_at, .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
212	    pending_strum_t s = { .strum_at_ms  = strum_at,  .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
213	    note_q_push(n);
214	    strum_q_push(s);
215	
216	    s_chord_open = false;
217	    s_chord_mask = 0u;
218	}
219	
220	static void process_notes(void)
221	{
222	    while (!note_q_empty())
223	    {
224	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
225	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - n->assert_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
226	
227	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
228	        {
229	            uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
230	            bool need = (n->fret_mask & bit) != 0u;
231	            bool have = (s_frets_active & bit) != 0u;
232	            if (need && !have)      { s_frets_active |= bit; }
233	            else if (!need && have) { s_frets_active &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
234	        }
235	        note_q_pop();
236	    }
237	}
238	
239	static void process_strums(void)
240	{
241	    while (!strum_q_empty())
242	    {
243	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
244	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s->strum_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
245	
246	        s_strum_active        = true;
247	        s_strum_direction     = !s_strum_direction;
248	        s_strum_release_at_ms = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
249	
250	        strum_q_pop();
251	    }
252	}
253	
254	static void process_releases(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
255	{
256	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
257	    {
258	        uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
259	        if ((s_release_pending_mask & bit) == 0u) { continue; }
260	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_release_at_ms[i]) < 0) { continue; }
261	        if (live_pressed_mask & bit) { continue; }
262	        if (note_q_any_needs(bit) || strum_q_any_needs(bit)) { continue; }
263	
264	        s_frets_active        &= (uint8_t)~bit;
265	        s_release_pending_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit;
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	static void advance(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
270	{
271	    if (s_chord_open && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms) >= (int32_t)TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS)
272	    {
273	        chord_commit();
274	    }
275	
276	    if (s_strum_active && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_strum_release_at_ms) >= 0)
277	    {
278	        s_strum_active = false;
279	    }
280	
281	    process_notes();
282	    process_strums();
283	    process_releases(live_pressed_mask);
284	
285	    uint8_t mask = s_frets_active;
286	    if (s_strum_active)
287	    {
288	        mask |= s_strum_direction ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN;
289	    }
290	    publish_mask(mask);
291	}
292	
293	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
294	{
295	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
296	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
297	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
298	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
299	
300	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
301	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
302	
303	    if (presses)
304	    {
305	        if (!s_chord_open)
306	        {
307	            s_chord_open     = true;
308	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
309	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
310	        }
311	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
312	    }
313	
314	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
315	    {
316	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
317	        {
318	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
319	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
320	        }
321	    }
322	
323	    advance(pressed_mask);
324	}
325	
326	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
327	{
328	    (void)param;
329	
330	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
331	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
332	
333	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
334	
335	    for (;;)
336	    {
337	        detector_state_t state;
338	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
339	        {
340	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
341	            {
342	                continue;
343	            }
344	            process_frame(&state);
345	        }
346	        else
347	        {
348	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
349	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
350	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
351	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
352	        }
353	    }
354	}
355	
356	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void)
357	{
358	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(timing_pipeline_task,
359	                            "Timing",
360	                            TP_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
361	                            NULL,
362	                            TP_TASK_PRIORITY,
363	                            s_task_stack,
364	                            &s_task_tcb);
365	}
366	
367	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
368	{
369	    s_pipeline_enabled = enabled;
370	}
371
```
