```text
5	
6	/* Lightweight logging shim. Goes through libc printf → xc32_monitor →
7	 * DBGU. Adds a runtime severity filter and FreeRTOS-aware locking.
8	 *
9	 * Pre-scheduler calls work too — the mutex is taken only when the
10	 * scheduler is running, so log_printf is safe to call from
11	 * APP_Initialize / SYS_Initialize.
12	 *
13	 * Do NOT call from an ISR — use a different mechanism for ISR-side
14	 * diagnostics (queue to a task, or atomic counter polled by a task).
15	 */
16	
17	typedef enum
18	{
19	    LOG_LEVEL_ERROR = 0,
20	    LOG_LEVEL_WARN  = 1,
21	    LOG_LEVEL_INFO  = 2,
22	    LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG = 3,
23	} log_level_t;
24	
25	/* Set up the FreeRTOS mutex. Safe to call before vTaskStartScheduler.
26	 * Pass the initial filter level. */
27	void log_init(log_level_t initial_level);
28	
29	void        log_set_level(log_level_t lvl);
30	log_level_t log_get_level(void);
31	
32	void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
33	void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
34	    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
35	
36	/* Convenience macros — match a typical embedded log API. */
37	#define LOG_ERROR(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, __VA_ARGS__)
38	#define LOG_WARN(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_WARN,  __VA_ARGS__)
39	#define LOG_INFO(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_INFO,  __VA_ARGS__)
40	#define LOG_DEBUG(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG, __VA_ARGS__)
41	
42	#endif
```

```c
#include "perf_log.h"
#include "perf_log_records.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "queue.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"

/* ─── Configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

#define PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS    512u                 /* 2 KB */
#define PL_DRAIN_PRIORITY       (tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2u)

#define PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH    128u
#define PL_PATCH_QUEUE_DEPTH    8u

/* State-queue slot is sized to the largest small record. */
#define PL_STATE_SLOT_BYTES     (sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t))
#define PL_PATCH_SLOT_BYTES     (sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t))

#define PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS   1000u
#define PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS     20u

/* ─── Internal types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

/* Discriminated slot for the state queue. The drain task switches on
 * hdr.type and writes only the populated bytes. Sized to the largest
 * small record so all types fit in one slot. */
typedef union
{
    perf_hdr_t                 hdr;
    perf_rec_session_t         session;
    perf_rec_stamp_t           stamp;
    perf_rec_detector_t        detector;
    perf_rec_timing_t          timing;
    perf_rec_drop_t            drop;
    perf_rec_task_highwater_t  hwm;
} perf_rec_state_slot_t;

/* ─── Static storage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static QueueHandle_t s_state_q;
static StaticQueue_t s_state_q_buf;
static uint8_t       s_state_q_storage[PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t)];

static QueueHandle_t s_patch_q;
static StaticQueue_t s_patch_q_buf;
static uint8_t       s_patch_q_storage[PL_PATCH_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t)];

static StackType_t   s_drain_stack[PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t  s_drain_tcb;

static volatile uint32_t s_drop_state;
static volatile uint32_t s_drop_patch;
static volatile uint32_t s_drop_sink;

static volatile bool s_running;

/* ─── Header fill ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static inline void hdr_fill(perf_hdr_t *h, uint8_t type, uint8_t flags,
                            uint32_t frame_epoch)
{
    h->magic       = PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC;
    h->type        = type;
    h->flags       = flags;
    h->frame_epoch = frame_epoch;
    h->ts_counter  = (uint64_t)SYS_TIME_CounterGet();
}

/* ─── Sink (stub until MCC regen lands USB-device CDC) ───────────────────── */

extern void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void);
extern void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len);

static uint16_t record_size(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *r)
{
    switch (r->hdr.type)
    {
        case PERF_REC_SESSION:        return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_session_t);
        case PERF_REC_STAMP:          return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_stamp_t);
        case PERF_REC_DETECTOR:       return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_detector_t);
        case PERF_REC_TIMING:         return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_timing_t);
        case PERF_REC_DROP:           return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_drop_t);
        case PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER: return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_task_highwater_t);
        default:                      return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_hdr_t);
    }
}

/* ─── Drain task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void emit_session_record(void)
{
    perf_rec_session_t r;
    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_SESSION, 0u, 0u);
    r.timer_freq_hz  = SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet();
    r.schema_version = (uint16_t)PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION;
    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
}

static void emit_drop_record(void)
{
    perf_rec_drop_t r;
    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_DROP, 0u, 0u);
    r.dropped_state = s_drop_state;
    r.dropped_patch = s_drop_patch;
    r.dropped_sink  = s_drop_sink;
    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
}

static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
    s_running = true;
    emit_session_record();

    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();

    for (;;)
    {
        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
        {
            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
        }

        perf_rec_patch_t prec;
        while (xQueueReceive(s_patch_q, &prec, 0) == pdTRUE)
        {
            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&prec, (uint16_t)sizeof(prec));
        }

        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
        {
            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
            emit_drop_record();
        }
    }
}

/* ─── Init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLog_Initialize(void)
{
    s_state_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                   sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t),
                                   s_state_q_storage,
                                   &s_state_q_buf);
    configASSERT(s_state_q != NULL);

    s_patch_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_PATCH_QUEUE_DEPTH,
                                   sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t),
                                   s_patch_q_storage,
                                   &s_patch_q_buf);
    configASSERT(s_patch_q != NULL);
}

void PerfLog_Start(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(perf_log_drain_task,
                            "PerfDrain",
                            PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL,
                            PL_DRAIN_PRIORITY,
                            s_drain_stack,
                            &s_drain_tcb);
}

bool PerfLog_IsRunning(void)
{
    return s_running;
}

/* ─── Emit (task context) ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static inline void send_state(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *slot)
{
    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
    if (xQueueSend(s_state_q, slot, 0) != pdTRUE)
    {
        (void)__atomic_add_fetch(&s_drop_state, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
}

void PerfLog_EmitStamp(perf_stage_t stage, uint32_t frame_epoch, uint32_t aux)
{
    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, 0u, frame_epoch);
    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
    send_state(&slot);
}

void PerfLog_EmitDetector(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                          const uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT],
                          const uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT],
                          uint8_t  pressed_mask,
                          uint8_t  edge_active_mask)
{
    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
    hdr_fill(&slot.detector.hdr, PERF_REC_DETECTOR, 0u, frame_epoch);
    memcpy(slot.detector.hold_dist, hold_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.hold_dist));
    memcpy(slot.detector.edge_dist, edge_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.edge_dist));
    slot.detector.pressed_mask     = pressed_mask;
    slot.detector.edge_active_mask = edge_active_mask;
    send_state(&slot);
}

void PerfLog_EmitTiming(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                        uint8_t  publish_mask,
                        uint8_t  chord_window_fill,
                        uint8_t  fifo_depth,
                        uint8_t  strum_dir)
{
    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
    hdr_fill(&slot.timing.hdr, PERF_REC_TIMING, 0u, frame_epoch);
    slot.timing.publish_mask      = publish_mask;
    slot.timing.chord_window_fill = chord_window_fill;
    slot.timing.fifo_depth        = fifo_depth;
    slot.timing.strum_dir         = strum_dir;
    send_state(&slot);
}

void PerfLog_EmitPatch(uint32_t frame_epoch,
                       uint16_t frame_w, uint16_t frame_h,
                       const perf_patch_fret_t fret[FRET_COUNT])
{
    if (s_patch_q == NULL) { return; }
    perf_rec_patch_t r;
    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_PATCH, 0u, frame_epoch);
    r.frame_w = frame_w;
    r.frame_h = frame_h;
    memcpy(r.fret, fret, sizeof(r.fret));
    if (xQueueSend(s_patch_q, &r, 0) != pdTRUE)
    {
        (void)__atomic_add_fetch(&s_drop_patch, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
}

/* ─── Emit (ISR context) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
                              uint32_t frame_epoch,
                              uint32_t aux,
                              BaseType_t *higher_priority_task_woken)
{
    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR, frame_epoch);
    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
    if (xQueueSendFromISR(s_state_q, &slot, higher_priority_task_woken) != pdTRUE)
    {
        (void)__atomic_add_fetch(&s_drop_state, 1u, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
    }
}

/* ─── Sink-side drop accounting ──────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop(uint32_t bytes_dropped)
{
    (void)__atomic_add_fetch(&s_drop_sink, bytes_dropped, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);
}
```

```c
#include "perf_log_sink.h"
#include "perf_log.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "log.h"

/* USB-device CDC sink — stub. The real device-CDC bring-up follows the
 * UDPHS MCC regen; until then the sink frames records exactly the way
 * the wire path will, and discards them with periodic drained-bytes
 * accounting via LOG_INFO. This lets the producer side land + smoke-
 * test independently of the device-CDC stack. */

#define SINK_HEARTBEAT_MS    1000u

/* CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflect, no xorout). */
static uint16_t crc16_ccitt(uint16_t crc, const uint8_t *p, uint16_t len)
{
    while (len--)
    {
        crc ^= (uint16_t)(*p++) << 8;
        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 8u; i++)
        {
            crc = (crc & 0x8000u) ? (uint16_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021u)
                                  : (uint16_t)(crc << 1);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

static volatile uint32_t s_drained_records;
static volatile uint32_t s_drained_bytes;
static TickType_t        s_last_heartbeat_tick;

void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
{
    s_last_heartbeat_tick = xTaskGetTickCount();
    LOG_INFO("PERF: sink stub up (USB-device CDC pending MCC regen)\r\n");
}

/* Frames are: SOF[4] + LEN(LE u16) + PAYLOAD + CRC16(LE) over LEN+PAYLOAD.
 * Stub computes the CRC so the producer path exercises the same code
 * the wire sink will run. */
void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
{
    uint8_t  hdr[6];
    hdr[0] = 0x55u; hdr[1] = 0x4Du; hdr[2] = 0x52u; hdr[3] = 0x56u;
    hdr[4] = (uint8_t)(len & 0xFFu);
    hdr[5] = (uint8_t)((len >> 8) & 0xFFu);

    uint16_t crc = 0xFFFFu;
    crc = crc16_ccitt(crc, &hdr[4], 2u);
    crc = crc16_ccitt(crc, (const uint8_t *)payload, len);
    (void)crc;   /* would be appended in the wire sink */

    s_drained_records += 1u;
    s_drained_bytes   += (uint32_t)(sizeof(hdr) + len + 2u);

    TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
    if ((now - s_last_heartbeat_tick) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_HEARTBEAT_MS))
    {
        s_last_heartbeat_tick = now;
        LOG_INFO("PERF: sink stub drained %u rec / %u B\r\n",
                 (unsigned)s_drained_records, (unsigned)s_drained_bytes);
        s_drained_records = 0u;
        s_drained_bytes   = 0u;
    }
}

```

```text
1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.
10	
11	Scaffold is in place as of 2026-05-20: `detector/detector.{h,c}` owns the bus queue + a temporary drain task that logs records-per-second; `detector/cv_marvin_v1.{h,c}` subscribes to the video frame queue and publishes one `detector_state_t` per frame with `frame_epoch = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count` and all-zero fret state. Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.
12	
13	**Capture/display pipeline is done as of 2026-05-02:** source → TC358743 → CSI-2 @ 972 Mbps/lane → SAM9X75 → ISC DMA → DDR (BGRX32) → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel.
14	
15	> **Deeper-dive references:**
16	> - [`spec.md`](spec.md) — system-level spec (read first).
17	> - [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) — HDMI → DDR capture stage (CSI2DC, ISC, register settings, datasheet citations).
18	> - [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) — DDR → LCD display stage (XLCDC OVR1 wiring, pillarbox, cache coherence).
19	
20	> **Earlier entries** (capture/display bring-up, 2026-05-01 → 2026-05-15) are preserved in [`journal-archive.md`](journal-archive.md).
21	
22	---
23	
24	## Decision log
25	
26	| Date | Decision | Rationale |
27	|------|----------|-----------|
28	| 2026-05-21 | `manual_control` lands as the second producer of `fretboard_link`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Mode-level arbitration is two-mode (`timing_pipeline` vs `manual_control`) and embedded in `ManualControl_SetEnabled`: entering manual mode calls `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false)` then takes the wire; exiting reverses. | First concrete validation of the 2026-05-20 multi-producer `fretboard_link` design — `FretboardLink_Send` stays the only entry point; arbitration lives one layer up. Embedded toggle is enough for two producers; refactor to a dedicated `actuator_mode` arbiter when a third producer (game-state controller §4.8) arrives. `timing_pipeline.publish_mask` keeps updating internal state when gated so the next ≤5 ms tick after re-enable republishes a correct mask without a stale frame. |
29	| 2026-05-21 | Legato chosen for the manual-control surface; widgets authored in Microchip Graphics Composer (regenerated into `le_gen_screen_Screen0.{h,c}`); marvin-side code is a thin event-binding shim (`ui/manual_input.c`) | Composer makes the layout iterable in a tool rather than C source, and keeps our code out of MCC-clobbered files: only the binding shim references the Composer-generated widget pointers. **Does not commit spec Q5 for the full operator UI** — that's still M5's call. The thin-shim shape works equally well behind a future custom GFX2D UI by swapping the bind module. |
30	| 2026-05-21 | Manual-control input model is single-finger momentary; multi-finger chord input is out of scope for this surface | Legato's input pipeline (`legato_input.c:340/429`) routes each touch to a single focus widget, so a second simultaneous touch cancels the first button's release and strands its `pressed` state. Workarounds (custom maxtouch dispatcher; toggle-style frets) are real but not worth the complexity here — primary use case is game-menu navigation, which is single-finger by nature. Revisit only if a user-facing flow needs held chords. |
31	| 2026-05-21 | `fret_t` lives in `game/fret.h`, a top-level domain header. Detector / actuator / UI all include it directly; detector.h re-includes it so `detector_state_t` still compiles cleanly. | The fret colors (G/R/Y/B/O) are a Guitar Hero / Rock Band domain primitive, not a detector concept — the actuator and UI shouldn't reach into `detector/` for them. `game/` also stakes out the directory the future game-state controller (spec §4.8) will land in, so we don't have a transient home. Header-only, no cmake change. |
32	| 2026-05-20 | Relax Microchip's host CDC-ACM Communications-interface protocol check to accept `bInterfaceProtocol == 0x00 (None)` in addition to `0x01 (AT_V250)` | The fretboard hardware exposes its UART to marvin via the on-board EDBG debugger's CDC ACM (composite VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175: HID + CDC ACM IAD + vendor + MSC). EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. Both are CDC ACM in practice and Linux/macOS accept either. Two-line OR per check in `usb_host_cdc.c`; logged as patch #7 in the re-apply list. |
33	| 2026-05-20 | `USB_HOST_Initialize` ordering relative to `DRV_USB_EHCI/OHCI_Initialize` and `Legato_Initialize` is **not** load-bearing — keep MCC's emitted order | A prior session hand-edited `initialization.c` to move `USB_HOST_Initialize` *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits on the theory that the host layer needed the HCD interfaces present at init time. Empirical retest with the CDC diagnostic logging in place: MCC's original order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well. The host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time, not at `USB_HOST_Initialize`. Reverted the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. (This is unrelated to patch #6, which is the *peripheral* init order — MMU/AIC ahead of TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC — that one is still a real regression and stays in the list.) |
34	| 2026-05-20 | Marvin replaces the fret-tuner PC as the runtime brain | One-host architecture. fret-tuner persists as an off-band dev/calibration tool. fretboard stays a dumb relay (ADC out, bitmask in). |
35	| 2026-05-20 | Marvin is the *reference detector* — not a debug aid | HDMI-direct CV is ground-truth for the system. Fretboard's photo-detection and any future Edge-AI MCU are trained against marvin's output. Recording reference data is therefore a first-class subsystem (spec §4.6), not an afterthought. |
36	| 2026-05-20 | Multiple coexisting detectors are in scope; one canonical detector-state bus | At minimum `cv_marvin_v1` (CV) and `adc_fretboard` (over UART ingest). Bus shape: typed `detector_state_t` records on a FreeRTOS queue, single-consumer (timing pipeline). Recording snoops via tee from each producer. Spec §4.2. |
37	| 2026-05-20 | Timing pipeline (chord window, FIFO, strum scheduling) lives on marvin by default; fretboard-takeover is a fallback mode | Centralized = single source of truth, easier multi-detector fusion. Latency budget allows a few ms of UART jitter. Fallback mode disables marvin's pipeline; fretboard runs its own existing `fret_button.c` and feeds emitted-command telemetry up to marvin for capture/display. Spec §4.4 + §6. |
38	| 2026-05-20 | Reference-data export = SD card, format = detector-state + sparse keyframes | SD chosen over Ethernet/USB CDC because primary consumers are Edge-AI training (offline) and replay/sanity-check (offline). Live side-by-side comparison deferred. Format: dense `detector_state_t` records for all detectors + raw BGRX32 keyframes every 60 frames (1.38 MB/s sustained, comfortable on Class-10). No software JPEG (Cortex-A5 can't keep up; SAM9X75 has no HW encoder). Spec §4.6. |
39	| 2026-05-20 | `frame_epoch` (32-bit, incremented per captured ISC frame) is the master sync token across recordings, detectors, and any future off-board observers | Need single shared timeline; off-board detectors (e.g. Edge-AI device) record in their own format keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch` so post-hoc training-data alignment is trivial. Wraps after ~830 days @ 60 Hz. |
40	| 2026-05-20 | Operating modes are independent toggles (`detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`); named modes are presets over them | Matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split which has worked well in practice. Avoids a brittle global state machine. Spec §6. |
41	| 2026-05-01 | First real driver work is the TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI bridge | It's the gate between hardware-wired and pixels-in-memory. Everything downstream (vision, actuation) depends on it. |
42	| 2026-05-01 | Reference source = mainline Linux tc358743 driver + community 480p dumps | Linux driver has correct state machine / EDID / IRQ handling; community dumps have verified 480p register values. |
43	| 2026-05-01 | Integration shape (sensor vs standalone) deferred until Phase 3 | Avoid premature structure; real answer depends on how much state the driver actually needs. |
44	| 2026-05-01 | Journal lives at `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` | Firmware docs co-located with firmware; top-level `docs/` is hardware/mechanical. |
```

```text
130	### 2026-05-21 — Perf-logging bandwidth/capacity scoping
131	
132	Crunched numbers ahead of designing a frame-by-frame perf log (video + detector + actuator state) so we know which resolutions and which transports are actually in scope. Detail below; takeaway is that the spec's already-chosen "sparse keyframes + dense state" point (~1 MB/s) is the only real sweet spot, and the "full-rate raw video" wish is dead on arrival across every transport SAM9X75 has.
133	
134	**Baseline — 720×480 RGB888 (BGR888-packed in our pipeline) @ 60 Hz**
135	
136	- Per frame: 720 × 480 × 3 = **1.04 MB**.
137	- Per second: **62.2 MB/s ≈ 498 Mb/s**.
138	- All state payload (detector_state_t × 2 detectors + actuator + timing snapshot + per-frame metadata header) is ~150 B/frame ≈ **9 KB/s** — rounding error against pixels. This is a video-bandwidth problem, not a state-volume problem.
139	
140	**Scaled-down variants (per-second bandwidth)**
141	
142	| Variant | B/s |
143	|---|---|
144	| Full 720×480 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 62.2 MB/s |
145	| Same @ 30 Hz | 31.1 MB/s |
146	| 720×480 RGB565 @ 60 Hz | 41.5 MB/s |
147	| 720×480 grayscale @ 60 Hz | 20.7 MB/s |
148	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 15.6 MB/s |
149	| 360×240 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 7.78 MB/s |
150	| 180×120 RGB888 @ 30 Hz | 1.94 MB/s |
151	| Strike-line strip 720×80 @ 60 Hz | 10.4 MB/s |
152	| 5 ROI patches 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 922 KB/s |
153	| State-only (no pixels) @ 60 Hz | 9.1 KB/s |
154	
155	**Capacity over a session length**
156	
157	| Stream | 1 min | 5 min (song) | 10 min |
158	|---|---|---|---|
159	| Full @ 60 Hz | 3.73 GB | 18.7 GB | 37.3 GB |
160	| 360×240 @ 30 Hz | 467 MB | 2.33 GB | 4.67 GB |
161	| 1 keyframe/s + state (≈ spec §4.6) | 62 MB | 311 MB | 622 MB |
162	| ROI patches 60 Hz | 55 MB | 277 MB | 553 MB |
163	| State only | 547 KB | 2.7 MB | 5.5 MB |
164	
165	**Transport ceilings on this hardware** (sustained, realistic)
166	
167	| Channel | Sustained | Peripheral status |
168	|---|---|---|
169	| UART 115.2 kBd (console) | ~11 KB/s | in use (FLEXCOM4) |
170	| UART 921.6 kBd | ~92 KB/s | EDBG bridge cap |
171	| UART 3 Mbd (FLEXCOM max) | ~300 KB/s | unlikely through bridges |
172	| USB CDC ACM (HS device, class-stack overhead) | ~5–15 MB/s | device peripheral unused |
173	| USB Bulk (HS device, custom class) | ~30–40 MB/s | needs custom host-side reader |
174	| SDMMC Class-10 via FAT32 | ~5–10 MB/s | already planned for §4.6 keyframes |
175	| SDMMC UHS-I | ~25–50 MB/s | bus capable, FS overhead bites |
176	| GMAC Ethernet UDP | ~30–60 MB/s | GMAC unused |
177	| GMAC Ethernet TCP | ~10–20 MB/s | GMAC unused |
178	
179	**What fits where**
180	
181	- **State-only (9 KB/s)** fits everywhere including the console UART — no new transport needed if the goal is just "trace detector + timing + actuator decisions per frame."
182	- **ROI patches 60 Hz (~1 MB/s)** preserves everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples; streams comfortably over USB CDC, fits an entire song on SD with room to spare.
183	- **1 keyframe/s + dense state (~1 MB/s)** is what spec §4.6 already commits to, fits any modern SD card, and survives over USB CDC or Ethernet.
184	- **Full 60 Hz (62 MB/s)** doesn't fit any transport sustained, *and* a 5-minute song at that rate is 18.7 GB — DOA.
```

```text
188	### 2026-05-21 — cv_marvin_v1 threshold tuning + timing-pipeline tweaks
189	
190	First end-to-end gameplay test on hardware. Detector was firing roughly random presses at first; resolved by reading actual signal values rather than guessing.
191	
192	**Visibility added:**
193	- State-reactive overlay in `cv_marvin_v1.c` — position rings always; filled center dot when `s_pressed[i]` (white in the hold ring) or `s_edge_active[i]` (fret-color in the edge ring). Lets the user watch chatter live: stable note → steady dot for hold duration; strum window → flash on the edge dot.
194	- Periodic ~2 Hz log dump (`frame_count % 30 == 0`) showing per-fret `hold_dist / edge_dist / P E` flags.
195	
196	**Diagnosis (Easy mode, no real B/O presses):**
197	- Idle hold floor sits at 22–48 across all five frets, **not** the limited-range 16 floor `display_path.md` would suggest. Playfield-glow at the sample sites is well above the limited-range black point.
198	- Real-press hold spikes to 67–186, leaving a clean gap above the noise ceiling.
199	- Hold threshold 50 with release-frac 0.6 (release=30) was *below* the idle floor for Y and B → those frets latched permanently pressed and never released.
200	- Edge threshold 50 was at the peak of real-edge signal (40–53), almost never tripping. timing_pipeline only uses `pressed` today, so dead edges aren't the chatter source — but lowering edge threshold lets `s_edge_active` overlay flicker meaningfully again.
201	
202	**Settings landed (in `cv_marvin_v1.c`):**
203	- `CV_HOLD_THRESH`: 50 → **100** (after iterating 65 → 80 → 100; 100 cleanly above noise across all frets, real presses still spike to 150–186).
204	- `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`: 0.60 → **0.78** (release ≈ 78 — above the noise ceiling, comfortably below real-press floor).
205	- `CV_EDGE_THRESH`: 50 → **25** (gives the overlay an honest edge indicator without affecting pipeline behavior).
206	- Sample coords nudged 1 px on G/R/Y/B/O edges + B hold for slightly cleaner alignment.
207	
208	**Performance:** Expert-mode play is now quite good — clean note recognition, fret hold-through across consecutive same-fret notes confirmed by trace through `process_releases` (release suppressed when the next chord-commit's `note_q` entry already needs the bit, within `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS − TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS = 190 ms` of detector-release-to-detector-press).
209	
210	**Timing-pipeline tweaks** (Greg's hand-edits): `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` 50→25, `TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS` 20→30, `TP_FIFO_CAP` 16→32.
211	
212	Open question added above: `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` is Expert-tuned; Easy/Medium/Hard may need different values because note travel time differs.
```

```text
97	/*******************************************************
98	 * USB CDC Device Events - Application Event Handler
99	 *******************************************************/
100	
101	USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE APP_USBDeviceCDCEventHandler
102	(
103	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX index,
104	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT event,
105	    void * pData,
106	    uintptr_t userData
107	)
108	{
109	    APP_DATA * appDataObject;
110	    USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE * controlLineStateData;
111	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_READ_COMPLETE * eventDataRead;
112	    
113	    appDataObject = (APP_DATA *)userData;
114	
115	    switch(event)
116	    {
117	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_GET_LINE_CODING:
118	
119	            /* This means the host wants to know the current line
120	             * coding. This is a control transfer request. Use the
121	             * USB_DEVICE_ControlSend() function to send the data to
122	             * host.  */
123	
124	            USB_DEVICE_ControlSend(appDataObject->deviceHandle,
125	                    &appDataObject->getLineCodingData, sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
126	
127	            break;
128	
129	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_LINE_CODING:
130	
131	            /* This means the host wants to set the line coding.
132	             * This is a control transfer request. Use the
133	             * USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive() function to receive the
134	             * data from the host */
135	
136	            USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive(appDataObject->deviceHandle,
137	                    &appDataObject->setLineCodingData, sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
138	
139	            break;
140	
141	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE:
142	
143	            /* This means the host is setting the control line state.
144	             * Read the control line state. We will accept this request
145	             * for now. */
146	
147	            controlLineStateData = (USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE *)pData;
148	            appDataObject->controlLineStateData.dtr = controlLineStateData->dtr;
149	            appDataObject->controlLineStateData.carrier = controlLineStateData->carrier;
150	
151	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
152	
153	            break;
154	
155	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SEND_BREAK:
156	
157	            /* This means that the host is requesting that a break of the
158	             * specified duration be sent. Read the break duration */
159	
160	            appDataObject->breakData = ((USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_SEND_BREAK *)pData)->breakDuration;
161	            
162	            /* Complete the control transfer by sending a ZLP  */
163	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
164	            
165	            break;
166	
167	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
168	
169	            /* This means that the host has sent some data*/
170	            eventDataRead = (USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_READ_COMPLETE *)pData;
171	            
172	            if(eventDataRead->status != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_ERROR)
173	            {
174	                appDataObject->isReadComplete = true;
175	                
176	                appDataObject->numBytesRead = eventDataRead->length; 
177	            }
178	            break;
179	
180	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_RECEIVED:
181	
182	            /* The data stage of the last control transfer is
183	             * complete. For now we accept all the data */
184	
185	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
186	            break;
187	
188	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
189	
190	            /* This means the GET LINE CODING function data is valid. We don't
191	             * do much with this data in this demo. */
192	            break;
193	
194	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
195	
196	            /* This means that the data write got completed. We can schedule
197	             * the next read. */
198	
199	            appDataObject->isWriteComplete = true;
200	            break;
201	
202	        default:
203	            break;
204	    }
205	
206	    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
207	}

209	/***********************************************
210	 * Application USB Device Layer Event Handler.
211	 ***********************************************/
212	void APP_USBDeviceEventHandler 
213	(
214	    USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, 
215	    void * eventData, 
216	    uintptr_t context 
217	)
218	{
219	    USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *configuredEventData;
220	
221	    switch(event)
222	    {
223	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
224	
225	            /* This event is used for switch debounce. This flag is reset
226	             * by the switch process routine. */
227	            appData.sofEventHasOccurred = true;
228	            
229	            break;
230	
231	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
232	
233	            /* Update LED to show reset state */
234	            LED_Off();
235	
236	            appData.isConfigured = false;
237	
238	            break;
239	
240	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
241	
242	            /* Check the configuration. We only support configuration 1 */
243	            configuredEventData = (USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED*)eventData;
244	            
245	            if ( configuredEventData->configurationValue == 1)
246	            {
247	                /* Update LED to show configured state */
248	                LED_On();
249	                
250	                /* Register the CDC Device application event handler here.
251	                 * Note how the appData object pointer is passed as the
252	                 * user data */
253	
254	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0, APP_USBDeviceCDCEventHandler, (uintptr_t)&appData);
255	
256	                /* Mark that the device is now configured */
257	                appData.isConfigured = true;
258	            }
259	            
260	            break;
261	
262	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
263	
264	            /* VBUS was detected. We can attach the device */
265	            USB_DEVICE_Attach(appData.deviceHandle);
266	            
267	            break;
268	
269	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
270	            
271	            /* VBUS is not available. We can detach the device */
272	            USB_DEVICE_Detach(appData.deviceHandle);
273	            
274	            appData.isConfigured = false;
275	            
276	            LED_Off();
277	            
278	            break;
279	
280	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
281	
282	            /* Switch LED to show suspended state */
283	            LED_Off();
284	            
285	            break;
286	
287	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
288	        
289	            if(appData.isConfigured == true)
290	            {
291	                LED_On();
292	            }
293	            break;
294	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
295	        default:
296	            
297	            break;
298	    }
299	}

306	
307	void APP_ProcessSwitchPress(void)
308	{
309	    /* This function checks if the switch is pressed and then
310	     * debounces the switch press*/
311	    
312	    if(SWITCH_STATE_PRESSED == (SWITCH_Get()))
313	    {
314	        if(appData.ignoreSwitchPress)
315	        {
316	            /* This means the key press is in progress */
317	            if(appData.sofEventHasOccurred)
318	            {
319	                /* A timer event has occurred. Update the debounce timer */
320	                appData.switchDebounceTimer ++;
321	                appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
322	                
323	                if (USB_DEVICE_ActiveSpeedGet(appData.deviceHandle) == USB_SPEED_FULL)
324	                {
325	                    appData.debounceCount = APP_USB_SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_COUNT_FS;
326	                }
327	                else if (USB_DEVICE_ActiveSpeedGet(appData.deviceHandle) == USB_SPEED_HIGH)
328	                {
329	                    appData.debounceCount = APP_USB_SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_COUNT_HS;
330	                }
331	                if(appData.switchDebounceTimer == appData.debounceCount)
332	                {
333	                    /* Indicate that we have valid switch press. The switch is
334	                     * pressed flag will be cleared by the application tasks
335	                     * routine. We should be ready for the next key press.*/
336	                    appData.isSwitchPressed = true;
337	                    appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
338	                    appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
339	                }
340	            }
341	        }
342	        else
343	        {
344	            /* We have a fresh key press */
345	            appData.ignoreSwitchPress = true;
346	            appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
347	        }
348	    }
349	    else
350	    {
351	        /* No key press. Reset all the indicators. */
352	        appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
353	        appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
354	        appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
355	    }
356	}
357	
358	/*****************************************************
359	 * This function is called in every step of the
360	 * application state machine.
361	 *****************************************************/
362	
363	bool APP_StateReset(void)
364	{
365	    /* This function returns true if the device
366	     * was reset  */
367	
368	    bool retVal;
369	
370	    if(appData.isConfigured == false)
371	    {
372	        appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION;
373	        appData.readTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
374	        appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
375	        appData.isReadComplete = true;
376	        appData.isWriteComplete = true;
377	        retVal = true;
378	    }
379	    else
380	    {
381	        retVal = false;
382	    }
383	
384	    return(retVal);
385	}

400	
401	void APP_Initialize(void)
402	{
403	    /* Place the App state machine in its initial state. */
404	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
405	    
406	    /* Device Layer Handle  */
407	    appData.deviceHandle = USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID ;
408	
409	    /* Device configured status */
410	    appData.isConfigured = false;
411	
412	    /* Initial get line coding state */
413	    appData.getLineCodingData.dwDTERate = 9600;
414	    appData.getLineCodingData.bParityType = 0;
415	    appData.getLineCodingData.bCharFormat= 0; 
416	    appData.getLineCodingData.bDataBits = 8;
417	
418	    /* Read Transfer Handle */
419	    appData.readTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
420	
421	    /* Write Transfer Handle */
422	    appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
423	
424	    /* Initialize the read complete flag */
425	    appData.isReadComplete = true;
426	
427	    /*Initialize the write complete flag*/
428	    appData.isWriteComplete = true;
429	
430	    /* Initialize Ignore switch flag */
431	    appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
432	
433	    /* Reset the switch debounce counter */
434	    appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
435	
436	    /* Reset other flags */
437	    appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
438	    
439	    /* To know status of Switch */
440	    appData.isSwitchPressed = false;
441	
442	    /* Set up the read buffer */
443	    appData.cdcReadBuffer = &cdcReadBuffer[0];
444	
445	    /* Set up the read buffer */
446	    appData.cdcWriteBuffer = &cdcWriteBuffer[0];       
447	}

450	/******************************************************************************
451	  Function:
452	    void APP_Tasks(void)
453	
454	  Remarks:
455	    See prototype in app.h.
456	 */
457	
458	void APP_Tasks(void)
459	{
460	    /* Update the application state machine based
461	     * on the current state */
462	    int i;
463	    
464	    switch(appData.state)
465	    {
466	        case APP_STATE_INIT:
467	
468	            /* Open the device layer */
469	            appData.deviceHandle = USB_DEVICE_Open( USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0, DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE );
470	
471	            if(appData.deviceHandle != USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
472	            {
473	                /* Register a callback with device layer to get event notification (for end point 0) */
474	                USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(appData.deviceHandle, APP_USBDeviceEventHandler, 0);
475	
476	                appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION;
477	            }
478	            else
479	            {
480	                /* The Device Layer is not ready to be opened. We should try
481	                 * again later. */
482	            }
483	
484	            break;
485	
486	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION:
487	
488	            /* Check if the device was configured */
489	            if(appData.isConfigured)
490	            {
491	                /* If the device is configured then lets start reading */
492	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ;
493	            }
494	            
495	            break;
496	
497	        case APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ:
498	
499	            if(APP_StateReset())
500	            {
501	                break;
502	            }
503	
504	            /* If a read is complete, then schedule a read
505	             * else wait for the current read to complete */
506	
507	            appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_READ_COMPLETE;
508	            if(appData.isReadComplete == true)
509	            {
510	                appData.isReadComplete = false;
511	                appData.readTransferHandle =  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
512	
513	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read (USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
514	                        &appData.readTransferHandle, appData.cdcReadBuffer,
515	                        APP_READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
516	                
517	                if(appData.readTransferHandle == USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID)
518	                {
519	                    appData.state = APP_STATE_ERROR;
520	                    break;
521	                }
522	            }
523	
524	            break;
525	
526	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_READ_COMPLETE:
527	        case APP_STATE_CHECK_SWITCH_PRESSED:
528	
529	            if(APP_StateReset())
530	            {
531	                break;
532	            }
533	
534	            APP_ProcessSwitchPress();
535	
536	            /* Check if a character was received or a switch was pressed.
537	             * The isReadComplete flag gets updated in the CDC event handler. */
538	
539	            if(appData.isReadComplete || appData.isSwitchPressed)
540	            {
541	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_WRITE;
542	            }
543	
544	            break;
545	
546	
547	        case APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_WRITE:
548	
549	            if(APP_StateReset())
550	            {
551	                break;
552	            }
553	
554	            /* Setup the write */
555	
556	            appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
557	            appData.isWriteComplete = false;
558	            appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_WRITE_COMPLETE;
559	
560	            if(appData.isSwitchPressed)
561	            {
562	                /* If the switch was pressed, then send the switch prompt*/
563	                appData.isSwitchPressed = false;
564	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
565	                        &appData.writeTransferHandle, switchPromptUSB, sizeof(switchPromptUSB),
566	                        USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
567	            }
568	            else
569	            {
570	                /* Else echo each received character by adding 1 */
571	                for(i = 0; i < appData.numBytesRead; i++)
572	                {
573	                    if((appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] != 0x0A) && (appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] != 0x0D))
574	                    {
575	                        appData.cdcWriteBuffer[i] = appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] + 1;
576	                    }
577	                }
578	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
579	                        &appData.writeTransferHandle,
580	                        appData.cdcWriteBuffer, appData.numBytesRead,
581	                        USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
582	            }
583	
584	            break;
585	
586	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_WRITE_COMPLETE:
587	
588	            if(APP_StateReset())
589	            {
590	                break;
591	            }
592	
593	            /* Check if a character was sent. The isWriteComplete
594	             * flag gets updated in the CDC event handler */
595	
596	            if(appData.isWriteComplete == true)
597	            {
598	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ;
599	            }
600	
601	            break;
602	
603	        case APP_STATE_ERROR:
604	        default:
605	            
606	            break;
607	    }
608	}
```

```c
#include "perf_log_sink.h"
#include "perf_log.h"

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"
#include "semphr.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "configuration.h"
#include "usb/usb_device.h"
#include "usb/usb_device_cdc.h"

#include "log.h"

/* USB-device CDC ACM sink. The MCC config provides USB_DEVICE_Initialize
 * + the USB_DEVICE_Tasks worker; we own the application-side state
 * machine: open the device handle, register event handlers, attach
 * on VBUS, and provide a blocking write API for the perf-log drain
 * task.
 *
 * Single producer (the drain task). Not thread-safe by design: serialize
 * one write at a time, wait for WRITE_COMPLETE, then post the next. A
 * second writer would overlap on the staging buffer. */

/* Header(6) + max payload (sizeof patch record) + CRC(2), padded up to
 * a cache-line multiple so UDPHS DMA can't share a line with whatever
 * sits next to us in BSS. */
#define SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX  832u

#define SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS    50u
#define SINK_CONFIG_WAIT_MS   100u
#define SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS 100u

static USB_DEVICE_HANDLE       s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID;
static volatile bool           s_is_configured;
static volatile USB_CDC_LINE_CODING s_line_coding =
{
    .dwDTERate   = 921600u,
    .bCharFormat = 0u,
    .bParityType = 0u,
    .bDataBits   = 8u,
};
static volatile USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE s_cls;

static SemaphoreHandle_t s_write_done;
static StaticSemaphore_t s_write_done_buf;

/* Staging buffer for one outgoing frame. UDPHS DMAs from this address;
 * keep it cache-aligned so the driver's cache-maintenance ops don't
 * collide with neighboring data. */
static uint8_t CACHE_ALIGN s_tx_frame[SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX];

/* CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflect, no xorout). */
static uint16_t crc16_ccitt(uint16_t crc, const uint8_t *p, uint16_t len)
{
    while (len--)
    {
        crc ^= (uint16_t)(*p++) << 8;
        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < 8u; i++)
        {
            crc = (crc & 0x8000u) ? (uint16_t)((crc << 1) ^ 0x1021u)
                                  : (uint16_t)(crc << 1);
        }
    }
    return crc;
}

/* ─── CDC class event handler ────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE cdc_event_handler(
    USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX index,
    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT event,
    void *pData,
    uintptr_t userData)
{
    (void)index;
    (void)userData;

    switch (event)
    {
        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_GET_LINE_CODING:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlSend(s_dev_handle,
                                         (void *)&s_line_coding,
                                         sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_LINE_CODING:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive(s_dev_handle,
                                            (void *)&s_line_coding,
                                            sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE:
        {
            const USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE *cls = pData;
            s_cls.dtr     = cls->dtr;
            s_cls.carrier = cls->carrier;
            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
            break;
        }

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SEND_BREAK:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_RECEIVED:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(s_dev_handle,
                                           USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
        {
            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
            break;
        }

        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
        default:
            break;
    }
    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
}

/* ─── Device-layer event handler ─────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void device_event_handler(USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, void *eventData,
                                 uintptr_t context)
{
    (void)context;

    switch (event)
    {
        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DECONFIGURED:
            s_is_configured = false;
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
        {
            const USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *cd = eventData;
            if (cd->configurationValue == 1u)
            {
                (void)USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
                                                    cdc_event_handler, 0u);
                s_is_configured = true;
                LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device CDC configured\r\n");
            }
            break;
        }

        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_Attach(s_dev_handle);
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
            (void)USB_DEVICE_Detach(s_dev_handle);
            s_is_configured = false;
            break;

        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
        default:
            break;
    }
}

/* ─── Public sink interface ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */

void PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize(void)
{
    s_write_done = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_write_done_buf);
    configASSERT(s_write_done != NULL);

    /* Open may fail until USB_DEVICE_Initialize finishes its own first
     * task tick — retry until success. Drain task is alive at this
     * point so vTaskDelay is fine. */
    while (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
    {
        s_dev_handle = USB_DEVICE_Open(USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0,
                                       DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE);
        if (s_dev_handle == USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
        {
            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_OPEN_RETRY_MS));
        }
    }

    USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(s_dev_handle, device_event_handler, 0u);
    LOG_INFO("PERF: USB device opened, waiting for host enumeration\r\n");
}

void PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(const void *payload, uint16_t len)
{
    if (!s_is_configured || !s_cls.dtr)
    {
        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
        return;
    }

    uint16_t total = (uint16_t)(6u + len + 2u);
    if (total > SINK_FRAME_BYTES_MAX)
    {
        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
        return;
    }

    s_tx_frame[0] = 0x55u;
    s_tx_frame[1] = 0x4Du;
    s_tx_frame[2] = 0x52u;
    s_tx_frame[3] = 0x56u;
    s_tx_frame[4] = (uint8_t)(len & 0xFFu);
    s_tx_frame[5] = (uint8_t)((len >> 8) & 0xFFu);
    memcpy(&s_tx_frame[6], payload, len);

    uint16_t crc = 0xFFFFu;
    crc = crc16_ccitt(crc, &s_tx_frame[4], (uint16_t)(2u + len));
    s_tx_frame[6u + len]      = (uint8_t)(crc & 0xFFu);
    s_tx_frame[6u + len + 1u] = (uint8_t)((crc >> 8) & 0xFFu);

    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);

    USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
    USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT r = USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
                                                  &th,
                                                  s_tx_frame, total,
                                                  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
    if (r != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_OK)
    {
        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
        return;
    }

    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done,
                       pdMS_TO_TICKS(SINK_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
    {
        /* Host went away mid-write or stalled. Mark dropped and let
         * the next state-machine pass observe DECONFIGURED. */
        PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop((uint32_t)len);
    }
}

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:24:13Z)**_

Sink is now a real USB-device CDC implementation, not a stub. Summary:

**[perf_log_sink_cdc.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_sink_cdc.c)** now owns the application side of the MCC-provided USB-device + CDC class:
- **Init**: opens `USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0` (retry loop until MCC's device task has the handle), registers the device-layer event handler.
- **Device events**: `POWER_DETECTED` → `USB_DEVICE_Attach`; `CONFIGURED` → register CDC class handler, set `s_is_configured`; `POWER_REMOVED`/`RESET`/`DECONFIGURED` → clear configured.
- **CDC events**: `GET/SET_LINE_CODING` and `SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE` (latches DTR into `s_cls`); `WRITE_COMPLETE` does `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` on a binary semaphore (matches the established pattern in [fretboard_link.c:60-101](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L60-L101)).
- **Write path**: single cache-aligned 832 B staging buffer (header 6 + max patch payload 814 + CRC 2). Builds the frame in place, calls `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write` with `DATA_COMPLETE`, waits on the write-done semaphore with 100 ms timeout. DTR-gated; not-configured / not-DTR / write-rejected / write-timeout all increment `s_drop_sink` via `PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop`.

Note: drain task emits `PERF_REC_SESSION` immediately at startup, so if the host plugs in later, that initial SESSION is lost (counted as drop). Worth handling later by re-emitting on configured-edge — left as a follow-up. Journal entry updated to reflect the sink landing.

Producer call sites are still unwired (next step). After flashing this build the device should enumerate as a CDC ACM port; before producers are wired you'll just see the periodic `PERF_REC_DROP` records from the drain task itself.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:27:01Z)**_

Replaced the four `__atomic_add_fetch` callsites with FreeRTOS-critical-section helpers (`counter_add_task` / `counter_add_isr`). Both wrap a plain `*p += v` in `taskENTER_CRITICAL` (or `_FROM_ISR`), which the ARM926 port implements as a global IRQ-disable — so the RMW is indivisible across both task and ISR preemption. No libatomic dependency, no libcall.

The driver only emits `POWER_DETECTED` on a low→high transition, so when the cable is already connected at boot the event has already fired by the time our handler is registered, and we miss it. Reading the GPIO directly recovers that case without changing the hot-plug path.

```text
97	/*******************************************************
98	 * USB CDC Device Events - Application Event Handler
99	 *******************************************************/
100	
101	USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE APP_USBDeviceCDCEventHandler
102	(
103	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX index,
104	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT event,
105	    void * pData,
106	    uintptr_t userData
107	)
108	{
109	    APP_DATA * appDataObject;
110	    USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE * controlLineStateData;
111	    USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_READ_COMPLETE * eventDataRead;
112	    
113	    appDataObject = (APP_DATA *)userData;
114	
115	    switch(event)
116	    {
117	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_GET_LINE_CODING:
118	
119	            /* This means the host wants to know the current line
120	             * coding. This is a control transfer request. Use the
121	             * USB_DEVICE_ControlSend() function to send the data to
122	             * host.  */
123	
124	            USB_DEVICE_ControlSend(appDataObject->deviceHandle,
125	                    &appDataObject->getLineCodingData, sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
126	
127	            break;
128	
129	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_LINE_CODING:
130	
131	            /* This means the host wants to set the line coding.
132	             * This is a control transfer request. Use the
133	             * USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive() function to receive the
134	             * data from the host */
135	
136	            USB_DEVICE_ControlReceive(appDataObject->deviceHandle,
137	                    &appDataObject->setLineCodingData, sizeof(USB_CDC_LINE_CODING));
138	
139	            break;
140	
141	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE:
142	
143	            /* This means the host is setting the control line state.
144	             * Read the control line state. We will accept this request
145	             * for now. */
146	
147	            controlLineStateData = (USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE *)pData;
148	            appDataObject->controlLineStateData.dtr = controlLineStateData->dtr;
149	            appDataObject->controlLineStateData.carrier = controlLineStateData->carrier;
150	
151	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
152	
153	            break;
154	
155	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_SEND_BREAK:
156	
157	            /* This means that the host is requesting that a break of the
158	             * specified duration be sent. Read the break duration */
159	
160	            appDataObject->breakData = ((USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_SEND_BREAK *)pData)->breakDuration;
161	            
162	            /* Complete the control transfer by sending a ZLP  */
163	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
164	            
165	            break;
166	
167	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_READ_COMPLETE:
168	
169	            /* This means that the host has sent some data*/
170	            eventDataRead = (USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_DATA_READ_COMPLETE *)pData;
171	            
172	            if(eventDataRead->status != USB_DEVICE_CDC_RESULT_ERROR)
173	            {
174	                appDataObject->isReadComplete = true;
175	                
176	                appDataObject->numBytesRead = eventDataRead->length; 
177	            }
178	            break;
179	
180	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_RECEIVED:
181	
182	            /* The data stage of the last control transfer is
183	             * complete. For now we accept all the data */
184	
185	            USB_DEVICE_ControlStatus(appDataObject->deviceHandle, USB_DEVICE_CONTROL_STATUS_OK);
186	            break;
187	
188	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_CONTROL_TRANSFER_DATA_SENT:
189	
190	            /* This means the GET LINE CODING function data is valid. We don't
191	             * do much with this data in this demo. */
192	            break;
193	
194	        case USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
195	
196	            /* This means that the data write got completed. We can schedule
197	             * the next read. */
198	
199	            appDataObject->isWriteComplete = true;
200	            break;
201	
202	        default:
203	            break;
204	    }
205	
206	    return USB_DEVICE_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE_NONE;
207	}
208	
209	/***********************************************
210	 * Application USB Device Layer Event Handler.
211	 ***********************************************/
212	void APP_USBDeviceEventHandler 
213	(
214	    USB_DEVICE_EVENT event, 
215	    void * eventData, 
216	    uintptr_t context 
217	)
218	{
219	    USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED *configuredEventData;
220	
221	    switch(event)
222	    {
223	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SOF:
224	
225	            /* This event is used for switch debounce. This flag is reset
226	             * by the switch process routine. */
227	            appData.sofEventHasOccurred = true;
228	            
229	            break;
230	
231	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESET:
232	
233	            /* Update LED to show reset state */
234	            LED_Off();
235	
236	            appData.isConfigured = false;
237	
238	            break;
239	
240	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_CONFIGURED:
241	
242	            /* Check the configuration. We only support configuration 1 */
243	            configuredEventData = (USB_DEVICE_EVENT_DATA_CONFIGURED*)eventData;
244	            
245	            if ( configuredEventData->configurationValue == 1)
246	            {
247	                /* Update LED to show configured state */
248	                LED_On();
249	                
250	                /* Register the CDC Device application event handler here.
251	                 * Note how the appData object pointer is passed as the
252	                 * user data */
253	
254	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_EventHandlerSet(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0, APP_USBDeviceCDCEventHandler, (uintptr_t)&appData);
255	
256	                /* Mark that the device is now configured */
257	                appData.isConfigured = true;
258	            }
259	            
260	            break;
261	
262	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_DETECTED:
263	
264	            /* VBUS was detected. We can attach the device */
265	            USB_DEVICE_Attach(appData.deviceHandle);
266	            
267	            break;
268	
269	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_POWER_REMOVED:
270	            
271	            /* VBUS is not available. We can detach the device */
272	            USB_DEVICE_Detach(appData.deviceHandle);
273	            
274	            appData.isConfigured = false;
275	            
276	            LED_Off();
277	            
278	            break;
279	
280	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_SUSPENDED:
281	
282	            /* Switch LED to show suspended state */
283	            LED_Off();
284	            
285	            break;
286	
287	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_RESUMED:
288	        
289	            if(appData.isConfigured == true)
290	            {
291	                LED_On();
292	            }
293	            break;
294	        case USB_DEVICE_EVENT_ERROR:
295	        default:
296	            
297	            break;
298	    }
299	}

306	
307	void APP_ProcessSwitchPress(void)
308	{
309	    /* This function checks if the switch is pressed and then
310	     * debounces the switch press*/
311	    
312	    if(SWITCH_STATE_PRESSED == (SWITCH_Get()))
313	    {
314	        if(appData.ignoreSwitchPress)
315	        {
316	            /* This means the key press is in progress */
317	            if(appData.sofEventHasOccurred)
318	            {
319	                /* A timer event has occurred. Update the debounce timer */
320	                appData.switchDebounceTimer ++;
321	                appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
322	                
323	                if (USB_DEVICE_ActiveSpeedGet(appData.deviceHandle) == USB_SPEED_FULL)
324	                {
325	                    appData.debounceCount = APP_USB_SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_COUNT_FS;
326	                }
327	                else if (USB_DEVICE_ActiveSpeedGet(appData.deviceHandle) == USB_SPEED_HIGH)
328	                {
329	                    appData.debounceCount = APP_USB_SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_COUNT_HS;
330	                }
331	                if(appData.switchDebounceTimer == appData.debounceCount)
332	                {
333	                    /* Indicate that we have valid switch press. The switch is
334	                     * pressed flag will be cleared by the application tasks
335	                     * routine. We should be ready for the next key press.*/
336	                    appData.isSwitchPressed = true;
337	                    appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
338	                    appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
339	                }
340	            }
341	        }
342	        else
343	        {
344	            /* We have a fresh key press */
345	            appData.ignoreSwitchPress = true;
346	            appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
347	        }
348	    }
349	    else
350	    {
351	        /* No key press. Reset all the indicators. */
352	        appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
353	        appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
354	        appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
355	    }
356	}

358	/*****************************************************
359	 * This function is called in every step of the
360	 * application state machine.
361	 *****************************************************/
362	
363	bool APP_StateReset(void)
364	{
365	    /* This function returns true if the device
366	     * was reset  */
367	
368	    bool retVal;
369	
370	    if(appData.isConfigured == false)
371	    {
372	        appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION;
373	        appData.readTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
374	        appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
375	        appData.isReadComplete = true;
376	        appData.isWriteComplete = true;
377	        retVal = true;
378	    }
379	    else
380	    {
381	        retVal = false;
382	    }
383	
384	    return(retVal);
385	}

396	
397	  Remarks:
398	    See prototype in app.h.
399	 */
400	
401	void APP_Initialize(void)
402	{
403	    /* Place the App state machine in its initial state. */
404	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
405	    
406	    /* Device Layer Handle  */
407	    appData.deviceHandle = USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID ;
408	
409	    /* Device configured status */
410	    appData.isConfigured = false;
411	
412	    /* Initial get line coding state */
413	    appData.getLineCodingData.dwDTERate = 9600;
414	    appData.getLineCodingData.bParityType = 0;
415	    appData.getLineCodingData.bCharFormat= 0; 
416	    appData.getLineCodingData.bDataBits = 8;
417	
418	    /* Read Transfer Handle */
419	    appData.readTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
420	
421	    /* Write Transfer Handle */
422	    appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
423	
424	    /* Initialize the read complete flag */
425	    appData.isReadComplete = true;
426	
427	    /*Initialize the write complete flag*/
428	    appData.isWriteComplete = true;
429	
430	    /* Initialize Ignore switch flag */
431	    appData.ignoreSwitchPress = false;
432	
433	    /* Reset the switch debounce counter */
434	    appData.switchDebounceTimer = 0;
435	
436	    /* Reset other flags */
437	    appData.sofEventHasOccurred = false;
438	    
439	    /* To know status of Switch */
440	    appData.isSwitchPressed = false;
441	
442	    /* Set up the read buffer */
443	    appData.cdcReadBuffer = &cdcReadBuffer[0];
444	
445	    /* Set up the read buffer */
446	    appData.cdcWriteBuffer = &cdcWriteBuffer[0];       
447	}

449	
450	/******************************************************************************
451	  Function:
452	    void APP_Tasks(void)
453	
454	  Remarks:
455	    See prototype in app.h.
456	 */
457	
458	void APP_Tasks(void)
459	{
460	    /* Update the application state machine based
461	     * on the current state */
462	    int i;
463	    
464	    switch(appData.state)
465	    {
466	        case APP_STATE_INIT:
467	
468	            /* Open the device layer */
469	            appData.deviceHandle = USB_DEVICE_Open( USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0, DRV_IO_INTENT_READWRITE );
470	
471	            if(appData.deviceHandle != USB_DEVICE_HANDLE_INVALID)
472	            {
473	                /* Register a callback with device layer to get event notification (for end point 0) */
474	                USB_DEVICE_EventHandlerSet(appData.deviceHandle, APP_USBDeviceEventHandler, 0);
475	
476	                appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION;
477	            }
478	            else
479	            {
480	                /* The Device Layer is not ready to be opened. We should try
481	                 * again later. */
482	            }
483	
484	            break;
485	
486	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_CONFIGURATION:
487	
488	            /* Check if the device was configured */
489	            if(appData.isConfigured)
490	            {
491	                /* If the device is configured then lets start reading */
492	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ;
493	            }
494	            
495	            break;
496	
497	        case APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ:
498	
499	            if(APP_StateReset())
500	            {
501	                break;
502	            }
503	
504	            /* If a read is complete, then schedule a read
505	             * else wait for the current read to complete */
506	
507	            appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_READ_COMPLETE;
508	            if(appData.isReadComplete == true)
509	            {
510	                appData.isReadComplete = false;
511	                appData.readTransferHandle =  USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
512	
513	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read (USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
514	                        &appData.readTransferHandle, appData.cdcReadBuffer,
515	                        APP_READ_BUFFER_SIZE);
516	                
517	                if(appData.readTransferHandle == USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID)
518	                {
519	                    appData.state = APP_STATE_ERROR;
520	                    break;
521	                }
522	            }
523	
524	            break;
525	
526	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_READ_COMPLETE:
527	        case APP_STATE_CHECK_SWITCH_PRESSED:
528	
529	            if(APP_StateReset())
530	            {
531	                break;
532	            }
533	
534	            APP_ProcessSwitchPress();
535	
536	            /* Check if a character was received or a switch was pressed.
537	             * The isReadComplete flag gets updated in the CDC event handler. */
538	
539	            if(appData.isReadComplete || appData.isSwitchPressed)
540	            {
541	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_WRITE;
542	            }
543	
544	            break;
545	
546	
547	        case APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_WRITE:
548	
549	            if(APP_StateReset())
550	            {
551	                break;
552	            }
553	
554	            /* Setup the write */
555	
556	            appData.writeTransferHandle = USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE_INVALID;
557	            appData.isWriteComplete = false;
558	            appData.state = APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_WRITE_COMPLETE;
559	
560	            if(appData.isSwitchPressed)
561	            {
562	                /* If the switch was pressed, then send the switch prompt*/
563	                appData.isSwitchPressed = false;
564	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
565	                        &appData.writeTransferHandle, switchPromptUSB, sizeof(switchPromptUSB),
566	                        USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
567	            }
568	            else
569	            {
570	                /* Else echo each received character by adding 1 */
571	                for(i = 0; i < appData.numBytesRead; i++)
572	                {
573	                    if((appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] != 0x0A) && (appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] != 0x0D))
574	                    {
575	                        appData.cdcWriteBuffer[i] = appData.cdcReadBuffer[i] + 1;
576	                    }
577	                }
578	                USB_DEVICE_CDC_Write(USB_DEVICE_CDC_INDEX_0,
579	                        &appData.writeTransferHandle,
580	                        appData.cdcWriteBuffer, appData.numBytesRead,
581	                        USB_DEVICE_CDC_TRANSFER_FLAGS_DATA_COMPLETE);
582	            }
583	
584	            break;
585	
586	        case APP_STATE_WAIT_FOR_WRITE_COMPLETE:
587	
588	            if(APP_StateReset())
589	            {
590	                break;
591	            }
592	
593	            /* Check if a character was sent. The isWriteComplete
594	             * flag gets updated in the CDC event handler */
595	
596	            if(appData.isWriteComplete == true)
597	            {
598	                appData.state = APP_STATE_SCHEDULE_READ;
599	            }
600	
601	            break;
602	
603	        case APP_STATE_ERROR:
604	        default:
605	            
606	            break;
607	    }
608	}
609	
610	/*******************************************************************************
611	 End of File
612	 */
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:38:45Z)**_

I read the UDPHS driver and the device-layer event mapping. The natural mechanism for cold-boot is:

1. `DRV_USB_UDPHS_Tasks` polls `vbusComparator` on every tick.
2. While `pEventCallBack == NULL` (no handler registered yet), the entire VBUS-check block is skipped — including the `vbusLevel = current` update at [drv_usb_udphs.c:261](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/driver/usb/udphs/src/drv_usb_udphs.c#L261). So `vbusLevel` stays `INVALID`.
3. When we register our handler, the next tick should detect `INVALID → VALID` and fire SESSION_VALID, which the device layer maps to `POWER_DETECTED` (they share the same enum value).

That should "just work" — but it doesn't. Most likely cause: the host PC saw a transient pull-up assertion during early boot (or saw nothing across several tries) and gave up retrying enumeration. Hot-plug always works because it's a fresh attach edge.

Cleanest fix: explicitly detach first, then attach, to force a clean attach edge the host will see. This also moots the question of "did POWER_DETECTED fire or not" because we drive the pull-up unconditionally on cold-boot.

Forced a clean detach→100ms→attach edge in `PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize`. The previous fix gated on `USB_VBUS_SENSE_Get()` — if that pin returns 0 unexpectedly, or if the host had already given up after a brief boot-time pull-up assertion, the conditional Attach was a no-op. The unconditional detach-then-attach gives the host a fresh arrival edge regardless of VBUS-sense state.

If this still doesn't enumerate at cold boot, the next thing I'd check is whether the device layer's `usbDeviceState` is `ATTACHED` at the time we call Attach — if SESSION_VALID never fired (handler-registration race), the device layer thinks VBUS is invalid and may ignore the Attach. In that case the fix would be to pump `USB_DEVICE_Tasks`/wait for `s_is_configured` to flip, and re-Attach if it stays false past a timeout.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:41:05Z)**_

Right now only the drain task itself emits records — no producers are wired yet. So with the device enumerated and a terminal opened on it (e.g. `screen /dev/cu.usbmodemXXX 921600`), you should see:

- **One `PERF_REC_SESSION`** at startup with `timer_freq_hz` and `schema_version=1`. **Caveat:** this is emitted once, right after Initialize. If your terminal opens the port after that, you miss it (DTR wasn't asserted yet, so the WriteFramed early-returns).
- **One `PERF_REC_DROP`** every second forever (zeros until a producer drops something).

Both come out as raw binary, framed as `55 4D 52 56 <len_lo> <len_hi> <payload> <crc_lo> <crc_hi>`. A terminal will print garbage; that's expected. To see structure, dump bytes with `xxd` or `python -c "import serial; s=serial.Serial('/dev/cu.usbmodemXXX',921600); print(s.read(200).hex())"`.

Two things worth fixing while you're here:

1. **Re-emit `SESSION` on the configured edge** so opening the terminal mid-session always sees a fresh schema record. One-line change in `cdc_event_handler`'s CONFIGURED case (or device handler).
2. **Wire the first producer** (e.g. `PerfLog_EmitStamp(VIDEO_PUBLISH, ...)` at [video.c:213](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/video.c#L213)) so you see real per-frame traffic instead of just the 1 Hz heartbeat.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:44:21Z)**_

Quick answer on baud: **no, baud is meaningless on direct USB CDC.** The `dwDTERate` in line-coding is just a value the host sends and we ignore — it would matter if we were bridging to a real UART, which we aren't. Underlying USB bulk transfers always run at the link speed (~5–15 MB/s sustained for HS bulk). Pick any baud in the terminal; same bandwidth either way.

Now #1 — emit SESSION on DTR rising edge so reconnecting a terminal always gets a fresh schema record.
