183	|---|---|---|
184	| UART 115.2 kBd (console) | ~11 KB/s | in use (FLEXCOM4) |
185	| UART 921.6 kBd | ~92 KB/s | EDBG bridge cap |
186	| UART 3 Mbd (FLEXCOM max) | ~300 KB/s | unlikely through bridges |
187	| USB CDC ACM (HS device, class-stack overhead) | ~5–15 MB/s | device peripheral unused |
188	| USB Bulk (HS device, custom class) | ~30–40 MB/s | needs custom host-side reader |
189	| SDMMC Class-10 via FAT32 | ~5–10 MB/s | already planned for §4.6 keyframes |
190	| SDMMC UHS-I | ~25–50 MB/s | bus capable, FS overhead bites |
191	| GMAC Ethernet UDP | ~30–60 MB/s | GMAC unused |
192	| GMAC Ethernet TCP | ~10–20 MB/s | GMAC unused |
193	
194	**What fits where**
195	
196	- **State-only (9 KB/s)** fits everywhere including the console UART — no new transport needed if the goal is just "trace detector + timing + actuator decisions per frame."
197	- **ROI patches 60 Hz (~1 MB/s)** preserves everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples; streams comfortably over USB CDC, fits an entire song on SD with room to spare.
198	- **1 keyframe/s + dense state (~1 MB/s)** is what spec §4.6 already commits to, fits any modern SD card, and survives over USB CDC or Ethernet.
199	- **Full 60 Hz (62 MB/s)** doesn't fit any transport sustained, *and* a 5-minute song at that rate is 18.7 GB — DOA.
200	
201	**Implication for what to build next.** The scoping confirms the spec's existing reference-data architecture is the right place to start; perf-logging is a *consumer* of the same infrastructure, not a separate path. Next step is to figure out which questions the perf log actually has to answer (latency attribution? frame-rate stability? detector confidence over time? actuator jitter?) and pick the minimum stream that answers them. State-only might already be enough for the latency/jitter questions; ROI patches are the cheapest way to get "did the detector see what I think it saw" replayability.
202	
203	### 2026-05-21 — cv_marvin_v1 threshold tuning + timing-pipeline tweaks
204	
205	First end-to-end gameplay test on hardware. Detector was firing roughly random presses at first; resolved by reading actual signal values rather than guessing.
206	
207	**Visibility added:**
208	- State-reactive overlay in `cv_marvin_v1.c` — position rings always; filled center dot when `s_pressed[i]` (white in the hold ring) or `s_edge_active[i]` (fret-color in the edge ring). Lets the user watch chatter live: stable note → steady dot for hold duration; strum window → flash on the edge dot.
209	- Periodic ~2 Hz log dump (`frame_count % 30 == 0`) showing per-fret `hold_dist / edge_dist / P E` flags.
210	
211	**Diagnosis (Easy mode, no real B/O presses):**
212	- Idle hold floor sits at 22–48 across all five frets, **not** the limited-range 16 floor `display_path.md` would suggest. Playfield-glow at the sample sites is well above the limited-range black point.
213	- Real-press hold spikes to 67–186, leaving a clean gap above the noise ceiling.
214	- Hold threshold 50 with release-frac 0.6 (release=30) was *below* the idle floor for Y and B → those frets latched permanently pressed and never released.
215	- Edge threshold 50 was at the peak of real-edge signal (40–53), almost never tripping. timing_pipeline only uses `pressed` today, so dead edges aren't the chatter source — but lowering edge threshold lets `s_edge_active` overlay flicker meaningfully again.
216	
217	**Settings landed (in `cv_marvin_v1.c`):**
218	- `CV_HOLD_THRESH`: 50 → **100** (after iterating 65 → 80 → 100; 100 cleanly above noise across all frets, real presses still spike to 150–186).
219	- `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`: 0.60 → **0.78** (release ≈ 78 — above the noise ceiling, comfortably below real-press floor).
220	- `CV_EDGE_THRESH`: 50 → **25** (gives the overlay an honest edge indicator without affecting pipeline behavior).
221	- Sample coords nudged 1 px on G/R/Y/B/O edges + B hold for slightly cleaner alignment.
222	
223	**Performance:** Expert-mode play is now quite good — clean note recognition, fret hold-through across consecutive same-fret notes confirmed by trace through `process_releases` (release suppressed when the next chord-commit's `note_q` entry already needs the bit, within `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS − TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS = 190 ms` of detector-release-to-detector-press).
224	
225	**Timing-pipeline tweaks** (Greg's hand-edits): `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` 50→25, `TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS` 20→30, `TP_FIFO_CAP` 16→32.
226	
227	Open question added above: `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220 ms` is Expert-tuned; Easy/Medium/Hard may need different values because note travel time differs.
228	
229	### 2026-05-21 — Manual fretboard-control producer + timing-pipeline gate
230	
231	Stood up the actuator-side half of a basic on-device manual-control surface — primarily for game-menu navigation (start a song, advance menus, hit pause) where single-finger input is the natural shape. UI half waits on a Microchip Graphics Composer regen.
232	
233	What landed:
234	
235	- `actuator/manual_control.{h,c}` — second producer of `FretboardLink_Send`, alongside `timing_pipeline`. Internal state: `s_fret_mask` (bits 0..4) and `s_strum_mask` (bits 5..6). Public API: `Initialize / SetEnabled / IsEnabled / SetFret / SetStrum`. Both fret and strum are momentary — held while the UI button is down, cleared on release. `recompute_and_send` only calls `FretboardLink_Send` while enabled.
236	- `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool)` — output gate on `publish_mask`. Pipeline still advances internal state when gated, so the next `advance()` (≤ `TP_TICK_MS` = 5 ms) after re-enable republishes the right mask without a stale frame.
237	- `ManualControl_SetEnabled` ordering: enter manual mode = gate timing pipeline first, zero local state, send `0`, set enabled flag (so a stale pipeline frame can't race a manual zero on the wire); exit = clear enabled flag, zero state, send `0`, ungate pipeline.
238	- App init wires `ManualControl_Initialize()` after `TimingPipeline_Initialize()`. No Legato dependency at this stage.
239	- `cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake` adds `manual_control.c` and `ui/manual_input.c`.
240	
241	UI half landed same session after Greg ran the Composer regen. Composer added 8 buttons to `Screen0` — `Screen0_Button_Manual_{Green,Red,Yellow,Blue,Orange,StrumDown,StrumUp,Enable}` — plus 15 extern `event_Screen0_Button_Manual_*` handler declarations the application must define. The binding shape came out simpler than the plan called for: `screenShow_Screen0` itself calls `setPressedEventCallback` / `setReleasedEventCallback` with those extern symbols, so the linker resolves them and **no `ManualInput_Bind()` walk is needed**. `ui/manual_input.c` is just the 15 function bodies forwarding to `ManualControl_SetFret / Strum / SetEnabled`. The originally planned `APP_Tasks` poll-loop for null widget pointers is moot — `APP_Tasks` keeps the existing `vTaskDelete(NULL)`.
242	
243	Strum buttons are momentary, not one-shot: holding the strum button keeps the fretboard's strum line asserted, which Guitar Hero / Rock Band menus interpret as auto-repeat scrolling — the primary use case for this surface. Gameplay-path strums still pulse correctly because they go through `timing_pipeline`, which has its own `TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS` one-shot. The Enable button is `setToggleable(LE_TRUE)` with only `OnReleased`; both the widget and `ManualControl` default to off, so a simple `SetEnabled(!IsEnabled())` flip stays in sync without querying the widget's toggle state.
244	
245	Plan agent flagged two real blockers worth recording: (1) Legato's input pipeline routes each touch to one focus widget — multi-finger momentary chords aren't possible without a custom dispatcher, so the model is single-finger only; (2) the lazy widget-pointer init means any code that walks the `Screen0_*` pointers has to run post-`screenShow_Screen0` — moot here because Composer does the wiring itself, but still true for any future shim that needs to read or modify widget state.
246	
247	Decision-log entries above cover the producer-as-peer pattern, the Composer-driven UI choice, and the single-finger input model.
248	
249	**Bring-up over the wire.** Marvin enumerates the EDBG CDC and `FretboardLink_Send` round-trips cleanly through the queue, but the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 wasn't receiving anything. Two real fixes:
250	
251	1. **EDBG bridge needs DTR raised.** The bridge holds its UART TX idle until the host asserts DTR. Added `USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet` with `dtr=1, carrier=1` to `open_cdc()` after the existing `LineCodingSet(115200)`. Baud matters here — fretboard runs a real UART at 115200, not USB-CDC-ignored.
252	2. **Control-pipe completion handlers run from ISR context.** First instrumented attempt logged `LOG_INFO` directly from the new `SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE` / `SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE` event cases; system froze mid-print. Microchip's CDC stack dispatches *all* class events from ISR (the existing `WRITE_COMPLETE` case already uses `*FromISR` primitives — that was the precedent). `log_vprintf` takes a mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`, illegal from ISR. Stripped both the diagnostic logging and the latch infrastructure once the link was confirmed functional. Captured for the journal because it's a recurring shape: any new event-handler case in this stack must stay strictly ISR-safe.
253	
254	### 2026-05-20 — USB CDC host attach: EDBG composite enumerates, CDC class driver now binds
255	
256	Picked up where the prior session left off — VBUS not asserting, no device detected. Closed both halves.
257	
258	**VBUS.** MCC's `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` callback is wired in the host driver but the host stack never invokes it on this build. Asserted the two VBUS GPIOs (`VBUS_AH_PC27_PowerEnable_Set` / `VBUS_AH_PC31_PowerEnable_Set`) directly from `APP_Initialize` ahead of consumer init and `USB_HOST_BusEnable`. EDBG immediately enumerates.
259	
260	**Class-driver binding.** Enumeration succeeded but the CDC attach handler never fired. Added per-interface descriptor logging inside `F_USB_HOST_UpdateDeviceTask` to see what was actually being matched. Output revealed VID `0x03EB` PID `0x2175` — an EDBG composite with five interfaces: HID/CMSIS-DAP, CDC ACM IAD pair (comm + data), vendor, MSC. The IAD passed TPL match and got assigned to the CDC driver, but the CDC instance still flipped to `STATE_ERROR` without our app-level handler ever seeing the attach.
261	
262	Root cause was inside Microchip's CDC class driver: `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` (both single-interface and IAD paths) requires the comm interface to declare `bInterfaceProtocol == USB_CDC_PROTOCOL_AT_V250` (`0x01`). EDBG declares `0x00` (none) — functionally identical CDC ACM in practice; Linux/macOS accept either. The TPL/IAD pre-check passes (TPL wildcards subclass/protocol), the CDC driver gets the interface group, then immediately rejects it on the AT-V.250 check. The interrupt pipe never opens, the instance errors out, and the app-level listener stays silent.
263	
264	Fix: relaxed both checks to `(AT_V250 || NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. After the patch the FBL log shows `CDC device attached, handle opened` and `c=Y` heartbeat as expected. Logged as patch #7 in the MCC re-apply list.
265	
266	Also tested a hypothesis from the prior session that `USB_HOST_Initialize` had to run *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits. With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. Backed out the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Decision-log entry above.
267	
268	Diagnostic instrumentation stripped at the end of the session: the per-interface descriptor dump and enumeration state-change logger in `usb_host.c`, and the periodic OHCI/EHCI register heartbeat in `fretboard_link.c`. What remains on disk: the two `usb_host_cdc.c` protocol-relaxation lines (patch #7), the app-level VBUS asserts, and a minimal `USB_HOST_EVENT` printf so future host-stack drama still surfaces in the log.
269	
270	Next session: revisit timing-pipeline behavior end-to-end now that the actuator wire is live.
271	
272	### 2026-05-20 — Hardware bring-up after USB CDC host regen: TC358743 wedge resolved
273	
274	First on-target test after the M2 actuator path landed. Symptoms: video stream not starting, USB ports unpowered, FBL heartbeat firing with `connected=N`. Boot stopped after `TC358743: probe starting`.
275	
276	Root cause: the USB MCC regen reordered SYS_Initialize so `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize` ran *after* `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize`. With AIC initialized late, the FLEXCOM6 interrupt vector wasn't owned by the AIC when the first I²C transfer ran; `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` blocked forever waiting for an ISR that never fired. FBL stayed alive because it's pure FreeRTOS — no peripheral interrupt dependency.
277	
278	Fix: reverted SYS_Initialize order so MMU/AIC/WDT-disable run before TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC. Display + capture came back on first boot. Logged as patch #6 in the MCC re-apply list above.

60	/* ─── HEO scaler helper ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

62	/* HEO scaler factor is 12.20 fixed-point, factor = (src / dst) << 20.
63	 * 1.0 (= 0x100000) means 1:1, no scaling. Mirrors plib_xlcdc.c's
64	 * static CALC_SCALING_FACT. */
65	static uint32_t scaler_factor(uint32_t src, uint32_t dst)
66	{
67	    if (dst == 0u) { return 0x100000u; }
68	    return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)src << 20) / dst);
69	}

71	/* ─── HEO bind / unbind ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
72	
73	/* Point HEO at the capture buffer at (x, y) sized dst_w × dst_h. If the
74	 * destination size matches the source size, the HEO scaler stays at its
75	 * 1.0 factor (effectively bypassed). Otherwise the bilinear scaler is
76	 * engaged. BASE DISCEN is set to the destination rect so BASE skips DMA
77	 * for the area HEO covers (§44.6.4.7). */
78	static void lcd_bind(uint32_t src_w, uint32_t src_h,
79	                     uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
80	{
81	    if (x + dst_w > LCD_PANEL_W || y + dst_h > LCD_PANEL_H)
82	    {
83	        LOG_WARN("VIDEO: window %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) exceeds panel %ux%u; skipping bind\r\n",
84	                 (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
85	                 (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y,
86	                 LCD_PANEL_W, LCD_PANEL_H);
87	        return;
88	    }
89	
90	    /* Initial HEO address: the latest completed buffer if we have one,
91	     * else fall back to the framebuffer base. The on_frame_done IRQ
92	     * re-points HEO at every subsequent completed buffer, so this is
93	     * the seed that holds for at most one frame-time before the first
94	     * IRQ overwrites it. */
95	    uint32_t initial_addr = s_latest_buffer;
96	    if (initial_addr == 0u) { initial_addr = ISC_Capture_GetBufferAddress(); }
97	
98	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
99	    XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO,
100	                               XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_888_PACKED, false);
101	    XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, initial_addr, false);
102	    XLCDC_SetLayerXStride(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, 0u, false);
103	    XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYPos(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, x, y, false);
104	
105	    /* Display rect (HEOCFG3) and source-memory rect (HEOCFG4) are the same
106	     * for 1:1 and differ for scaling. Write them directly — XLCDC_Set-
107	     * LayerWindowXYSize writes both registers to the same value, which is
108	     * only correct for 1:1. */
109	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG3 = LCDC_HEOCFG3_XSIZE(dst_w - 1u)
110	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG3_YSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
111	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG4 = LCDC_HEOCFG4_XMEMSIZE(src_w - 1u)
112	                             | LCDC_HEOCFG4_YMEMSIZE(src_h - 1u);
113	
114	    bool scaling = (dst_w != src_w) || (dst_h != src_h);
115	    if (scaling)
116	    {
117	        uint32_t hf = scaler_factor(src_w, dst_w);
118	        uint32_t vf = scaler_factor(src_h, dst_h);
119	
120	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(1)
121	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(1)
122	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(1)
123	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(1);
124	        /* Bicubic luminance + bicubic chrominance, both planes. Mirrors
125	         * MCC's surface-set path — best image quality for video. */
126	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG30 = LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYCFG(1)
127	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSYBICU(1)
128	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCCFG(1)
129	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG30_VXSCBICU(1);
130	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG31 = LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYCFG(1)
131	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSYBICU(1)
132	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCCFG(1)
133	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG31_HXSCBICU(1);
134	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG24 = LCDC_HEOCFG24_VXSYFACT(vf);
135	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG25 = LCDC_HEOCFG25_VXSCFACT(vf);
136	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG26 = LCDC_HEOCFG26_HXSYFACT(hf);
137	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG27 = LCDC_HEOCFG27_HXSCFACT(hf);
138	    }
139	    else
140	    {
141	        /* Disable scaler — matches MCC's HEO-setup defaults. */
142	        XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_HEOCFG23 = LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSYEN(0)
143	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_VXSCEN(0)
144	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSYEN(0)
145	                                  | LCDC_HEOCFG23_HXSCEN(0);
146	    }

148	    /* §44.6.4.7 — discard BASE DMA in the destination rect. HEO with MCC's
149	     * default SFACTC=4 (A0×As) / DFACTC=6 (1−A0×As) reaches 100% opacity
150	     * for RGB_888_PACKED (no per-pixel alpha → As sourced from A0=255),
151	     * so BASE pixels in this rect are blended out. DISCEN tells the BASE
152	     * channel to skip fetching them. */
153	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG5 = LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCXPOS(x)
154	                              | LCDC_BASECFG5_DISCYPOS(y);

156	                              | LCDC_BASECFG6_DISCYSIZE(dst_h - 1u);
157	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 |= LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;

160	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, true, true);
161	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
162	
163	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: HEO bound src %lux%lu → dst %lux%lu @(%lu,%lu) %s\r\n",
164	             (unsigned long)src_w, (unsigned long)src_h,
165	             (unsigned long)dst_w, (unsigned long)dst_h,
166	             (unsigned long)x, (unsigned long)y,
167	             scaling ? "scaled" : "1:1");
168	}

171	static void lcd_unbind(void)
172	{
173	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);

178	/* ─── Frame-done ISR (runs in IRQ context) ─────────────────────────────── */
179	
180	static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
181	                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
182	                          uintptr_t ctx)
183	{
184	    (void)ctx;
185	
186	    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;
187	
188	    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
189	     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
190	     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
191	     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
192	     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
193	    if (s_display_bound)
194	    {
195	        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
196	    }
197	
198	    Video_FrameInfo info =
199	    {
200	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
201	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
202	        .width           = s_src_w,
203	        .height          = s_src_h,
204	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
205	    };
206	
207	    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
208	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
209	    {
210	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
211	        if (q != NULL)
212	        {
213	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
214	        }
215	    }
216	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
217	}

219	/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
220	
221	static bool capture_arm(void)
222	{
223	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
224	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
225	
226	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
227	    s_src_w = w;
228	    s_src_h = h;
229	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
230	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
231	    {
232	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
233	        return false;
234	    }
235	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
236	    return true;
237	}
238	
239	static void capture_disarm(void)
240	{
241	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
242	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
243	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
244	}
245	
246	/* Bind/unbind display from current intent + most-recent source size +
247	 * caller-set window. A zero-sized window means the app hasn't set one
248	 * yet — silently skip the bind in that case rather than emit a malformed
249	 * HEO geometry; DisplayShow without a prior SetWindow is a no-op. */
250	static void display_apply(void)
251	{
252	    window_t w = s_window;
253	    bool window_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
254	    bool source_valid = (s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u);
255	    bool want = s_display_shown && source_valid && window_valid;
256	
257	    if (want && !s_display_bound)
258	    {
259	        lcd_bind(s_src_w, s_src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
260	        s_display_bound = true;
261	    }
262	    else if (!want && s_display_bound)
263	    {
264	        lcd_unbind();
265	        s_display_bound = false;
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* Each tick: align current chain state (capture armed / display bound) to
270	 * the user's intent flags, given the current source-lock state. */
271	static void reconcile(void)
272	{
273	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
274	
275	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
276	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
277	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
278	    {
279	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
280	    }
281	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
282	    {
283	        capture_disarm();
284	        s_capture_armed = false;
285	    }
286	
287	    /* Display: shown iff intent + we have a source size to work with. The
288	     * source size is captured at arm time and persists across capture
289	     * teardown so the user can leave HEO bound on a stale frame. */
290	    display_apply();
291	}

293	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
294	
295	static void video_task(void *param)
296	{
297	    (void)param;
298	
299	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
300	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge,
301	     * backlight, and parks the panel in UI-only mode. */
302	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
303	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
304	    TC358743_Initialize();
305	    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
306	    lcd_unbind();
307	
308	    for (;;)
309	    {
310	        TC358743_Tasks();
311	        reconcile();
312	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
313	    }
314	}

11	 * publishing at 60 Hz and the stub consumer draining every tick, depth 8
12	 * absorbs a few ms of consumer stall without dropping records. Bump when
13	 * adding more producers or a slower consumer. */
14	#define DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH       8u
15	
16	#define DRAIN_TASK_STACK_WORDS   512u
17	#define DRAIN_TASK_PRIORITY      1u
18	#define DRAIN_LOG_INTERVAL_MS    1000u

30	static void drain_task(void *param)
31	{
32	    (void)param;
33	
34	    TickType_t window_start = xTaskGetTickCount();
35	    uint32_t   window_count = 0;
36	
37	    for (;;)
38	    {
39	        detector_state_t state;
40	        if (xQueueReceive(s_bus_queue, &state, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE)
41	        {
42	            continue;
43	        }
44	        window_count++;
45	
46	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
47	        if ((uint32_t)(now - window_start) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(DRAIN_LOG_INTERVAL_MS))
48	        {
49	            LOG_INFO("DETECTOR: bus drain %lu records/s (last epoch=%lu id=%u)\r\n",
50	                     (unsigned long)window_count,
51	                     (unsigned long)state.frame_epoch,
52	                     (unsigned)state.detector_id);
53	            window_start = now;
54	            window_count = 0;
55	        }
56	    }
57	}

46	 * request completes. Used to serialize the LineCodingSet ->
47	 * ControlLineStateSet pair in open_cdc; the host stack will silently
48	 * drop the second request if it's issued before the first settles. */
49	static SemaphoreHandle_t s_ctrl_done;
50	static StaticSemaphore_t s_ctrl_done_buf;
51	
52	#define FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS     500u

54	static volatile USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ    s_cdc_obj_pending = (USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ)0;
55	static volatile bool                s_cdc_obj_valid;

59	
60	static USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONSE cdc_event_handler(USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE handle,
61	                                                    USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT event,
62	                                                    void *eventData,
63	                                                    uintptr_t context)
64	{
65	    (void)handle;
66	    (void)context;
67	
68	    switch (event)
69	    {
70	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE:
71	        {
72	            const USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_WRITE_COMPLETE_DATA *d = eventData;
73	            s_last_write_result = d->result;
74	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
75	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
76	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
77	            break;
78	        }
79	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE:
80	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_ACM_SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE:
81	        {
82	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
83	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_ctrl_done, &hpw);
84	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
85	            break;
86	        }
87	        case USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_DEVICE_DETACHED:
88	        {
89	            s_connected = false;
90	            /* Wake any pending writer so it observes the detach instead
91	             * of waiting out the timeout. */
92	            BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
93	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_write_done, &hpw);
94	            portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
95	            break;
96	        }
97	        default:

99	    }
100	    return USB_HOST_CDC_EVENT_RESPONE_NONE;
101	}

103	static void cdc_attach_handler(USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ obj, uintptr_t context)
104	{
105	    (void)context;
106	    /* Hand the object to the link task; opening the device must happen
107	     * outside the host stack callback. */

111	
112	static void close_cdc(void)
113	{
114	    if (s_cdc_handle != USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID)
115	    {
116	        USB_HOST_CDC_Close(s_cdc_handle);
117	        s_cdc_handle = USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID;
118	    }
119	    s_connected = false;

121	
122	static bool open_cdc(USB_HOST_CDC_OBJ obj)
123	{
124	    USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE h = USB_HOST_CDC_Open(obj);
125	    if (h == USB_HOST_CDC_HANDLE_INVALID) { return false; }
126	
127	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_EventHandlerSet(h, cdc_event_handler, 0u) != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
128	    {
129	        USB_HOST_CDC_Close(h);
130	        return false;
131	    }
132	
133	    static USB_CDC_LINE_CODING line_coding =
134	    {
135	        .dwDTERate   = FBL_BAUDRATE,
136	        .bCharFormat = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_STOP_1_BIT,
137	        .bParityType = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_PARITY_NONE,
138	        .bDataBits   = USB_CDC_LINE_CODING_DATA_8_BIT,
139	    };
140	    USB_HOST_CDC_REQUEST_HANDLE rh;
141	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
142	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_LineCodingSet(h, &rh, &line_coding) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
143	    {
144	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
145	    }
146	
147	    /* Some EDBG-CDC firmwares hold the bridge UART idle until the host
148	     * raises DTR. Assert DTR + carrier so the bridge actually drives
149	     * bytes out to the fretboard MCU's SERCOM1 RX. */
150	    static USB_CDC_CONTROL_LINE_STATE cls = { .dtr = 1u, .carrier = 1u };
151	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, 0);
152	    if (USB_HOST_CDC_ACM_ControlLineStateSet(h, &rh, &cls) == USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
153	    {
154	        (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_ctrl_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_CTRL_TIMEOUT_MS));
155	    }

157	    s_cdc_handle = h;
158	    s_connected  = true;
159	    LOG_INFO("FBL: CDC device attached, handle opened\r\n");

163	static bool send_one_byte(uint8_t mask)

170	    /* Drain any prior signal so we wait for *this* write's completion. */
171	    (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, 0);
172	
173	    USB_HOST_CDC_TRANSFER_HANDLE th;
174	    USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT r = USB_HOST_CDC_Write(s_cdc_handle, &th, &tx_byte, 1u);
175	    if (r != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
176	    {
177	        LOG_WARN("FBL: CDC_Write rejected, r=%d\r\n", (int)r);
178	        return false;
179	    }
180	
181	    if (xSemaphoreTake(s_write_done, pdMS_TO_TICKS(FBL_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS)) != pdTRUE)
182	    {
183	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write timeout, marking detached\r\n");
184	        close_cdc();
185	        return false;
186	    }
187	    if (s_last_write_result != USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_SUCCESS)
188	    {
189	        LOG_WARN("FBL: write completion err=%d\r\n", (int)s_last_write_result);
190	        return false;
191	    }
192	    return true;
193	}

232	                                     s_cmd_queue_storage,

243	     * stack only matches a class driver if its attach handler is in place
244	     * when enumeration completes. App-level USB_HOST_BusEnable runs right
245	     * after this init returns. */
246	    (void)USB_HOST_CDC_AttachEventHandlerSet(cdc_attach_handler, 0u);
247

249	                            "FretLink",
250	                            FBL_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
251	                            NULL,

253	                            s_task_stack,
254	                            &s_task_tcb);

262	void FretboardLink_Send(uint8_t mask)
263	{
264	    if (s_cmd_queue == NULL) { return; }
265	    uint8_t v = (uint8_t)(mask & 0x7F);
266	    /* Overwrite is strictly latest-wins: a newer producer's mask replaces
267	     * any unsent older one — keeps a stalled USB write from accumulating
268	     * stale chord state. */
269	    (void)xQueueOverwrite(s_cmd_queue, &v);

146	/* Edge derivation:

151	 * a quality gate; left untouched here. */
152	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
153	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
154	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
155	{
156	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
157	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
158	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
159	
160	    bool first = !s_press_count_seen;
161	
162	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
163	    {
164	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
165	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
166	
167	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
168	        uint16_t pc = state->fret[i].confidence;  /* placeholder slot */
169	        (void)pc;

174	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
175	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
176	
177	        s_prev_press_count[i] = state->fret[i].confidence;
178	    }
179	
180	    if (first) { s_press_count_seen = true; }
181	
182	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
183	    *presses_mask  = pm;
184	    *releases_mask = rm;
185	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
186	}

188	static void chord_commit(void)
189	{
190	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
191	    {
192	        s_chord_open = false;
193	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
194	        return;
195	    }
196	
197	    uint32_t assert_at = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS - TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
198	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
199	
200	    if (!strum_q_empty())
201	    {
202	        uint8_t  last_idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + TP_FIFO_CAP - 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
203	        uint32_t earliest = s_strum_q[last_idx].strum_at_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
204	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0)
205	        {
206	            assert_at = earliest;
207	            strum_at  = assert_at + TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
208	        }
209	    }
210	
211	    pending_note_t  n = { .assert_at_ms = assert_at, .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
212	    pending_strum_t s = { .strum_at_ms  = strum_at,  .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
213	    note_q_push(n);
214	    strum_q_push(s);
215	
216	    s_chord_open = false;
217	    s_chord_mask = 0u;
218	}

220	static void process_notes(void)

225	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - n->assert_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
226	
227	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
228	        {
229	            uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
230	            bool need = (n->fret_mask & bit) != 0u;
231	            bool have = (s_frets_active & bit) != 0u;
232	            if (need && !have)      { s_frets_active |= bit; }
233	            else if (!need && have) { s_frets_active &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
234	        }
235	        note_q_pop();
236	    }
237	}

239	static void process_strums(void)

241	    while (!strum_q_empty())
242	    {

244	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s->strum_at_ms) < 0) { break; }

246	        s_strum_active        = true;
247	        s_strum_direction     = !s_strum_direction;
248	        s_strum_release_at_ms = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;

250	        strum_q_pop();

252	}
253	
254	static void process_releases(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
255	{

257	    {

260	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_release_at_ms[i]) < 0) { continue; }
261	        if (live_pressed_mask & bit) { continue; }
262	        if (note_q_any_needs(bit) || strum_q_any_needs(bit)) { continue; }

264	        s_frets_active        &= (uint8_t)~bit;
265	        s_release_pending_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit;
266	    }
267	}

269	static void advance(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
270	{

272	    {
273	        chord_commit();
274	    }
275	
276	    if (s_strum_active && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_strum_release_at_ms) >= 0)
277	    {
278	        s_strum_active = false;
279	    }
280	
281	    process_notes();
282	    process_strums();
283	    process_releases(live_pressed_mask);

285	    uint8_t mask = s_frets_active;
286	    if (s_strum_active)
287	    {

289	    }
290	    publish_mask(mask);
291	}
292	
293	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
294	{
295	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
296	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
297	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
298	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
299	
300	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
301	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
302	
303	    if (presses)
304	    {
305	        if (!s_chord_open)
306	        {
307	            s_chord_open     = true;
308	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
309	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
310	        }
311	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
312	    }
313	
314	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
315	    {
316	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
317	        {
318	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
319	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
320	        }
321	    }
322	
323	    advance(pressed_mask);
324	}
325	
326	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
327	{
328	    (void)param;
329	
330	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
331	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
332	
333	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
334	
335	    for (;;)
336	    {
337	        detector_state_t state;
338	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
339	        {
340	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
341	            {
342	                continue;
343	            }
344	            process_frame(&state);
345	        }
346	        else
347	        {
348	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
349	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
350	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
351	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
352	        }
353	    }
354	}

50	         * and our enable flip. */

58	    else

61	         * pipeline's next advance() (≤ TP_TICK_MS = 5 ms) republishes
62	         * its own correct mask. */
63	        s_enabled = false;
64	        s_fret_mask = 0u;
65	        s_strum_mask = 0u;

67	        TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true);

59	{
60	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.0f, 0.7f } },
61	    [FRET_RED]    = { { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.7f, 0.0f } },
62	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { { 0.0f, 0.5f, 0.5f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
63	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { { 1.0f, 0.4f, 0.0f }, { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.4f } },
64	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
65	};
66	
67	/* Per-fret detector state. Private — not on the bus. press_count is the
68	 * rising-edge counter the strum scheduler will eventually consume. */
69	static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
70	static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
71	static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];
72	static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];
73	static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];
74	
75	static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
76	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
77	
78	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
79	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;
80	
81	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
82	
83	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
84	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
85	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
86	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
87	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
88	{
89	    int cx = (int)px;
90	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
91	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
92	    int cy = (int)py;
93	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
94	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
95	
96	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
97	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
98	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
99	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
100	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
101	
102	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
103	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
104	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
105	    {
106	        const uint8_t *row = frame
107	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
108	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
109	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
110	        {
111	            sum_b += row[0];
112	            sum_g += row[1];
113	            sum_r += row[2];
114	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
115	        }
116	    }
117	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
118	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
119	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
120	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
121	}
122	
123	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
124	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
125	{
126	    float m = bgr[0];
127	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
128	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
129	    return m;
130	}
131	
132	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
133	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
134	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
135	{
136	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
137	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
138	    float cmin = bgr[0];
139	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
140	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
141	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
142	
143	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
144	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
145	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
146	    return (target - reject) * sat;
147	}
148	
149	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
150	
151	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
152	{
153	    detector_state_t state;
154	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
155	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
156	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
157	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
158	
159	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
160	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
161	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
162	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
163	
164	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
165	    {
166	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
167	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
168	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
169	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
170	
171	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
172	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
173	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
174	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
175	
176	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
177	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
178	
179	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
180	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
181	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
182	
183	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
184	
185	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
186	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
187	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
188	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
189	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
190	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
191	
192	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
193	        float h = hd;
194	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
195	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
196	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
197	    }
198	
199	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
200	}
201	
202	/* ─── Calibration overlay ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
203	
204	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point on the just-sampled frame so
205	 * the user can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets. The
206	 * ring radius is outside the 5×5 sample patch — overdrawing here would
207	 * not affect *this* frame's reads (detect_frame already ran) but a future
208	 * re-sample on the same ring slot must still see clean source pixels. */
209	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
210	
211	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
212	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
213	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
214	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
215	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
216	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
217	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
218	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
219	};
220	
221	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
222	                                 int x, int y,
223	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
224	{
225	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
226	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
227	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
228	}
229	
230	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
231	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
232	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
233	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
234	{
235	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
236	    while (x >= y)
237	    {
238	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
239	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
240	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
241	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
242	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
243	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
244	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
245	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
246	        y++;
247	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
248	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
249	    }
250	}
251	
252	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
253	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
254	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
255	{
256	    int rr = radius * radius;
257	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
258	    {
259	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
260	        {
261	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
262	            {
263	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
264	            }
265	        }
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
270	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
271	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
272	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
273	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
274	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
275	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
276	
277	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh)
278	{
279	    int w = (int)fw, h = (int)fh;
280	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
281	    {
282	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
283	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
284	
285	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
286	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
287	        draw_ring(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
288	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
289	
290	        if (s_pressed[i])
291	        {
292	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.hx, s.hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
293	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
294	        }
295	        if (s_edge_active[i])
296	        {
297	            draw_filled_disk(frame, w, h, s.ex, s.ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
298	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
299	        }
300	    }
301	}

303	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
304	
305	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
306	{
307	    (void)param;
308	
309	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
310	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
311	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
312	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
313	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
314	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
315	    configASSERT(subscribed);
316	
317	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
318	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
319	
320	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
321	
322	    for (;;)
323	    {
324	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
325	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
326	
327	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
328	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
329	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
330	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
331	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
332	
333	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
334	        draw_overlay((uint8_t *)frame.buffer, frame.width, frame.height);
335	
336	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
337	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
338	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)
339	        // {
340	        //     LOG_INFO("CV: G %3d/%3d%c%c R %3d/%3d%c%c Y %3d/%3d%c%c B %3d/%3d%c%c O %3d/%3d%c%c\r\n",
341	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_GREEN],  (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_GREEN],

345	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_YELLOW], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_YELLOW],
346	        //              s_pressed[FRET_YELLOW]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_YELLOW] ? 'E' : '.',
347	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_BLUE],   (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_BLUE],
348	        //              s_pressed[FRET_BLUE]       ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_BLUE]   ? 'E' : '.',
349	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_ORANGE], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_ORANGE],
350	        //              s_pressed[FRET_ORANGE]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_ORANGE] ? 'E' : '.');
351	        // }
352	    }
353	}
354	
355	void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void)
356	{
357	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(cv_marvin_v1_task,

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 02:57:36Z)**_

Journal entry is in. Three things worth your eyes before we touch any code:

**1. Real bug — `DetectorDrain` is stealing half the bus records.** Both it (priority 1) and the `Timing` task (priority 2) `xQueueReceive` from `s_bus_queue`. M3 plan said to delete it when timing pipeline went live; that step was missed. One-line fix: drop the `xTaskCreateStatic(drain_task, …)` in `Detector_Initialize` and the supporting `drain_task` function.

**2. Priority inversion — `VideoTask` is at 1, its consumer `CvMarvinV1` is at 2.** Latent stall whenever any priority-2 task is briefly busy: video can't push capture state forward, detector blocks on empty frame queue. Bump VideoTask to priority 2.

**3. Priority budget is too narrow.** `configMAX_PRIORITIES = 5`. With 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, there's no headroom for further structure. Recommend bumping to 8 and re-tiering — costs ~60 B BSS per band. Layout I'd propose:

| Band | Tasks |
|---:|---|
| 4 | Timing, FretLink |
| 3 | VideoTask, CvMarvinV1 |
| 2 | PerfDrain, USB_HOST, USB_DEVICE, DRV_USB_UDPHS |
| 1 | XLCDC, MAXTOUCH, Legato, SYS_INPUT |
| 0 | idle |

**Analytics enable diff** for `FreeRTOSConfig.h`:

```c

```

Suggested order: (1) delete DetectorDrain, smoke-test; (2) bump VideoTask priority, retest; (3) enable analytics flags + counter macros, take baseline; (4) bump `configMAX_PRIORITIES` and re-tier with real data in hand. Want me to start at (1)?

Honest answer: yes, but with a tighter scope than the journal's first pass suggested.

The journal proposal would re-tier MCC tasks too (USB host/device up to priority 2, UI down to 1). That requires editing `tasks.c` and adding an 8th entry to the MCC re-apply patch list — and we don't actually have evidence the MCC USB tasks need to outrank the UI tasks. The "missed enumeration window" concern was theoretical.

Tighter scope I'd recommend instead — touch only our hand-written tasks, leave MCC alone:

| Band | Tasks | Was |
|---:|---|---|
| 4 | Timing, FretLink | (2) |
| 3 | VideoTask, CvMarvinV1 | (1, 2) |
| 2 | PerfDrain | (2) |
| 1 | 9 MCC pollers | (1) — unchanged |
| 0 | idle | unchanged |

Why this works:
- VideoTask at 3 with CvMarvinV1 at 3 fixes finding (2). They time-slice, but CvMarvinV1 is almost always blocked on the frame queue, so VideoTask effectively runs whenever ready.
- Real-time output (Timing/FretLink) above real-time input (Video/Cv) is correct — a late strum is worse than a late detector tick.
- PerfDrain below the pipeline so a busy diagnostic writer never starves real-time work.
- MCC tasks unchanged → no `tasks.c` patch, no addition to the re-apply list.

Tradeoff: MCC USB host/device stay at priority 1 with the UI tasks. If we later observe USB enumeration jitter or PerfDrain getting starved by Legato/MAXTOUCH, we promote them in a follow-up — at that point we have analytics data to justify it.

Two changes total: `configMAX_PRIORITIES = 5 → 8` in [FreeRTOSConfig.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/FreeRTOSConfig.h), and the four priority literals in our task creates. ~5 line diff.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:08:50Z)**_

Walked through the whole project + foreseeable additions. Here's what I think is right.

**Inputs to the layout:**

Tasks we have today + tasks the spec/journal already names as coming:

- **Strum-critical output chain** — Timing → FretLink → USB host CDC class → USB host driver. Lateness here = missed notes during gameplay. Future M10 game-state controller is a third FretboardLink producer in the same band (mode-arbitrated against Timing).
- **Vision real-time input chain** — Video → CvMarvinV1. Future M9 game-state recognizer is another video-frame consumer in the same band. Possibly future second CV detector.
- **Diagnostic/secondary I/O** — PerfDrain → USB device CDC class → USB device driver. Future M5 SD recorder (if mostly I/O-bound) sits here.
- **UI** — Legato + MAXTOUCH + SYS_INPUT + XLCDC. Visible jitter only; can't break correctness.

The strum chain needs to outrank the UI chain because Legato can hold CPU for tens of ms doing a full redraw — a strum mask waiting on USB host while Legato animates is a real failure mode on Hard/Expert. The vision chain needs to be between them: above the UI (so capture/detect doesn't drop frames during heavy UI work) but below strum output (a late detector tick recovers next frame; a late strum is a missed note).

USB driver tasks (`DRV_USB_HOST_TASKS`, `USB_HOST_TASKS`) sit *with* their consumer (FretLink). If they were below, a busy higher-priority task could starve the wire. If they were above, FretLink might be preempted mid-write-prep — but FretLink blocks on a semaphore anyway, so equal-priority round-robin is the correct shape. Same logic applies on the device side: PerfDrain co-tiered with `USB_DEVICE_TASKS` + `DRV_USB_UDPHS_TASKS`.

**Proposed layout (`configMAX_PRIORITIES = 6`):**

| Band | Tasks | Reason |
|---:|---|---|
| 5 | Timing, FretLink, USB_HOST_TASKS, DRV_USB_HOST_TASKS | Strum-critical output. Future: M10 game-state controller. |
| 4 | VideoTask, CvMarvinV1 | Vision real-time. Future: M9 recognizer, second CV detector. |
| 3 | PerfDrain, USB_DEVICE_TASKS, DRV_USB_UDPHS_TASKS | Diagnostic + perf-log wire. Future: M5 SD recorder if I/O-bound. |
| 2 | LEGATO_Tasks, DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks, SYS_INPUT_Tasks, XLCDC_Tasks | UI; jitter-only failure mode. |
| 1 | (reserved) | Background work, e.g. periodic watchdog kick, slow housekeeping. |
| 0 | idle | — |

**What this fixes:**
- Finding (2): VideoTask above MCC pollers — no more inversion. Co-located with CvMarvinV1 since CvMarvinV1 is almost always blocked on the frame queue, so they don't fight.
- Finding (3): one open band today, more if we go to 8 later. Cheap to revisit.
- Real concern (Legato starving USB): UI now can't preempt USB tasks.

**What this doesn't try to do:**
- No band for "panic" or watchdog (band 1 reserve covers it; or bump to 7 if that lands).
- M5 SD recording: parking it at band 3 *if* it's I/O-bound (write blocks on SDMMC ISR). If it ends up CPU-bound (e.g. compression or format conversion), it'd belong at band 1 instead so it can't starve UI. Punt to M5 with stats data in hand.

**Cost:**
- `configMAX_PRIORITIES` 5 → 6: ~60 B BSS for the extra ready-list.
- Edits in `tasks.c` (MCC re-apply patch #8 — five tasks bumped from 1 to 2/3/5 depending).
- Edits to four hand-written tasks' `xTaskCreateStatic` priority arg.

Sound good, or do you want to push different tasks into different bands?

_**User (2026-05-22 03:09:40Z)**_

is there downside to more available priority levels? why limit to only 6?

---

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:09:59Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:10:09Z)**_

Fair pushback — I was being conservatively restrained without much justification.

**Real costs of larger `configMAX_PRIORITIES`:**

- One `List_t` per band in the ready-list array (~20 B on this port). Linear cost.
- The port-optimised task selection (`configUSE_PORT_OPTIMISED_TASK_SELECTION = 1`) uses a CLZ-based bitmap that fits in one word for priorities ≤ 32. Constant-time scheduling regardless of band count, *up to 32*. Beyond 32 you fall back to a generic linear scan — measurable hit. So 32 is the natural hardware-imposed ceiling on this port.
- Below 32: cost is essentially `(N - current) × 20 B` of BSS. On 256 MB DDR, irrelevant.

**Cognitive cost:** more bands invite "well let me put this at 11 because it's slightly more important than 10," which is how priority hygiene rots over time. The discipline isn't enforced by the kernel; it's enforced by having a reason for each band you actually use.

**My recommendation: bump to 8.** Same byte cost class as 6 (~40 B more BSS than 6 vs. the original 5 — meaningless), comfortable headroom, and 3-bit numbering is easy to reason about. Layout becomes:

| Band | Use |
|---:|---|
| 7 | (reserved — emergency stop, hard watchdog) |
| 6 | (reserved — soft watchdog, fault recovery) |
| 5 | Strum-critical output (Timing, FretLink, USB host driver+class) |
| 4 | Vision real-time (Video, CvMarvinV1) |
| 3 | Diagnostic + perf-log wire (PerfDrain, USB device driver+class) |
| 2 | UI (Legato, MAXTOUCH, SYS_INPUT, XLCDC) |
| 1 | (reserved — background housekeeping) |
| 0 | idle |

Three reserve bands (1, 6, 7) costs us nothing and lets future "this needs to outrank strum" or "this is just lazy background work" land cleanly without revisiting the whole layout.

Going higher than 8 doesn't have a technical downside until you cross 32 — but at some point you're just creating empty bands for the sake of it. 8 covers everything I can see coming. If you'd rather go straight to 16 for even more headroom, the BSS cost is still <200 B; entirely your call.

Want 8 or 16?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:20:58Z)**_

No functional reason. `tskIDLE_PRIORITY` is just `((UBaseType_t) 0U)` per the FreeRTOS header you have open (`task.h`), so `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 3u` and `3u` produce identical machine code.

It's a stylistic FreeRTOS idiom — "N levels above idle" reads as more intentional than a bare literal. But every other marvin task file uses the bare-integer form (`VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY 4u`, `CV_TASK_PRIORITY 4u`, `TP_TASK_PRIORITY 5u`, `FBL_TASK_PRIORITY 5u`). perf_log is the odd one out because I cargo-culted the FreeRTOS demo style when I wrote the module.

Want me to normalize it to `3u` to match the rest? One-line change.

179	**Finding 1 (bug, fix before next test): `DetectorDrain` is double-consuming the bus.** Both `DetectorDrain` (priority 1, [detector.c:30-57](../default/src/detector/detector.c#L30-L57)) and `Timing` (priority 2, [timing_pipeline.c:330,338](../default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L330)) call `xQueueReceive` on `s_bus_queue`. FreeRTOS queues are single-consumer-per-record by design, so each task sees roughly half the records — the half DetectorDrain gets is silently dropped. Plays nicely with what we observe (gameplay still works, but timing decisions are derived from every other detector publish at best). The 2026-05-20 plan-of-record explicitly said `DetectorDrain` would be deleted when M3 wired the real consumer; that step was missed. Fix is one-line: delete the `xTaskCreateStatic(drain_task, …)` call in `Detector_Initialize` and the supporting `drain_task` function. Throughput logging it provided is moot now that the perf-log path exists.
180	
181	**Finding 2 (priority inversion): `VideoTask` runs below its consumers.** `VideoTask` is the source of frames `CvMarvinV1` blocks on, but it's at priority 1 while `CvMarvinV1`/`Timing`/`FretLink`/`PerfDrain` all sit at 2. A late-frame condition (TC358743 lock churn, ISC retry) needs `VideoTask` to push the capture-pipeline state machine forward, but any priority-2 work currently runnable will preempt it. The detector then blocks on an empty frame queue while the video task can't run. Empirically not biting because `CvMarvinV1` only runs on frame arrival (event-driven, blocks immediately after consuming), but it's a latent class of stall whenever a priority-2 task ends up briefly busy. `VideoTask` belongs at priority 2 (or above) — the producer of the real-time pipeline shouldn't be in the same priority band as MCC's polling tasks.
182	
183	**Finding 3 (structural): the priority budget is too narrow.** `configMAX_PRIORITIES = 5` (priorities 0..4). Idle is 0. With time-slicing on (`configUSE_TIME_SLICING = 1`, `configIDLE_SHOULD_YIELD = 1`) and round-robin between equal-priority Ready tasks, current bunching is:
184	
185	- Priority 4: (unused)
186	- Priority 3: (unused)
187	- Priority 2: CvMarvinV1, Timing, FretLink, PerfDrain (4 tasks — real-time path, all event-driven, mostly mutually exclusive)
188	- Priority 1: 9 MCC polling tasks + VideoTask + DetectorDrain (11 tasks)
189	- Priority 0: idle
190	
191	With 11 tasks ready at priority 1 and the tick rate at 1 kHz, each priority-1 task gets ≈ 1 ms of every ≈ 11 ms — tolerable but means each MCC stack does its 10 ms `vTaskDelay` poll on roughly the cadence it asks for plus or minus a tick of jitter. The bigger problem is that we have *zero* headroom for further structure: there's no place to put a faster-than-detector watchdog, a strict-priority audio path, or anything that should clearly outrank `Timing` without sharing. If we ever hit a priority-inversion class problem the kernel can't help via priority inheritance because there's nowhere to invert *to*. Preferred fix is to bump `configMAX_PRIORITIES` to 8 — costs 3 × `sizeof(List_t)` ≈ 60 bytes of BSS per extra band on this port, trivial — and reorganize as:
192	
193	- 4: real-time strum-critical (Timing, FretLink)
194	- 3: real-time vision (VideoTask, CvMarvinV1)
195	- 2: PerfDrain + MCC USB host/device + DRV_USB_UDPHS (anything where stalling means a missed enumeration window)
196	- 1: MCC display/touch/Legato/SYS_INPUT (UI tasks; visible jitter only, not failure)
197	- 0: idle
198	
199	The MCC tasks are dynamic-created but their priority arg comes from a single MCC config knob per task; we can override via the existing `user.cmake` patch list rather than editing `tasks.c` directly. Worth doing alongside enabling analytics — once HWM + run-time-stats are live we'll have the data to confirm the split is correct.

225	### 2026-05-21 — Perf-log producer-side module landed
226	
227	Built the perf-log subsystem end-to-end on the producer side, including the real USB-device CDC ACM sink. Producers are not yet wired (module is dark beyond a SESSION + 1 Hz DROP heartbeat), but the wire path is live: a `PERF_REC_SESSION` is re-emitted on every host DTR-rising edge, so reconnecting a terminal mid-session always sees the schema record.
228	
229	**What landed under [`firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/`](../default/src/perf_log/):**
230	- `perf_log_records.h` — wire format, schema version 1. 16 B common header (`magic` 0x4D56 'MV', `type`, `flags`, `frame_epoch`, `ts_counter`). Record types: SESSION, STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, PATCH, DROP, TASK_HIGHWATER. Stage IDs cover ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE.
231	- `perf_log.{h,c}` — façade with separate task / `*FromISR` entry points (mirrors `xQueueSend` / `xQueueSendFromISR`). Two queues sized for the 30× small/large record-size ratio: state queue (slot = 40 B largest small record, depth 128) and patch queue (slot = `sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t)` = 814 B, depth 8). Drop-on-full, never block. Per-queue + sink drop counters RMW under `taskENTER_CRITICAL` / `taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR` (the XC32 ARM926 port doesn't link libatomic; GCC's `__atomic_add_fetch` falls through to a libcall and won't link). Drain task at `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` (above idle, below detector/timing) with 2 KB stack; emits one `PERF_REC_DROP` per second.
232	- `perf_log_sink.h` + `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — sink interface and USB-device CDC ACM implementation. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over `LEN || PAYLOAD`; framing is `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 || u16 LEN || PAYLOAD || u16 CRC`. MCC now ships USB-device + USB-device-CDC class config (UDPHS); the sink owns the application side: opens `USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0`, registers the device-layer event handler (Attach on POWER_DETECTED, register CDC handler on CONFIGURED), and exposes a blocking `WriteFramed`. CDC class events handle GET/SET line coding, control-line state (DTR latched into `s_cls`), and signal `WRITE_COMPLETE` via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` on a binary semaphore. Single producer (the drain task); writes are serialized one at a time on a single cache-aligned 832 B staging buffer (header + max patch payload + CRC). DTR-gated: if the host hasn't asserted DTR, frames are dropped into `s_drop_sink`. Write timeout (100 ms) drops + accumulates and the next state-machine pass observes DECONFIGURED if the host went away.
233	+ Cold-boot-with-cable required an explicit `Detach → 100 ms → Attach` edge after handler registration; relying on the driver's natural VBUS-edge `POWER_DETECTED` event to fire after-the-fact didn't enumerate (suspected: host gave up retrying after observing transient pull-up state during early boot, or the UDPHS driver's `vbusLevel` tracking races with handler-registration timing). The forced edge gives the host an unambiguous device-arrival regardless.
234	- μs timestamps via `SYS_TIME_CounterGet()` (TC0 CH0 raw counter) — host divides by `timer_freq_hz` from the SESSION record. Explicitly *not* the `xTaskGetTickCount() * (1000000 / configTICK_RATE_HZ)` pattern at [cv_marvin_v1.c:156](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L156); that's ms-resolution masquerading as μs and is useless for sub-frame attribution.

28:| 2026-05-21 | `configMAX_PRIORITIES` bumped 5 → 8; tasks re-tiered into 4 active bands (UI=2, diagnostic+perf-wire=3, vision=4, strum-critical+host-wire=5) plus 3 reserve bands (1, 6, 7) and idle (0). MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |
31:| 2026-05-21 | Manual-control input model is single-finger momentary; multi-finger chord input is out of scope for this surface | Legato's input pipeline (`legato_input.c:340/429`) routes each touch to a single focus widget, so a second simultaneous touch cancels the first button's release and strands its `pressed` state. Workarounds (custom maxtouch dispatcher; toggle-style frets) are real but not worth the complexity here — primary use case is game-menu navigation, which is single-finger by nature. Revisit only if a user-facing flow needs held chords. |

EDBG declares the comm interface with `bInterfaceProtocol=0x00` rather than the AT-command protocol Microchip hardcodes. The TPL/IAD match accepts the device (host stack does call `interfaceAssign`), but the per-interface check inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign` then rejects the comm interface, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to STATE_ERROR, and our attach handler never fires. Empirical retest with the CDC diagnostic logging in place: MCC's original order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well. The host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time, not at `USB_HOST_Initialize`. Reverted the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Two paths considered: invalidate D-cache per frame in the ISR, or move the pool to the linker's already-defined uncached region. Nocache is simpler and bug-resistant — every reader sees DMA-fresh bytes without explicit maintenance. 241:The MCC priorities are set in the per-component yml files (`gfx_legato.yml`, `usb_host.yml`, `drv_usbhs_v1.yml`, `drv_usb_udphs.yml`, `usb_device.yml`, `gfx_maxtouch_controller.yml`, `le_gfx_driver_xlcdc.yml`, `sys_input.yml`) plus `FreeRTOS.yml` for `FREERTOS_MAX_PRIORITIES = 8`, so MCC regen will produce the same `tasks.c` priority arguments — **no MCC re-apply patch needed for this layout**.
254:- `perf_log_records.h` — wire format, schema version 1. 16 B common header (`magic` 0x4D56 'MV', `type`, `flags`, `frame_epoch`, `ts_counter`). Record types: SESSION, STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, PATCH, DROP, TASK_HIGHWATER. Stage IDs cover ISC_IRQ, VIDEO_PUBLISH, CV_START, CV_END, TP_TICK, FBL_SEND, CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE.
255:- `perf_log.{h,c}` — façade with separate task / `*FromISR` entry points (mirrors `xQueueSend` / `xQueueSendFromISR`). Two queues sized for the 30× small/large record-size ratio: state queue (slot = 40 B largest small record, depth 128) and patch queue (slot = `sizeof(perf_rec_patch_t)` = 814 B, depth 8). Drop-on-full, never block. Per-queue + sink drop counters RMW under `taskENTER_CRITICAL` / `taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR` (the XC32 ARM926 port doesn't link libatomic; GCC's `__atomic_add_fetch` falls through to a libcall and won't link). Drain task at `tskIDLE_PRIORITY + 2` (above idle, below detector/timing) with 2 KB stack; emits one `PERF_REC_DROP` per second.
256:- `perf_log_sink.h` + `perf_log_sink_cdc.c` — sink interface and USB-device CDC ACM implementation. CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over `LEN || PAYLOAD`; framing is `0x55 0x4D 0x52 0x56 || u16 LEN || PAYLOAD || u16 CRC`. MCC now ships USB-device + USB-device-CDC class config (UDPHS); the sink owns the application side: opens `USB_DEVICE_INDEX_0`, registers the device-layer event handler (Attach on POWER_DETECTED, register CDC handler on CONFIGURED), and exposes a blocking `WriteFramed`. CDC class events handle GET/SET line coding, control-line state (DTR latched into `s_cls`), and signal `WRITE_COMPLETE` via `xSemaphoreGiveFromISR` on a binary semaphore. Single producer (the drain task); writes are serialized one at a time on a single cache-aligned 832 B staging buffer (header + max patch payload + CRC). DTR-gated: if the host hasn't asserted DTR, frames are dropped into `s_drop_sink`. Write timeout (100 ms) drops + accumulates and the next state-machine pass observes DECONFIGURED if the host went away.
262:**Producers not yet wired** — module is dark today. Next steps land them in this order: (1) ISR producers (`video.c` ISC_IRQ + VIDEO_PUBLISH; `fretboard_link.c` CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE — *no* `LOG_INFO` from this ISR per the 2026-05-20/21 freeze pattern); (2) task producers in `cv_marvin_v1`, `timing_pipeline`, `fretboard_link.FretboardLink_Send`. Replaces the commented-out 2 Hz dump at [`cv_marvin_v1.c:336-351`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L336-L351). `PERF_REC_PATCH` emission slots in last (Tier 2 — reuses already-sampled 5×5 patches, no new I/O).
286:| 5 ROI patches 32×32 RGB888 @ 60 Hz | 922 KB/s |
296:| ROI patches 60 Hz | 55 MB | 277 MB | 553 MB |
316:- **ROI patches 60 Hz (~1 MB/s)** preserves everything cv_marvin_v1 actually samples; streams comfortably over USB CDC, fits an entire song on SD with room to spare.
320:**Implication for what to build next.** The scoping confirms the spec's existing reference-data architecture is the right place to start; perf-logging is a *consumer* of the same infrastructure, not a separate path. Next step is to figure out which questions the perf log actually has to answer (latency attribution? frame-rate stability? detector confidence over time? actuator jitter?) and pick the minimum stream that answers them. State-only might already be enough for the latency/jitter questions; ROI patches are the cheapest way to get "did the detector see what I think it saw" replayability.
364:Plan agent flagged two real blockers worth recording: (1) Legato's input pipeline routes each touch to one focus widget — multi-finger momentary chords aren't possible without a custom dispatcher, so the model is single-finger only; (2) the lazy widget-pointer init means any code that walks the `Screen0_*` pointers has to run post-`screenShow_Screen0` — moot here because Composer does the wiring itself, but still true for any future shim that needs to read or modify widget state.
371:2. **Control-pipe completion handlers run from ISR context.** First instrumented attempt logged `LOG_INFO` directly from the new `SET_LINE_CODING_COMPLETE` / `SET_CONTROL_LINE_STATE_COMPLETE` event cases; system froze mid-print. Microchip's CDC stack dispatches *all* class events from ISR (the existing `WRITE_COMPLETE` case already uses `*FromISR` primitives — that was the precedent). `log_vprintf` takes a mutex with `portMAX_DELAY`, illegal from ISR. Stripped both the diagnostic logging and the latch infrastructure once the link was confirmed functional. Captured for the journal because it's a recurring shape: any new event-handler case in this stack must stay strictly ISR-safe.
383:Fix: relaxed both checks to `(AT_V250 || NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. After the patch the FBL log shows `CDC device attached, handle opened` and `c=Y` heartbeat as expected. Logged as patch #7 in the MCC re-apply list.
385:Also tested a hypothesis from the prior session that `USB_HOST_Initialize` had to run *after* the EHCI/OHCI driver inits. With the diagnostic logging in place, MCC's emitted order (`USB_HOST_Initialize` → `Legato_Initialize` → driver inits) enumerates and binds the CDC IAD just as well — the host layer evidently looks up HCD interfaces lazily at `USB_HOST_BusEnable` time. Backed out the hand-edit; one fewer re-apply patch to maintain. Decision-log entry above.
387:Diagnostic instrumentation stripped at the end of the session: the per-interface descriptor dump and enumeration state-change logger in `usb_host.c`, and the periodic OHCI/EHCI register heartbeat in `fretboard_link.c`. What remains on disk: the two `usb_host_cdc.c` protocol-relaxation lines (patch #7), the app-level VBUS asserts, and a minimal `USB_HOST_EVENT` printf so future host-stack drama still surfaces in the log.
397:Fix: reverted SYS_Initialize order so MMU/AIC/WDT-disable run before TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC. Display + capture came back on first boot. Logged as patch #6 in the MCC re-apply list above.
407:2. **cv_marvin_v1 reference port.** Ported `tools/fret-tuner/detect_video.py` to C — 5×5 patch BGR sampling, brightness-based hold detect with hysteresis (`HOLD_THRESH=50`, release at 60%), color-filtered edge detect with rising-edge `press_count`, per-fret BGR target/reject filter table. Coords scaled from Python's 1920×1080 anchor to 720×480 (Wii 480p60) at port time — same Elgato direct-pixel topology, just different resolution. Bus record stays canonical (option A): only `pressed / confidence / raw_value` cross the bus; `press_count` and raw color distances stay private to the module. Recording-format choice (custom packed binary vs nanopb vs CBOR) deferred to M5. ISC framebuffer pool moved from `.region_cache_aligned` to `.region_nocache` so CPU readers see DMA writes coherently; cap dropped 1080p→720p to fit the 16 MB nocache region.
409:3. **USB CDC host MCC regen.** Decided on USB CDC (marvin host, fretboard device) for the actuator/detector link instead of FLEXCOM UART — single cable, auto-enumeration, host-PC-debuggable. MCC regenerated with EHCI+OHCI host drivers and CDC host class. VBUS power-enable pins on PC27+PC31 (one per port). Hand-edit needed in `initialization.c` `DRV_USB_VBUSPowerEnable` because MCC assumes a single VBUS pin named `VBUS_AH` and emits one Set/Clear call; with two pins we need both per-pin macros explicitly. 85	**Carried into future sessions:**
86	
87	- **FreeRTOS analytics not yet enabled.** No runtime stats, task list dumps, or stack high-water-mark queries available. Bring up `vTaskList` / `vTaskGetRunTimeStats` / `uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark` plumbing (and an on-demand way to dump them — UART command? UI button? log on idle hook?) so we can size stacks empirically, attribute CPU, and catch latency regressions. Already bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. Pull `vApplicationStackOverflowHook` into the same scope: MCC's default is a silent spin, so an actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze — patching the hook to emit task name + spin (carefully, since the stack is already corrupt) belongs with the rest of the analytics work.
88	
89	- **Legato `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` adequacy.** Legato has its own internal pool (`LE_MALLOC` per touch event in `leInput_InjectTouchDown`). With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.
90	
91	- **Single-screen attach assumption for `ui/manual_input`.** `screenHide_Screen0` deletes the root widget tree, taking the Composer-generated `Screen0_*` widget pointers with it. We bind callbacks once after the first `screenShow_Screen0`. If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.
92	
93	- **Spec ↔ implementation drift on capture format.** Spec still uses "BGRX32" in ~10 places (§2 status table, §2.1 diagram, §3.1 hardware list, §4.1 video task, §4.2 detector input, §4.6.5 keyframe filename + size math, §4.7 sample config). The actual capture has been BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel) since the 2026-05-02 switch (`isc_capture.c:65-74`). Fixed §4.2.2 inline 2026-05-20 because M1 reads against it; the rest needs a sweep — including recalc of keyframe size (720×480 × 3 = 1.04 MB, not 1.38 MB) and on-disk recording layout. Defer to a doc-only pass before M5.
