```text
#ifndef MARVIN_LOG_H
#define MARVIN_LOG_H

#include <stdarg.h>

/* Lightweight logging shim. Goes through libc printf → xc32_monitor →
 * DBGU. Adds a runtime severity filter and FreeRTOS-aware locking.
 *
 * Pre-scheduler calls work too — the mutex is taken only when the
 * scheduler is running, so log_printf is safe to call from
 * APP_Initialize / SYS_Initialize.
 *
 * Do NOT call from an ISR — use a different mechanism for ISR-side
 * diagnostics (queue to a task, or atomic counter polled by a task).
 */

typedef enum
{
    LOG_LEVEL_ERROR = 0,
    LOG_LEVEL_WARN  = 1,
    LOG_LEVEL_INFO  = 2,
    LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG = 3,
} log_level_t;

/* Set up the FreeRTOS mutex. Safe to call before vTaskStartScheduler.
 * Pass the initial filter level. */
void log_init(log_level_t initial_level);

void        log_set_level(log_level_t lvl);
log_level_t log_get_level(void);

void log_vprintf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
void log_printf(log_level_t lvl, const char *fmt, ...)
    __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));

/* Convenience macros — match a typical embedded log API. */
#define LOG_ERROR(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_ERROR, __VA_ARGS__)
#define LOG_WARN(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_WARN,  __VA_ARGS__)
#define LOG_INFO(...)  log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_INFO,  __VA_ARGS__)
#define LOG_DEBUG(...) log_printf(LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG, __VA_ARGS__)

#endif
```

```text
36	
37	    /* Take the mutex only when the scheduler is running and the mutex
38	     * was created. Pre-scheduler we're single-threaded so interleaving
39	     * isn't possible; xSemaphoreTake with portMAX_DELAY would hang
40	     * before vTaskStartScheduler. */
41	    bool locked = false;
42	    if (s_mutex != NULL
43	        && xTaskGetSchedulerState() == taskSCHEDULER_RUNNING)
44	    {

46	        {

48	        }
49	    }
50	
51	    (void)vprintf(fmt, ap);
52	
53	    if (locked)
54	    {
55	        (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_mutex);
56	    }
57	}
```

```c
#include "diag.h"

#include <stdint.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"

#define DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS    1024u
#define DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY       1u

#define DIAG_PERIOD_MS           10000u
#define DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS      2000u
#define DIAG_BUF_BYTES           1024u

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
static char         s_buf[DIAG_BUF_BYTES];

static void emit_static_header(void)
{
    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: build ===\r\n"
             "  CPU=%u Hz  tick=%u Hz  max_pri=%u\r\n"
             "  rt_counter=SYS_TIME (%u Hz)  total_heap=%u  free_now=%u\r\n",
             (unsigned)configCPU_CLOCK_HZ,
             (unsigned)configTICK_RATE_HZ,
             (unsigned)configMAX_PRIORITIES,
             (unsigned)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet(),
             (unsigned)configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE,
             (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
}

static void diag_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    emit_static_header();

    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS));

    for (;;)
    {
        s_buf[0] = '\0';
        vTaskListTasks(s_buf, sizeof(s_buf));
        LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: tasks (Name State Pri StackHWM Num) ===\r\n%s",
                 s_buf);

        s_buf[0] = '\0';
        vTaskGetRunTimeStatistics(s_buf, sizeof(s_buf));
        LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: runtime (Name Counter Pct) ===\r\n%s",
                 s_buf);

        LOG_INFO("=== diag: heap free=%u min_ever_free=%u  ntasks=%u ===\r\n",
                 (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize(),
                 (unsigned)xPortGetMinimumEverFreeHeapSize(),
                 (unsigned)uxTaskGetNumberOfTasks());

        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_PERIOD_MS));
    }
}

void Diag_Initialize(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(diag_task,
                            "Diag",
                            DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL,
                            DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY,
                            s_task_stack,
                            &s_task_tcb);
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:47:54Z)**_

Diagnosis: `vTaskListTasks` and `vTaskGetRunTimeStatistics` internally call `pvPortMalloc` for a TaskStatus_t array. With **heap_1** linked, `vPortFree` is a no-op — every dump leaks ~1280 B. After 2 dumps the heap is exhausted, `pvPortMalloc` returns NULL, and the malloc-failed hook spins.

Fix: drop the convenience wrappers; use `uxTaskGetSystemState` against a static TaskStatus_t array and format each task line ourselves.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:48:06Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```c
#include "diag.h"

#include <stdint.h>

#include "FreeRTOS.h"
#include "task.h"

#include "definitions.h"
#include "log.h"

#define DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS    1024u
#define DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY       1u

#define DIAG_PERIOD_MS           10000u
#define DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS      2000u

/* Sized above the current 16-task footprint (9 MCC + 7 marvin) with
 * headroom for future tasks. uxTaskGetSystemState writes only as many
 * entries as it has tasks to fill. */
#define DIAG_MAX_TASKS           24u

static StackType_t  s_task_stack[DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
static TaskStatus_t s_status[DIAG_MAX_TASKS];

static char state_char(eTaskState s)
{
    switch (s)
    {
        case eRunning:   return 'X';
        case eReady:     return 'R';
        case eBlocked:   return 'B';
        case eSuspended: return 'S';
        case eDeleted:   return 'D';
        default:         return '?';
    }
}

static void emit_static_header(void)
{
    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: build ===\r\n"
             "  CPU=%u Hz  tick=%u Hz  max_pri=%u\r\n"
             "  rt_counter=SYS_TIME (%u Hz)  total_heap=%u  free_now=%u\r\n",
             (unsigned)configCPU_CLOCK_HZ,
             (unsigned)configTICK_RATE_HZ,
             (unsigned)configMAX_PRIORITIES,
             (unsigned)SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet(),
             (unsigned)configTOTAL_HEAP_SIZE,
             (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
}

static void emit_task_dump(void)
{
    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE total = 0;
    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(s_status, DIAG_MAX_TASKS, &total);

    LOG_INFO("\r\n=== diag: tasks (n=%u total_rt=%u) ===\r\n"
             "  %-16s St Pri  HWM      RT     Pct\r\n",
             (unsigned)n, (unsigned)total, "Name");

    /* total / 1000 gives a per-mille slice — pct printed as N.M%% without
     * floats. Guard against total==0 (no time elapsed yet). */
    configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE slice = total / 1000u;
    if (slice == 0u) { slice = 1u; }

    for (UBaseType_t i = 0u; i < n; i++)
    {
        unsigned pct10 = (unsigned)(s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter / slice);
        LOG_INFO("  %-16s %c  %2u %5u %10u  %3u.%01u%%\r\n",
                 s_status[i].pcTaskName,
                 state_char(s_status[i].eCurrentState),
                 (unsigned)s_status[i].uxCurrentPriority,
                 (unsigned)s_status[i].usStackHighWaterMark,
                 (unsigned)s_status[i].ulRunTimeCounter,
                 pct10 / 10u, pct10 % 10u);
    }
}

static void diag_task(void *param)
{
    (void)param;

    emit_static_header();

    vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_FIRST_DELAY_MS));

    for (;;)
    {
        emit_task_dump();
        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(DIAG_PERIOD_MS));
    }
}

void Diag_Initialize(void)
{
    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(diag_task,
                            "Diag",
                            DIAG_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
                            NULL,
                            DIAG_TASK_PRIORITY,
                            s_task_stack,
                            &s_task_tcb);
}

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:48:11Z)**_

No more `pvPortMalloc` per dump — `s_status` is static BSS (~960 B) and `uxTaskGetSystemState` just fills it. Output is one `LOG_INFO` per task line.

This also matches the project's static-allocation rule, which the convenience wrappers were silently violating.

Build & flash. Should sustain dumps indefinitely now.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:51:23Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-22 03:51:25Z)**_

Yeah — `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE` defaults to `uint32_t`, and SYS_TIME at 266 MHz fills 32 bits of accumulated CPU time in ~16 s. After that the totals wrap and percentages go nonsense.

Two fixes together:
1. Switch the counter to 64-bit (`SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` — already exists).

```bash
diag: periodic UART dump of FreeRTOS task list + run-time stats

Adds a tiny priority-1 task that emits task name, state, priority,
stack high-water, accumulated CPU (ms), and percentage every 10 s via
LOG_INFO. Uses a static TaskStatus_t[24] array against
uxTaskGetSystemState rather than the V11 vTaskListTasks /

dumps and the malloc-failed hook spins. Static array also keeps the
module aligned with the project's no-malloc rule.

(uint32_t) to SYS_TIME_Counter64Get (uint64_t) and sets
configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE to uint64_t. SYS_TIME runs at ~266 MHz
so a uint32_t accumulator wraps after ~16 s of cumulative CPU time
across all tasks; a multi-minute test confirmed totals went nonsense
without the widening.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -5
```
